This is the view of al-Nakha'i and Shurayh, and a narration of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hanifa and his companions went to it.

Al-Ash'ath related from al-Sha'bi, who said: Two litigants came to Shurayh, and one of them brought a witness whose hand and foot had been cut off for highway robbery, and then he had repented and amended his conduct. Shurayh permitted his testimony. The one against whom it was given said: "Do you permit his testimony against me while he has been amputated?" Shurayh said: "Every person subject to a prescribed penalty, when it has been enforced upon him and then he repents and amends his conduct, his testimony is permitted, except the slanderer, for that is a judgment from Allah that his testimony is never accepted; and his repentance is between him and Allah."

"And those who accuse their wives" — that is, who charge them with fornication.

"And they have no witnesses" — to confirm the truth of what they said.

"Except themselves; then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful." The people of Kufa read "arba'" with the nominative, as a subject and predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "that he should testify four testimonies."

"And the fifth" — meaning the fifth testimony. The common reading is with the nominative, as a subject, and its predicate is in "that." Hafs read it in the accusative, meaning "and he testifies the fifth testimony."

Nafi', Ya'qub and Ayyub read "anna" and "inna" lightened, with "la'natu" and "ghadabu" in the nominative; this is the narration of al-Mufaddal from Asim. The rest read the two nuns doubled, with what follows in the accusative.

"That he is of the liars." "And it averts from her the punishment" — that is, it wards off from the wife the prescribed penalty.

"That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he" — meaning the husband — "is surely of the liars."

And the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Nafi' recited ﴿أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهُ﴾ like "sami'a Allah" (as a verb), while the rest read it as a noun.

﴿And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Ever-Relenting, All-Wise﴾. The answer to "were it not" (law la) is omitted, meaning: He would have hastened punishment upon you and exposed you, but He concealed you and lifted the hadd from you through li'an, out of His wisdom and mercy.

As for the occasion of revelation of the verse:

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "By Allah, if I came upon a slut who had a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him until I brought four witnesses! By Allah, I would not bring four witnesses before he had finished his need and left. If I said what I saw, there would be eighty lashes on my back." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?" They said: "Do not blame him, for he is a jealous man. He has never married a woman except a virgin, and he never divorced a wife, so no man among us dared to marry her." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah I know that it is from Allah and that it is true, but I was surprised by it since you informed me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah refuses except that." He said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth."

He said: They had not stayed long before Hilal ibn Umayyah, a paternal cousin of his, came from his orchard and saw a man with his wife committing adultery. He held back until morning. In the morning he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was sitting with his companions, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with my wife. I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and it weighed heavily upon him, so that it was recognized in his face.

Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have brought you. By Allah knows that I am truthful and I said nothing but the truth, and I hope that Allah will make a way out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to strike him.

He said: The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said. Shall Hilal be flogged and his testimony nullified?" While they were so, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order his striking, revelation came down to him, and his companions held their speech when they recognized that revelation had descended, until it finished. Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ up to the end of the verses.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out for you." He said: "I had indeed hoped for that from Allah the Exalted."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her." She came, and when they were both together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she was told, and she denied it.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will either of you repent?"

Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, you have spoken the truth, and I said nothing but the truth."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make them swear li'an against each other." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." So he testified four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the truthful﴾. At the fifth it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter [[In the second copy there is an addition: and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people, and this fifth is the binding one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you.]]." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flog me for it." He testified the fifth: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾.

Then he said to the woman: "Testify." She testified [[In the second copy there is an addition: four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars﴾. He said to her at the fifth, and admonished her: "Fear Allah, for in the fifth is the binding one, and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people." So she hesitated for a while and was about to confess, then she said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people." Then she testified.]] the fifth: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and decided that the child belonged to her, and that the child should not be claimed for a father nor should her child be accused. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to her husband, and if she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to the one about whom it was said" [20] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 18/108. What is between brackets is from it and agrees with the second copy (Isfahan).]].

He said: So she bore a boy like a dark-brown calf, resembling the disliked one, and he was afterwards a governor in Egypt, and no one knew who his father was.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haythам narrated to us from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd from al-Hasan, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you see if a man sees a man with his wife and kills him, will they kill him? And if he reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes? Should he not strike him with the sword?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Enough with the sword, witness..." He intended to say "a witness," then stopped and said: "Were it not that jealous men and drunkards would follow up on this," and he mentioned the hadith.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said in the other narrations: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it on Friday from the pulpit. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari stood up and said: "May Allah make me your ransom. If a man of ours sees a man with his wife and reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes, and the Muslims call him a wicked person, and his testimony is never accepted. How can we find witnesses, when by the time we look for witnesses the man has finished his need and gone?" 'Asim had a paternal cousin called 'Uwaymir, whose wife was called Khawlah bint Qays ibn Muhsin. 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim and said: "I saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of my wife Khawlah." 'Asim said "Inna lillah," and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the following Friday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how quickly I was tested with the question you asked last Friday about my household!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what is that?" He said: "My paternal cousin 'Uwaymir informed me that he saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of his wife Khawlah." 'Uwaymir, Khawlah and Shurayk were all paternal relatives of 'Asim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them all and said to 'Uwaymir: "Fear Allah regarding your wife and your confidante and your paternal cousin, and do not slander her with calumny." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I swear by Allah that I saw Shurayk upon her belly, and I have not approached her for four months, and she is pregnant by another."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the woman: "Fear Allah and do not speak except of what you did." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Uwaymir is a jealous man, and he saw me and Shurayk prolonging our evening talk, so jealousy drove him to what he said."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Shurayk: "What do you say?" He said: "What the woman says." So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave orders until it was announced: "Congregational prayer!" He prayed the 'Asr prayer, then said to 'Uwaymir: "Stand." He stood and said: "I testify by Allah that Khawlah is an adulteress, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fourth he said: "I testify by Allah that I have not approached her for four months, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fifth he said: "The curse of Allah be upon 'Uwaymir" — meaning himself — "if he is of the liars concerning what he said."

Then he ordered him to sit and said to Khawlah: "Stand." She stood and said: "I testify by Allah that I am not an adulteress, and that 'Uwaymir is surely of the liars." Then in the second she said: "I testify by Allah that he did not see Shurayk upon my belly, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the third she said: "I testify by Allah that I am pregnant by him, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fourth she said: "I testify by Allah that he never saw me in an act of indecency, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fifth she said: "The wrath of Allah be upon Khawlah" — meaning herself — "if he is of the truthful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and said: "Were it not for these oaths, I would have had an opinion regarding their affair. Watch for her delivery: if she brings forth a reddish, thick-necked, long-stretching one inclining to blackness, he belongs to Shurayk ibn al-Sahma'; and if she brings forth a dark-brown, curly-haired, thin-legged one, he belongs to the one she was accused of with." [21]

Ibn 'Abbas said: She brought forth the one most resembling Shurayk among the creation of Allah. [[Sunan Ibn Majah with variations: 1/668, no. 2067.]]

Mention of the ruling of the verse:

If a man accuses his wife of adultery, the hadd becomes obligatory upon him, and he may free himself from it by producing evidence of her adultery or by li'an. If he produces evidence, it establishes her adultery and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. If he performs li'an, it establishes adultery against her, and she may free herself from it by li'an; if she does not perform li'an, the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. The husband may perform li'an whether or not he is able to produce evidence. Li'an is valid from every husband who is legally responsible, whether free or slave, Muslim or disbeliever; whoever's oath is valid, his accusation and li'an are valid.

The people of Iraq said: li'an is between any two free, adult persons, and li'an is not valid except before the judge or his deputy. When he conducts li'an between them, it is made stricter upon them in four respects: the number of formulas, the place, the time, and gathering the people.

As for the formula, it is four testimonies, and the fifth mentions the curse for the man and mentions the wrath for the woman, and the manner of this has already passed. As for the place, it is sought in the noblest places of the lands: if in Mecca, then at the Corner and the Maqam; if in Medina, then at the pulpit; if in Jerusalem, then in its mosque; and if in the rest of the cities, then in their mosques. If they are disbelievers, they are sent to the place they regard as sacred: if they are Jews, to the synagogue; if Christians, to the church; if Magians, to the fire-temple; and if they have no religion, like the idolaters, li'an is conducted between them in the session of his judgment. As for the time, it is after the 'Asr prayer. As for the number, it is required that there be four persons or more. The formula and gathering of people are conditions, while the place and time are recommended. When they perform li'an, four rulings attach to it: the falling of the hadd, the negation of the child, the termination of the marital bed, and the occurrence of permanent prohibition. All of this attaches to the husband's li'an. As for the wife's li'an, it only removes the hadd. If the man retracts his accusation, what is upon him returns (the hadd and lineage are restored to him), but what belongs to him does not return: the prohibition and the bed remain his, and they do not return. The separation by li'an is a annulment (fasakh), because it came from the wife's side.

Abu Hanifah and Sufyan said: li'an is a irrevocable single divorce, because it begins from the husband's side. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 1–10 (part 1 of 2):

Medinan. It has 5,680 letters, 1,316 words, and 64 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbazi related to us, saying: Ibn Hibban related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Farqadi related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Amr related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Atiyya related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, saying:
Zayd ibn Aslam related to us from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat an-Nur will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every believer, in the past and in the future." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/216.]] [19].

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us, saying: Salman ibn Tawba Abu Dawud al-Ansari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami related to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq related to us from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and her father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not house women in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, but teach them spinning and Surat an-Nur." [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 5/339.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"A surah which We have sent down" — the common reading is with the nominative (surah), meaning "this is a surah," because the Arabs do not begin with an indefinite noun; this is the view of al-Khalil. Al-Akhfash said: surah is a subject (mubtada') and its predicate is in "We have sent down." Talha ibn Musarrif [in the second copy: Mudarrif] read surah in the accusative, meaning "We have sent down a surah," and the pronoun is an extra connecting element. It was also said: "follow a surah which We have sent down." "And We have made it obligatory" — i.e., We have imposed the rulings contained in it. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "wa-farradnaha" with the doubled letter, meaning "We have explained and clarified it." It was also said: it is from "fard" (obligation), and the doubling indicates intensification, meaning We made them various obligations, and imposed them upon you and upon those after you until the Hour. The support for the lightened form is His saying: "Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an..." [[Al-Qasas: 85.]].

"And We have sent down in it clear signs, that you may remember." "The fornicatrix and the fornicator" — when both are free, adult, virgin and unmarried — "flog each one of them with a hundred lashes" — strike each of them. "And let not pity for them take hold of you" — compassion and tenderness.

Al-Akhfash said: "ra'fa" means tender compassion. It has three forms: "ra'fa" with the hamza silent (the hamza may also be lightened), which is the common reading; "ra'afa" with the hamza vowelled; and "ra'afa," with a hamza and a long vowel, like "al-kitaba," and these two are the reading of the people of Mecca, like "al-shana" and "al-sha'ana." It was also said: the short form is the noun and the long form is a verbal noun, like "sa'ul" and "sa'ala," and "qubh" and "qabaha." They did not differ concerning Surat al-Hadid that it is with the silent form, because the Arabs do not combine more than three fathas.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse. One group said: "And let not pity for them take hold of you" means that you should suspend the prescribed penalties and not enforce them.

Ma'mar related from Imran, who said: I said to Abu Mikhlad concerning this verse: "By Allah, we indeed have mercy on them, that a man be flogged or that his hand be cut off." He said: "That is only because it is not for the ruler, when they are brought to him, to leave them out of mercy towards them until he enforces the penalty upon them." This is the view of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Ibn Zayd and Sulayman ibn Yasar. What indicates it from the verse is that Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded flogging, and "jald" is the striking of the skin, like the head for striking the head; so He mentioned striking with the word "jald" lest it break the bone, nor cause lasting harm, nor reach the flesh.

Ibn Abi Mulayka related from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah that Abd Allah ibn Umar flogged a slave-girl of his, and said to the one who flogged: "Strike her back, her legs and her lower part, and make it light." I said: "Then where is the saying of Allah, 'and let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah'?" He said: "Shall I kill her? Allah commanded me to strike her and discipline her, and He did not command me to kill her."

Others said: rather, its meaning is "and let not pity take hold of you" so as to lighten the striking, but strike them painfully. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan.

Al-Zuhri said: one should exert oneself in the penalty for fornication and slander, and be lenient in the penalty for drinking.

Qatada said: one should be lenient in the penalty for drinking and slander, and exert oneself in the penalty for fornication.

Hammad said: the slanderer and the drinker are flogged while wearing their clothes, but the fornicator is stripped of his clothes; and he recited this verse.

"In the religion of Allah" — that is, in the judgment of Allah. Its parallel is His saying: "He could not take his brother under the law of the king."
[[Surat Yusuf: 76.]].

"If you believe in Allah and the Last Day, and let a group of the believers witness their punishment" — and let them attend their two punishments when they are carried out upon them. The scholars differed concerning the minimum number of the group. Al-Nakha'i and Mujahid said: the least of it is one man and above, and they argued with His saying: "And if two groups of the believers fight..." [[Surat al-Hujurat: 9.]] the verse. Ata' and Ikrimah: two men or more. Al-Zuhri: three or more. Ibn Zayd: four, according to the number whose testimony is accepted for fornication. Qatada: a company of the Muslims.

Hafs ibn Ghiyath related from Ash'ath from his father, who said: I came to Abu Barza al-Aslami on some business, and he had brought out a slave-girl of his to the door of the house, for she had committed fornication and borne a child from it. He threw a garment over her and ordered his son to strike her fifty strokes, not severely. He summoned a group and then recited: "and let a group of the believers witness their punishment."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Ali ibn Hanash [in the second copy: Habash, which agrees with the books of biographers] al-Muqri related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Nasra related to us, saying: Musaddad related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Ubayd related to us from Huraiz ibn Yazid al-Bajali from Abu Zur'a from Amr ibn Huraiz from Abu Hurayra, who said:
"The enforcing of a prescribed penalty in the land of Khayr is better for its people than forty nights of rain."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi related to us, saying: al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb informed me, saying:
Mu'awiya ibn Yahya informed me from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, from Hudhayfa, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, beware of fornication, for it has six characteristics, three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for those in the Hereafter: it brings about wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal abiding in the Fire." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 5/319.]].

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzayma informed us, reading it to him in the months of the year 383 AH, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Atiyya ibn Baqiyya related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abbad ibn Kathir related to me from Imran al-Qasir, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of my community are presented to me every Friday twice, and Allah's anger intensifies against the fornicators." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/167.]].

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in the second copy: Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh from Abu Ali ibn Habish al-Muqri from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Harun in Samarra, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dinawari said: Ibrahim ibn Zayd related to me.] al-Harrani said: al-Mughira ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Adi related to us from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: It is written in the Torah: "The fornicator does not die until he becomes poor, and the procurer does not die until he goes blind."

"The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix or a polytheist" — the verse.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse and its ruling.

One group said: The emigrants came to Medina, and among them were many poor people who had no wealth, no clans, and no families. In Medina there were prostitute women who hired out themselves, and they were at that time the most prosperous people of Medina. Some poor Muslims desired their earnings and said: "If we marry them and live with them until Allah makes us independent of them..." So they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission in that, and this verse was revealed, forbidding the marriage of the fornicatrix, to protect the believers from that. Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that the fornicatrix is only married by the fornicator or the polytheist, because they were fornicatresses and polytheists. Although the apparent form of the verse is a report, its implied meaning should be such-and-such, like His saying: "And whoever enters it is safe" [[Surat Al 'Imran: 97.]], and His saying, glorified and exalted: "Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing" [[Al-'Ankabut: 45.]], meaning it should be so. This is the view of Mujahid, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Qatada, al-Zuhri, al-Qasim ibn Abi Barza, al-Sha'bi, Abu Hamza al-Thumali, and a narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning well-known prostitute women in Mecca and Medina, who were numerous, and among them nine women who had banners, like the banners of the farrier by which they were recognized: Umm Mahzul, slave-girl of al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Makhzumi; Umm Anat, slave-girl of Safwan ibn Umayya; Hanna the Copt, slave-girl of al-As ibn Wa'il; Marriya, slave-girl of Malik ibn Umayla ibn al-Sabbaq; Halala, slave-girl of Suhayl ibn Amr; Umm Suwayd, slave-girl of Amr ibn Uthman al-Makhzumi; Sarifa, slave-girl of Zam'a ibn al-Aswad; Farsa, slave-girl of Hisham ibn Rabi'a ibn Habib ibn Hudhayfa; and Qarina, slave-girl of Hilal ibn Anas ibn Jabir ibn Namir. Their houses were called brothels in the Jahiliyya; no one entered upon them or came to them except a fornicator from the people of the qibla or a polytheist from the people of idols. A man would marry a fornicatrix in the Jahiliyya, taking her as his source of food. Some Muslims wished to marry them in that manner, and a man from the Muslims asked the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to marry Umm Mahzul, on condition that she spend on him; so Allah, glorified, revealed this verse, forbade the believers from that, and prohibited it for them.

Amr ibn Shu'ayb said: It was revealed concerning Murthid al-Ghanawi and Anaq. Murthid was a strong man, called Dildul, and he used to come to Mecca and carry the weak among the Muslims to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Anaq had been his lover in the Jahiliyya. When he came to Mecca, Anaq invited him to herself, and Murthid said: "Allah has forbidden fornication." She said: "Then marry me." He said: "Until I ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it." He asked him, and Allah, glorified, revealed this verse. The story has passed in Surat al-Baqara.

Others said: By marriage here is meant intercourse, and the meaning of the verse is: the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatrix or a polytheist, and the fornicatrix is not committed with except by a fornicator or a polytheist. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran informed me, saying: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muqri related to us, both saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Adani related to us from Sufyan from Habib ibn Abi Amra from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas: "The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix," he said: "This is not marriage, but intercourse; he does not commit fornication with her except a fornicator or a polytheist," so he used an euphemism.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Ali ibn Habish related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya related to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Rashid related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun said to us: "In my view, if he has intercourse with her while considering it lawful, he is a polytheist; and if he has intercourse with her while in a state of ihram, he is a fornicator."

Some of them said: This was the ruling of Allah for every fornicator male and female, until the following verse abrogated it: "And marry the single persons among you" [[Surat al-Nur: 32.]], and so the marriage of every Muslim woman and every Muslim man was made lawful. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who informed me, Ibn Fanjawayh, saying: Ibn Shayba related to us, saying: al-Faryabi related to us, saying: Qutayba related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us from Yahya ibn Sa'id from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: They claim that the verse "The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix or a polytheist" was abrogated by the following verse, "And marry the single persons among you," so the fornicatrix entered among the single women of the Muslims.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: the flogged man does not marry except a flogged woman.

"And those who accuse chaste women" — that is, who revile free, chaste Muslim women, and charge them with fornication; "then do not produce four witnesses" — upright witnesses who testify that they saw them doing that — "lash them" — meaning the accusers: strike each one of them "eighty lashes," "and do not accept their testimony ever, and they are the defiantly disobedient."

Then He made an exception, saying, exalted be He: "Except those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." The scholars differed concerning the ruling of this exception. One group said: It is an exception from His saying "and do not accept their testimony ever." They said: when the slanderer repents, his testimony is accepted and the name of defiant disobedience is removed from him, and his guardianship returns, whether he was punished or not. This is the view of al-Sha'bi, Masruq, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Abd Allah ibn Utba and al-Dahhak, and it is the view of the people of the Hijaz, and al-Shafi'i went to it.

They differed concerning the manner of his repentance. Some said: it is that he retracts his statement and disavows himself. Others said: it is regret for what has passed, seeking forgiveness for it, and not returning to it in what remains. When the penalty is enforced upon him, or the one slandered pardons him, the penalty falls. That is because slander is a right of the slandered person, like retaliation and injuries, and it falls away by pardon. If he pardons him and does not demand the penalty, or the slandered person dies before demanding the penalty, or it is not brought to the ruler so that he is not punished on account of this, or he is punished and then repents and amends his conduct, his testimony is accepted and his guardianship returns. What indicates this is what Ibn Ishaq related from al-Zuhri from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) struck those who testified against al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, namely Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Ma'bad and Nafi' ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah, and punished them, then said to them: "Whoever retracts his statement, his testimony will be accepted in what follows; whoever does not do so, I will not accept his testimony." Shibl and Nafi' retracted their statements and repented, but Abu Bakra refused to do so, and his testimony was never accepted.

Ibn Jurayj related from Imran ibn Musa, who said: I saw Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz permit the testimony of a slanderer together with one man.

Others said: This exception refers to His saying, "and they are the defiantly disobedient." As for His saying, "and do not accept their testimony," it is joined to "ever," and it is not permissible to accept it ever. This is the view of al-Nakha'i and Shurayh, and a narration of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hanifa and his companions went to it.

Al-Ash'ath related from al-Sha'bi, who said: Two litigants came to Shurayh, and one of them brought a witness whose hand and foot had been cut off for highway robbery, and then he had repented and amended his conduct. Shurayh permitted his testimony. The one against whom it was given said: "Do you permit his testimony against me while he has been amputated?" Shurayh said: "Every person subject to a prescribed penalty, when it has been enforced upon him and then he repents and amends his conduct, his testimony is permitted, except the slanderer, for that is a judgment from Allah that his testimony is never accepted; and his repentance is between him and Allah."

"And those who accuse their wives" — that is, who charge them with fornication.

"And they have no witnesses" — to confirm the truth of what they said.

"Except themselves; then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful." The people of Kufa read "arba'" with the nominative, as a subject and predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "that he should testify four testimonies."

"And the fifth" — meaning the fifth testimony. The common reading is with the nominative, as a subject, and its predicate is in "that." Hafs read it in the accusative, meaning "and he testifies the fifth testimony."

Nafi', Ya'qub and Ayyub read "anna" and "inna" lightened, with "la'natu" and "ghadabu" in the nominative; this is the narration of al-Mufaddal from Asim. The rest read the two nuns doubled, with what follows in the accusative.

"That he is of the liars." "And it averts from her the punishment" — that is, it wards off from the wife the prescribed penalty.

"That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he" — meaning the husband — "is surely of the liars."

And the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Nafi' recited ﴿أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهُ﴾ like "sami'a Allah" (as a verb), while the rest read it as a noun.

﴿And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Ever-Relenting, All-Wise﴾. The answer to "were it not" (law la) is omitted, meaning: He would have hastened punishment upon you and exposed you, but He concealed you and lifted the hadd from you through li'an, out of His wisdom and mercy.

As for the occasion of revelation of the verse:

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "By Allah, if I came upon a slut who had a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him until I brought four witnesses! By Allah, I would not bring four witnesses before he had finished his need and left. If I said what I saw, there would be eighty lashes on my back." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?" They said: "Do not blame him, for he is a jealous man. He has never married a woman except a virgin, and he never divorced a wife, so no man among us dared to marry her." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah I know that it is from Allah and that it is true, but I was surprised by it since you informed me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah refuses except that." He said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth."

He said: They had not stayed long before Hilal ibn Umayyah, a paternal cousin of his, came from his orchard and saw a man with his wife committing adultery. He held back until morning. In the morning he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was sitting with his companions, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with my wife. I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and it weighed heavily upon him, so that it was recognized in his face.

Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have brought you. By Allah knows that I am truthful and I said nothing but the truth, and I hope that Allah will make a way out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to strike him.

He said: The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said. Shall Hilal be flogged and his testimony nullified?" While they were so, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order his striking, revelation came down to him, and his companions held their speech when they recognized that revelation had descended, until it finished. Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ up to the end of the verses.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out for you." He said: "I had indeed hoped for that from Allah the Exalted."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her." She came, and when they were both together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she was told, and she denied it.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will either of you repent?"

Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, you have spoken the truth, and I said nothing but the truth."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make them swear li'an against each other." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." So he testified four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the truthful﴾. At the fifth it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter [[In the second copy there is an addition: and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people, and this fifth is the binding one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you.]]." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flog me for it." He testified the fifth: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾.

Then he said to the woman: "Testify." She testified [[In the second copy there is an addition: four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars﴾. He said to her at the fifth, and admonished her: "Fear Allah, for in the fifth is the binding one, and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people." So she hesitated for a while and was about to confess, then she said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people." Then she testified.]] the fifth: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and decided that the child belonged to her, and that the child should not be claimed for a father nor should her child be accused. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to her husband, and if she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to the one about whom it was said" [20] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 18/108. What is between brackets is from it and agrees with the second copy (Isfahan).]].

He said: So she bore a boy like a dark-brown calf, resembling the disliked one, and he was afterwards a governor in Egypt, and no one knew who his father was.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haythам narrated to us from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd from al-Hasan, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you see if a man sees a man with his wife and kills him, will they kill him? And if he reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes? Should he not strike him with the sword?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Enough with the sword, witness..." He intended to say "a witness," then stopped and said: "Were it not that jealous men and drunkards would follow up on this," and he mentioned the hadith.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said in the other narrations: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it on Friday from the pulpit. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari stood up and said: "May Allah make me your ransom. If a man of ours sees a man with his wife and reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes, and the Muslims call him a wicked person, and his testimony is never accepted. How can we find witnesses, when by the time we look for witnesses the man has finished his need and gone?" 'Asim had a paternal cousin called 'Uwaymir, whose wife was called Khawlah bint Qays ibn Muhsin. 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim and said: "I saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of my wife Khawlah." 'Asim said "Inna lillah," and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the following Friday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how quickly I was tested with the question you asked last Friday about my household!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what is that?" He said: "My paternal cousin 'Uwaymir informed me that he saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of his wife Khawlah." 'Uwaymir, Khawlah and Shurayk were all paternal relatives of 'Asim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them all and said to 'Uwaymir: "Fear Allah regarding your wife and your confidante and your paternal cousin, and do not slander her with calumny." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I swear by Allah that I saw Shurayk upon her belly, and I have not approached her for four months, and she is pregnant by another."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the woman: "Fear Allah and do not speak except of what you did." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Uwaymir is a jealous man, and he saw me and Shurayk prolonging our evening talk, so jealousy drove him to what he said."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Shurayk: "What do you say?" He said: "What the woman says." So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave orders until it was announced: "Congregational prayer!" He prayed the 'Asr prayer, then said to 'Uwaymir: "Stand." He stood and said: "I testify by Allah that Khawlah is an adulteress, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fourth he said: "I testify by Allah that I have not approached her for four months, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fifth he said: "The curse of Allah be upon 'Uwaymir" — meaning himself — "if he is of the liars concerning what he said."

Then he ordered him to sit and said to Khawlah: "Stand." She stood and said: "I testify by Allah that I am not an adulteress, and that 'Uwaymir is surely of the liars." Then in the second she said: "I testify by Allah that he did not see Shurayk upon my belly, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the third she said: "I testify by Allah that I am pregnant by him, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fourth she said: "I testify by Allah that he never saw me in an act of indecency, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fifth she said: "The wrath of Allah be upon Khawlah" — meaning herself — "if he is of the truthful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and said: "Were it not for these oaths, I would have had an opinion regarding their affair. Watch for her delivery: if she brings forth a reddish, thick-necked, long-stretching one inclining to blackness, he belongs to Shurayk ibn al-Sahma'; and if she brings forth a dark-brown, curly-haired, thin-legged one, he belongs to the one she was accused of with." [21]

Ibn 'Abbas said: She brought forth the one most resembling Shurayk among the creation of Allah. [[Sunan Ibn Majah with variations: 1/668, no. 2067.]]

Mention of the ruling of the verse:

If a man accuses his wife of adultery, the hadd becomes obligatory upon him, and he may free himself from it by producing evidence of her adultery or by li'an. If he produces evidence, it establishes her adultery and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. If he performs li'an, it establishes adultery against her, and she may free herself from it by li'an; if she does not perform li'an, the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. The husband may perform li'an whether or not he is able to produce evidence. Li'an is valid from every husband who is legally responsible, whether free or slave, Muslim or disbeliever; whoever's oath is valid, his accusation and li'an are valid.

The people of Iraq said: li'an is between any two free, adult persons, and li'an is not valid except before the judge or his deputy. When he conducts li'an between them, it is made stricter upon them in four respects: the number of formulas, the place, the time, and gathering the people.

As for the formula, it is four testimonies, and the fifth mentions the curse for the man and mentions the wrath for the woman, and the manner of this has already passed. As for the place, it is sought in the noblest places of the lands: if in Mecca, then at the Corner and the Maqam; if in Medina, then at the pulpit; if in Jerusalem, then in its mosque; and if in the rest of the cities, then in their mosques. If they are disbelievers, they are sent to the place they regard as sacred: if they are Jews, to the synagogue; if Christians, to the church; if Magians, to the fire-temple; and if they have no religion, like the idolaters, li'an is conducted between them in the session of his judgment. As for the time, it is after the 'Asr prayer. As for the number, it is required that there be four persons or more. The formula and gathering of people are conditions, while the place and time are recommended. When they perform li'an, four rulings attach to it: the falling of the hadd, the negation of the child, the termination of the marital bed, and the occurrence of permanent prohibition. All of this attaches to the husband's li'an. As for the wife's li'an, it only removes the hadd. If the man retracts his accusation, what is upon him returns (the hadd and lineage are restored to him), but what belongs to him does not return: the prohibition and the bed remain his, and they do not return. The separation by li'an is a annulment (fasakh), because it came from the wife's side.

Abu Hanifah and Sufyan said: li'an is a irrevocable single divorce, because it begins from the husband's side. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 1–10 (part 1 of 2):

Medinan. It has 5,680 letters, 1,316 words, and 64 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbazi related to us, saying: Ibn Hibban related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Farqadi related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Amr related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Atiyya related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, saying:
Zayd ibn Aslam related to us from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat an-Nur will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every believer, in the past and in the future." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/216.]] [19].

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us, saying: Salman ibn Tawba Abu Dawud al-Ansari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami related to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq related to us from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and her father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not house women in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, but teach them spinning and Surat an-Nur." [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 5/339.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"A surah which We have sent down" — the common reading is with the nominative (surah), meaning "this is a surah," because the Arabs do not begin with an indefinite noun; this is the view of al-Khalil. Al-Akhfash said: surah is a subject (mubtada') and its predicate is in "We have sent down." Talha ibn Musarrif [in the second copy: Mudarrif] read surah in the accusative, meaning "We have sent down a surah," and the pronoun is an extra connecting element. It was also said: "follow a surah which We have sent down." "And We have made it obligatory" — i.e., We have imposed the rulings contained in it. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "wa-farradnaha" with the doubled letter, meaning "We have explained and clarified it." It was also said: it is from "fard" (obligation), and the doubling indicates intensification, meaning We made them various obligations, and imposed them upon you and upon those after you until the Hour. The support for the lightened form is His saying: "Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an..." [[Al-Qasas: 85.]].

"And We have sent down in it clear signs, that you may remember." "The fornicatrix and the fornicator" — when both are free, adult, virgin and unmarried — "flog each one of them with a hundred lashes" — strike each of them. "And let not pity for them take hold of you" — compassion and tenderness.

Al-Akhfash said: "ra'fa" means tender compassion. It has three forms: "ra'fa" with the hamza silent (the hamza may also be lightened), which is the common reading; "ra'afa" with the hamza vowelled; and "ra'afa," with a hamza and a long vowel, like "al-kitaba," and these two are the reading of the people of Mecca, like "al-shana" and "al-sha'ana." It was also said: the short form is the noun and the long form is a verbal noun, like "sa'ul" and "sa'ala," and "qubh" and "qabaha." They did not differ concerning Surat al-Hadid that it is with the silent form, because the Arabs do not combine more than three fathas.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse. One group said: "And let not pity for them take hold of you" means that you should suspend the prescribed penalties and not enforce them.

Ma'mar related from Imran, who said: I said to Abu Mikhlad concerning this verse: "By Allah, we indeed have mercy on them, that a man be flogged or that his hand be cut off." He said: "That is only because it is not for the ruler, when they are brought to him, to leave them out of mercy towards them until he enforces the penalty upon them." This is the view of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Nakha'i, al-Sha'bi, Ibn Zayd and Sulayman ibn Yasar. What indicates it from the verse is that Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded flogging, and "jald" is the striking of the skin, like the head for striking the head; so He mentioned striking with the word "jald" lest it break the bone, nor cause lasting harm, nor reach the flesh.

Ibn Abi Mulayka related from Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah that Abd Allah ibn Umar flogged a slave-girl of his, and said to the one who flogged: "Strike her back, her legs and her lower part, and make it light." I said: "Then where is the saying of Allah, 'and let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah'?" He said: "Shall I kill her? Allah commanded me to strike her and discipline her, and He did not command me to kill her."

Others said: rather, its meaning is "and let not pity take hold of you" so as to lighten the striking, but strike them painfully. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and al-Hasan.

Al-Zuhri said: one should exert oneself in the penalty for fornication and slander, and be lenient in the penalty for drinking.

Qatada said: one should be lenient in the penalty for drinking and slander, and exert oneself in the penalty for fornication.

Hammad said: the slanderer and the drinker are flogged while wearing their clothes, but the fornicator is stripped of his clothes; and he recited this verse.

"In the religion of Allah" — that is, in the judgment of Allah. Its parallel is His saying: "He could not take his brother under the law of the king."
[[Surat Yusuf: 76.]].

"If you believe in Allah and the Last Day, and let a group of the believers witness their punishment" — and let them attend their two punishments when they are carried out upon them. The scholars differed concerning the minimum number of the group. Al-Nakha'i and Mujahid said: the least of it is one man and above, and they argued with His saying: "And if two groups of the believers fight..." [[Surat al-Hujurat: 9.]] the verse. Ata' and Ikrimah: two men or more. Al-Zuhri: three or more. Ibn Zayd: four, according to the number whose testimony is accepted for fornication. Qatada: a company of the Muslims.

Hafs ibn Ghiyath related from Ash'ath from his father, who said: I came to Abu Barza al-Aslami on some business, and he had brought out a slave-girl of his to the door of the house, for she had committed fornication and borne a child from it. He threw a garment over her and ordered his son to strike her fifty strokes, not severely. He summoned a group and then recited: "and let a group of the believers witness their punishment."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Ali ibn Hanash [in the second copy: Habash, which agrees with the books of biographers] al-Muqri related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Uthman related to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Nasra related to us, saying: Musaddad related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Ubayd related to us from Huraiz ibn Yazid al-Bajali from Abu Zur'a from Amr ibn Huraiz from Abu Hurayra, who said:
"The enforcing of a prescribed penalty in the land of Khayr is better for its people than forty nights of rain."

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Nu'aym Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn Adi related to us, saying: al-Abbas ibn al-Walid ibn Mazid al-Bayruti informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Shu'ayb informed me, saying:
Mu'awiya ibn Yahya informed me from Sulayman al-A'mash, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, from Hudhayfa, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O people, beware of fornication, for it has six characteristics, three in this world and three in the Hereafter. As for those in this world: it removes radiance, brings poverty, and shortens life. As for those in the Hereafter: it brings about wrath, evil reckoning, and eternal abiding in the Fire." [[Kanz al-Ummal: 5/319.]].

Abu Tahir ibn Khuzayma informed us, reading it to him in the months of the year 383 AH, saying: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Muslim related to us, saying: Atiyya ibn Baqiyya related to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Abbad ibn Kathir related to me from Imran al-Qasir, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of my community are presented to me every Friday twice, and Allah's anger intensifies against the fornicators." [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/167.]].

Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Yazid [in the second copy: Abu Abd Allah ibn Fanjawayh from Abu Ali ibn Habish al-Muqri from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Harun in Samarra, Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Dinawari said: Ibrahim ibn Zayd related to me.] al-Harrani said: al-Mughira ibn Saqlab related to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Adi related to us from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: It is written in the Torah: "The fornicator does not die until he becomes poor, and the procurer does not die until he goes blind."

"The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix or a polytheist" — the verse.

The scholars differed concerning the meaning of the verse and its ruling.

One group said: The emigrants came to Medina, and among them were many poor people who had no wealth, no clans, and no families. In Medina there were prostitute women who hired out themselves, and they were at that time the most prosperous people of Medina. Some poor Muslims desired their earnings and said: "If we marry them and live with them until Allah makes us independent of them..." So they asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for permission in that, and this verse was revealed, forbidding the marriage of the fornicatrix, to protect the believers from that. Allah, glorified and exalted, informed that the fornicatrix is only married by the fornicator or the polytheist, because they were fornicatresses and polytheists. Although the apparent form of the verse is a report, its implied meaning should be such-and-such, like His saying: "And whoever enters it is safe" [[Surat Al 'Imran: 97.]], and His saying, glorified and exalted: "Indeed, prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing" [[Al-'Ankabut: 45.]], meaning it should be so. This is the view of Mujahid, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Qatada, al-Zuhri, al-Qasim ibn Abi Barza, al-Sha'bi, Abu Hamza al-Thumali, and a narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas.

Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning well-known prostitute women in Mecca and Medina, who were numerous, and among them nine women who had banners, like the banners of the farrier by which they were recognized: Umm Mahzul, slave-girl of al-Sa'ib ibn Abi al-Sa'ib al-Makhzumi; Umm Anat, slave-girl of Safwan ibn Umayya; Hanna the Copt, slave-girl of al-As ibn Wa'il; Marriya, slave-girl of Malik ibn Umayla ibn al-Sabbaq; Halala, slave-girl of Suhayl ibn Amr; Umm Suwayd, slave-girl of Amr ibn Uthman al-Makhzumi; Sarifa, slave-girl of Zam'a ibn al-Aswad; Farsa, slave-girl of Hisham ibn Rabi'a ibn Habib ibn Hudhayfa; and Qarina, slave-girl of Hilal ibn Anas ibn Jabir ibn Namir. Their houses were called brothels in the Jahiliyya; no one entered upon them or came to them except a fornicator from the people of the qibla or a polytheist from the people of idols. A man would marry a fornicatrix in the Jahiliyya, taking her as his source of food. Some Muslims wished to marry them in that manner, and a man from the Muslims asked the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) for permission to marry Umm Mahzul, on condition that she spend on him; so Allah, glorified, revealed this verse, forbade the believers from that, and prohibited it for them.

Amr ibn Shu'ayb said: It was revealed concerning Murthid al-Ghanawi and Anaq. Murthid was a strong man, called Dildul, and he used to come to Mecca and carry the weak among the Muslims to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Anaq had been his lover in the Jahiliyya. When he came to Mecca, Anaq invited him to herself, and Murthid said: "Allah has forbidden fornication." She said: "Then marry me." He said: "Until I ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it." He asked him, and Allah, glorified, revealed this verse. The story has passed in Surat al-Baqara.

Others said: By marriage here is meant intercourse, and the meaning of the verse is: the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatrix or a polytheist, and the fornicatrix is not committed with except by a fornicator or a polytheist. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Abd Allah informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sunni related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Imran informed me, saying: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Muqri related to us, both saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Walid al-Adani related to us from Sufyan from Habib ibn Abi Amra from Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas: "The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix," he said: "This is not marriage, but intercourse; he does not commit fornication with her except a fornicator or a polytheist," so he used an euphemism.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed us, saying: Abu Ali ibn Habish related to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Zakariyya related to me, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Rashid related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun said to us: "In my view, if he has intercourse with her while considering it lawful, he is a polytheist; and if he has intercourse with her while in a state of ihram, he is a fornicator."

Some of them said: This was the ruling of Allah for every fornicator male and female, until the following verse abrogated it: "And marry the single persons among you" [[Surat al-Nur: 32.]], and so the marriage of every Muslim woman and every Muslim man was made lawful. This is the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who informed me, Ibn Fanjawayh, saying: Ibn Shayba related to us, saying: al-Faryabi related to us, saying: Qutayba related to us, saying: al-Layth related to us from Yahya ibn Sa'id from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said: They claim that the verse "The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatrix or a polytheist" was abrogated by the following verse, "And marry the single persons among you," so the fornicatrix entered among the single women of the Muslims.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is: the flogged man does not marry except a flogged woman.

"And those who accuse chaste women" — that is, who revile free, chaste Muslim women, and charge them with fornication; "then do not produce four witnesses" — upright witnesses who testify that they saw them doing that — "lash them" — meaning the accusers: strike each one of them "eighty lashes," "and do not accept their testimony ever, and they are the defiantly disobedient."

Then He made an exception, saying, exalted be He: "Except those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful." The scholars differed concerning the ruling of this exception. One group said: It is an exception from His saying "and do not accept their testimony ever." They said: when the slanderer repents, his testimony is accepted and the name of defiant disobedience is removed from him, and his guardianship returns, whether he was punished or not. This is the view of al-Sha'bi, Masruq, Sulayman ibn Yasar, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ata', Tawus, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Abd Allah ibn Utba and al-Dahhak, and it is the view of the people of the Hijaz, and al-Shafi'i went to it.

They differed concerning the manner of his repentance. Some said: it is that he retracts his statement and disavows himself. Others said: it is regret for what has passed, seeking forgiveness for it, and not returning to it in what remains. When the penalty is enforced upon him, or the one slandered pardons him, the penalty falls. That is because slander is a right of the slandered person, like retaliation and injuries, and it falls away by pardon. If he pardons him and does not demand the penalty, or the slandered person dies before demanding the penalty, or it is not brought to the ruler so that he is not punished on account of this, or he is punished and then repents and amends his conduct, his testimony is accepted and his guardianship returns. What indicates this is what Ibn Ishaq related from al-Zuhri from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) struck those who testified against al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba, namely Abu Bakra, Shibl ibn Ma'bad and Nafi' ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah, and punished them, then said to them: "Whoever retracts his statement, his testimony will be accepted in what follows; whoever does not do so, I will not accept his testimony." Shibl and Nafi' retracted their statements and repented, but Abu Bakra refused to do so, and his testimony was never accepted.

Ibn Jurayj related from Imran ibn Musa, who said: I saw Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz permit the testimony of a slanderer together with one man.

Others said: This exception refers to His saying, "and they are the defiantly disobedient." As for His saying, "and do not accept their testimony," it is joined to "ever," and it is not permissible to accept it ever. This is the view of al-Nakha'i and Shurayh, and a narration of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Hanifa and his companions went to it.

Al-Ash'ath related from al-Sha'bi, who said: Two litigants came to Shurayh, and one of them brought a witness whose hand and foot had been cut off for highway robbery, and then he had repented and amended his conduct. Shurayh permitted his testimony. The one against whom it was given said: "Do you permit his testimony against me while he has been amputated?" Shurayh said: "Every person subject to a prescribed penalty, when it has been enforced upon him and then he repents and amends his conduct, his testimony is permitted, except the slanderer, for that is a judgment from Allah that his testimony is never accepted; and his repentance is between him and Allah."

"And those who accuse their wives" — that is, who charge them with fornication.

"And they have no witnesses" — to confirm the truth of what they said.

"Except themselves; then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful." The people of Kufa read "arba'" with the nominative, as a subject and predicate. The rest read it in the accusative, meaning "that he should testify four testimonies."

"And the fifth" — meaning the fifth testimony. The common reading is with the nominative, as a subject, and its predicate is in "that." Hafs read it in the accusative, meaning "and he testifies the fifth testimony."

Nafi', Ya'qub and Ayyub read "anna" and "inna" lightened, with "la'natu" and "ghadabu" in the nominative; this is the narration of al-Mufaddal from Asim. The rest read the two nuns doubled, with what follows in the accusative.

"That he is of the liars." "And it averts from her the punishment" — that is, it wards off from the wife the prescribed penalty.

"That she testify four testimonies by Allah that he" — meaning the husband — "is surely of the liars."

And the fifth: that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Nafi' recited ﴿أَنَّ غَضَبَ اللَّهُ﴾ like "sami'a Allah" (as a verb), while the rest read it as a noun.

﴿And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Ever-Relenting, All-Wise﴾. The answer to "were it not" (law la) is omitted, meaning: He would have hastened punishment upon you and exposed you, but He concealed you and lifted the hadd from you through li'an, out of His wisdom and mercy.

As for the occasion of revelation of the verse:

Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses, lash them eighty lashes﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "By Allah, if I came upon a slut who had a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or move him until I brought four witnesses! By Allah, I would not bring four witnesses before he had finished his need and left. If I said what I saw, there would be eighty lashes on my back." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief says?" They said: "Do not blame him, for he is a jealous man. He has never married a woman except a virgin, and he never divorced a wife, so no man among us dared to marry her." Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, by Allah I know that it is from Allah and that it is true, but I was surprised by it since you informed me." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah refuses except that." He said: "Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth."

He said: They had not stayed long before Hilal ibn Umayyah, a paternal cousin of his, came from his orchard and saw a man with his wife committing adultery. He held back until morning. In the morning he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was sitting with his companions, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with my wife. I saw it with my eyes and heard it with my ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and it weighed heavily upon him, so that it was recognized in his face.

Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I see the aversion in your face at what I have brought you. By Allah knows that I am truthful and I said nothing but the truth, and I hope that Allah will make a way out." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to strike him.

He said: The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Sa'd said. Shall Hilal be flogged and his testimony nullified?" While they were so, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order his striking, revelation came down to him, and his companions held their speech when they recognized that revelation had descended, until it finished. Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾ up to the end of the verses.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made a way out for you." He said: "I had indeed hoped for that from Allah the Exalted."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her." She came, and when they were both together with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), she was told, and she denied it.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar. Will either of you repent?"

Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be your ransom, you have spoken the truth, and I said nothing but the truth."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Make them swear li'an against each other." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." So he testified four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the truthful﴾. At the fifth it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter [[In the second copy there is an addition: and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people, and this fifth is the binding one that makes the punishment obligatory upon you.]]." Hilal said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not flog me for it." He testified the fifth: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾.

Then he said to the woman: "Testify." She testified [[In the second copy there is an addition: four testimonies: ﴿I testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars﴾. He said to her at the fifth, and admonished her: "Fear Allah, for in the fifth is the binding one, and the punishment of Allah is more severe than the punishment of people." So she hesitated for a while and was about to confess, then she said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people." Then she testified.]] the fifth: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and decided that the child belonged to her, and that the child should not be claimed for a father nor should her child be accused. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "If she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to her husband, and if she brings him forth like such-and-such, he belongs to the one about whom it was said" [20] [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 18/108. What is between brackets is from it and agrees with the second copy (Isfahan).]].

He said: So she bore a boy like a dark-brown calf, resembling the disliked one, and he was afterwards a governor in Egypt, and no one knew who his father was.

And Muhammad ibn 'Abdus informed us: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz informed us: al-Qasim ibn Salam informed us: Haythам narrated to us from Yunus ibn 'Ubayd from al-Hasan, who said: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women, then do not produce four witnesses﴾ was revealed, Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do you see if a man sees a man with his wife and kills him, will they kill him? And if he reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes? Should he not strike him with the sword?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Enough with the sword, witness..." He intended to say "a witness," then stopped and said: "Were it not that jealous men and drunkards would follow up on this," and he mentioned the hadith.

Ibn 'Abbas and Muqatil said in the other narrations: When the verse ﴿And those who accuse chaste women﴾ was revealed, the Prophet (ﷺ) recited it on Friday from the pulpit. 'Asim ibn 'Adi al-Ansari stood up and said: "May Allah make me your ransom. If a man of ours sees a man with his wife and reports what he saw, he is flogged eighty lashes, and the Muslims call him a wicked person, and his testimony is never accepted. How can we find witnesses, when by the time we look for witnesses the man has finished his need and gone?" 'Asim had a paternal cousin called 'Uwaymir, whose wife was called Khawlah bint Qays ibn Muhsin. 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim and said: "I saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of my wife Khawlah." 'Asim said "Inna lillah," and came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on the following Friday and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how quickly I was tested with the question you asked last Friday about my household!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "And what is that?" He said: "My paternal cousin 'Uwaymir informed me that he saw Shurayk ibn al-Sahma' upon the belly of his wife Khawlah." 'Uwaymir, Khawlah and Shurayk were all paternal relatives of 'Asim. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned them all and said to 'Uwaymir: "Fear Allah regarding your wife and your confidante and your paternal cousin, and do not slander her with calumny." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, I swear by Allah that I saw Shurayk upon her belly, and I have not approached her for four months, and she is pregnant by another."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the woman: "Fear Allah and do not speak except of what you did." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, 'Uwaymir is a jealous man, and he saw me and Shurayk prolonging our evening talk, so jealousy drove him to what he said."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Shurayk: "What do you say?" He said: "What the woman says." So Allah the Exalted revealed ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ the verse. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave orders until it was announced: "Congregational prayer!" He prayed the 'Asr prayer, then said to 'Uwaymir: "Stand." He stood and said: "I testify by Allah that Khawlah is an adulteress, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fourth he said: "I testify by Allah that I have not approached her for four months, and that I am surely of the truthful." Then in the fifth he said: "The curse of Allah be upon 'Uwaymir" — meaning himself — "if he is of the liars concerning what he said."

Then he ordered him to sit and said to Khawlah: "Stand." She stood and said: "I testify by Allah that I am not an adulteress, and that 'Uwaymir is surely of the liars." Then in the second she said: "I testify by Allah that he did not see Shurayk upon my belly, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the third she said: "I testify by Allah that I am pregnant by him, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fourth she said: "I testify by Allah that he never saw me in an act of indecency, and that he is surely of the liars." Then in the fifth she said: "The wrath of Allah be upon Khawlah" — meaning herself — "if he is of the truthful." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them and said: "Were it not for these oaths, I would have had an opinion regarding their affair. Watch for her delivery: if she brings forth a reddish, thick-necked, long-stretching one inclining to blackness, he belongs to Shurayk ibn al-Sahma'; and if she brings forth a dark-brown, curly-haired, thin-legged one, he belongs to the one she was accused of with." [21]

Ibn 'Abbas said: She brought forth the one most resembling Shurayk among the creation of Allah. [[Sunan Ibn Majah with variations: 1/668, no. 2067.]]

Mention of the ruling of the verse:

If a man accuses his wife of adultery, the hadd becomes obligatory upon him, and he may free himself from it by producing evidence of her adultery or by li'an. If he produces evidence, it establishes her adultery and the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. If he performs li'an, it establishes adultery against her, and she may free herself from it by li'an; if she does not perform li'an, the hadd becomes obligatory upon her. The husband may perform li'an whether or not he is able to produce evidence. Li'an is valid from every husband who is legally responsible, whether free or slave, Muslim or disbeliever; whoever's oath is valid, his accusation and li'an are valid.

The people of Iraq said: li'an is between any two free, adult persons, and li'an is not valid except before the judge or his deputy. When he conducts li'an between them, it is made stricter upon them in four respects: the number of formulas, the place, the time, and gathering the people.

As for the formula, it is four testimonies, and the fifth mentions the curse for the man and mentions the wrath for the woman, and the manner of this has already passed. As for the place, it is sought in the noblest places of the lands: if in Mecca, then at the Corner and the Maqam; if in Medina, then at the pulpit; if in Jerusalem, then in its mosque; and if in the rest of the cities, then in their mosques. If they are disbelievers, they are sent to the place they regard as sacred: if they are Jews, to the synagogue; if Christians, to the church; if Magians, to the fire-temple; and if they have no religion, like the idolaters, li'an is conducted between them in the session of his judgment. As for the time, it is after the 'Asr prayer. As for the number, it is required that there be four persons or more. The formula and gathering of people are conditions, while the place and time are recommended. When they perform li'an, four rulings attach to it: the falling of the hadd, the negation of the child, the termination of the marital bed, and the occurrence of permanent prohibition. All of this attaches to the husband's li'an. As for the wife's li'an, it only removes the hadd. If the man retracts his accusation, what is upon him returns (the hadd and lineage are restored to him), but what belongs to him does not return: the prohibition and the bed remain his, and they do not return. The separation by li'an is a annulment (fasakh), because it came from the wife's side.

Abu Hanifah and Sufyan said: li'an is a irrevocable single divorce, because it begins from the husband's side. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 1–10 (part 1 of 2):

Medinan. It has 5,680 letters, 1,316 words, and 64 verses.

Abu al-Husayn al-Khabbazi related to us, saying: Ibn Hibban related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ali al-Farqadi related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Amr related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Atiyya related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, saying:
Zayd ibn Aslam related to us from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat an-Nur will be given the reward of ten good deeds for every believer, in the past and in the future." [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 7/216.]] [19].

And al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shayba related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Karabisi related to us, saying: Salman ibn Tawba Abu Dawud al-Ansari related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Shami related to us, saying: Shu'ayb ibn Ishaq related to us from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) and her father, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not house women in upper chambers, do not teach them writing, but teach them spinning and Surat an-Nur." [[Zad al-Masir of Ibn al-Jawzi: 5/339.]].

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

"A surah which We have sent down" — the common reading is with the nominative (surah), meaning "this is a surah," because the Arabs do not begin with an indefinite noun; this is the view of al-Khalil. Al-Akhfash said: surah is a subject (mubtada') and its predicate is in "We have sent down." Talha ibn Musarrif [in the second copy: Mudarrif] read surah in the accusative, meaning "We have sent down a surah," and the pronoun is an extra connecting element. It was also said: "follow a surah which We have sent down." "And We have made it obligatory" — i.e., We have imposed the rulings contained in it. Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read "wa-farradnaha" with the doubled letter, meaning "We have explained and clarified it." It was also said: it is from "fard" (obligation), and the doubling indicates intensification, meaning We made them various obligations, and imposed them upon you and upon those after you until the Hour. The support for the lightened form is His saying: "Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an..." [[Al-Qasas: 85.]].
