She said: I said: "And what is it?" She told me the talk of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in to me, greeted, and then said: "How are you?" I said: "Would you permit me to go to my parents?" She said: I wanted at that time to be certain of the news from them both. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted me, so I went to my parents and said to my mother: "O mother, what are the people talking about?"
She said: "O daughter, make it easy on yourself, for by Allah, there has rarely been a woman who was beautiful with a husband who loved her, and who had co-wives, but they did not provoke her much." I said: "Glory be to Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?" She said: "Yes." She said:
I spent that night until morning, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then I woke up weeping. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zayd when revelation was delayed, and consulted them about separating from his family.
As for Usama, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the affection he held for them in his heart, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good." As for 'Ali, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her. If you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barira and said: "O Barira, have you seen anything that makes you doubt concerning the affair of 'A'isha?" Barira said to him: "By He who sent you with the truth, if I have seen anything in her that I would conceal, it is no more than that she is a young girl who sleeps over her family's dough, so a domestic animal comes and eats it."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and sought his excuse from 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said while on the pulpit:
"O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me concerning my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my family's house except with me."
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood and said: "I excuse you, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, you have ordered us and we will do your command."
She said: Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, who was the chief of the Khazraj, and was a righteous man, but partisan zeal carried him away, said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You lie, by the life of Allah!" Sa'd said: "By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites."
She said: The Aws and the Khazraj rose up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to calm them until they were silent, and he was silent.
She said: I remained that day, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep, while my parents thought that weeping would split my liver.
She said: While they were both sitting with me, and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, and I permitted her, so she sat and wept with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, and sat. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said about me had been said to me, and he had remained for a month without revelation concerning my affair. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat, then said: "As to what follows, O 'A'isha, it has reached me that such and such is said about you. If you are innocent, Allah, glorified is He, will clear you. And if you have committed a sin, seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I did not feel a single drop. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So I said, and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this matter until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you a sin, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Yusuf, and I do not remember his name: 'So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.'"
She said: Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I, by Allah, at that time knew that I was innocent, and that Allah, glorified is He, would clear me by my innocence. But, by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning my affair to be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my own estimation for Allah to speak about me with a matter to be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream by which Allah would clear me.
She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when Allah, glorified is He, sent down revelation upon His Prophet (ﷺ). He was seized by what used to seize him of the distress at the time of revelation, until sweat poured from him like pearls, even in the cold day, from the weight of the revelation that was sent down to him.
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was: "Rejoice, O 'A'isha, by Allah, Allah has cleared you." My mother said to me: "Get up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise anyone but Allah, glorified is He, who sent down my innocence."
She said: Then Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you," ten verses, and Allah, glorified is He, sent down this verse for my innocence.
She said: Abu Bakr, who used to spend on Mistah because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about 'A'isha." So Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the kinsmen..." up to "Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?" (Qur'an 24:22).
Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I indeed love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistah the maintenance that he used to give him, and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."
'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): "What do you know, or what have you seen?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing but good."
'A'isha said: She was the one who used to rival me among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah, glorified is He, protected her through piety. And her sister Hamna bint Jahsh fought on her behalf, and she perished among those who perished.
Al-Zuhri said: This is what has reached us from these men.
Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh narrated to us in Makka, and Muhammad ibn Harb al-Madini in al-Fustat, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me from Hisham ibn 'Urwa from his father from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. Abu Uways said: And 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr also narrated to me from 'Amra from 'A'isha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ), when he wished to travel on a journey, would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, he took her with him. So the lot of 'A'isha came out in the campaign of the Prophet (ﷺ) against Banu al-Mustaliq of Khuza'a, and he mentioned the report at length with a similar meaning.
'Urwa said, concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) questioning Barira about 'A'isha: He rebuked her, some of his companions said: "Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah." 'Urwa said: That was criticized in the one who said it. She said: "No, by Allah, I know nothing about her except what the goldsmith knows of red gold ingots. And if she had done what the people say, Allah would inform you of it." So the people marvelled at her understanding.
He said: When that was reported to the one who had been spoken of, he said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I never uncovered the side of a woman ever," and he was then killed as a martyr in the way of Allah. And he added at its end: She said: Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal lay in wait for Hassan ibn Thabit, and struck him with a sword, and when he struck him he said:
"Get out of the way of the sword's blow from me, for I am a youth, when I am provoked, and I am not a poet.
But I protect my sanctuary and take revenge on the lying slanderer who accused the innocent ones."
Hassan ibn Thabit shouted and called the people for help against Safwan, so Safwan fled. Hassan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained about Safwan for his striking him. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked him to forgive Safwan's striking him, and he forgave it for the Prophet (ﷺ), and in return he was compensated with a great palm garden and a Roman slave girl. Then Hassan sold that garden to Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan during his governorship for a great sum of money. 'A'isha said: Poetry was then composed about the people of the slander.
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Mistah for his slandering 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and he was called 'Awf:
"O 'Awf, woe to you, why did you not say a word of knowledge, and did not seek thereby any gain?
Then the heat of a proud people seized you, and 'Awf was not one to cut off in cutting.
When you slandered a chaste woman, not defiled, trustworthy in her pocket, of whom we knew no lowliness,
among those who slandered her, and you were a people of falsehood, using ugly speech, of foul language,
then Allah sent down an excuse for her innocence, and what 'Awf and Allah's dealings with him had done.
So if I live, I will repay 'Awf for his speech with the worst recompense, for what I found to be following."
Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari, then al-Najjari, said, clearing 'A'isha of what was said about her and apologizing to her:
"A chaste, sound woman, who is not suspected of a rank, and who wakes up hungry from the flesh of heedless women.
A wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance, and the generous, bountiful virtues.
A noble lady of a tribe of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, of noble endeavours, whose glory never departs.
Refined, whose tent Allah has perfumed, and purified her from every blemish and falsehood.
If what came from me was what was said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And what has been said is not a blemish upon you for all time, but the speech of a man who is not a fool.
And how, when my love, as long as I live, and my support for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings,
they have a rank high above the people, whose excellence the reach of the boaster falls short of."
He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that those who slandered 'A'isha be given the prescribed punishment, eighty lashes each. Hassan ibn Thabit said:
"'Abd Allah has indeed been repaid, though he was not of his people, and Mistah, when they said his name was 'hajir' (evil talk).
They pursued stoning with words against the wife of their Prophet, and they earned the wrath of the Lord, the Generous, so they were ruined.
They harmed the Messenger of Allah concerning her, so they covered over the disgraces of humiliation with which they were disgraced and exposed."

So this is the occasion of revelation of the verse and its story. As for the tafsir, His saying, Exalted is He: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander" — with falsehood — "are a band" — a group — "among you."

Al-Farra' said: "al-'usba" is the group, from one to forty.

"Do not reckon it an evil for you" — O 'A'isha and Safwan — "rather it is good for you," because Allah will reward you for it and make your innocence manifest. "For every man of them" — meaning of those who brought the slander — "is what he earned of sin," the recompense for what he committed of sin and disobedience.

"And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof" — who bore most of it, and so began the talk of it. The reading of the majority is "kibrahu" with a kasra on the kaf; Khalil, al-A'raj and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read it with a damma on the kaf.

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: This is an error, because "kubr" with a damma on the kaf is used for lineage and age. From it is the hadith: "Clientage is for the eldest," and he is the eldest son of a man among the males and the closest of them to him in lineage.

Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, like "saffar" and "sifr."

The exegetes differed concerning the one meant by His saying, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment."

Some people said: It is Hassan ibn Thabit.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from 'Amir al-Sha'bi that 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I have not heard of anything more beautiful than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I quoted it I hoped for Paradise for him. His saying to Abu Sufyan:

"You satirized Muhammad, so answer for him, and with Allah is the recompense in that.
My father, my mother, and my honour are a shield for the honour of Muhammad from you.
Do you revile him, when you are not his equal? So the evil of you both is a ransom for the good of the two of you.
My tongue is a sharp sword with no flaw in it, and my sea is not muddied by buckets."

It was said: O Mother of the Believers, does not Allah say, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: Has he not already suffered a great punishment? Did his sight not depart, and was he not struck with the sword and paralysed?

Abu al-Duha related from Masruq who said: I was with 'A'isha when Hassan ibn Thabit entered, and she ordered that a cushion be placed for him. When he left, I said to 'A'isha: Do you allow this man to enter upon you when he said what he said, and Allah sent down concerning him, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: And what punishment is more severe than blindness? Perhaps Allah made that great punishment the loss of his sight. And she said: He used to defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, it is 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 11–20 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said in the hadith of the slander (al-ifk): "Then I mounted, and Safwan took hold of the reins, and we passed by a group of the hypocrites, and it was their custom to alight apart from the people. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, their leader, said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'ʿAʾishah.' He said: 'By God, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her. The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her.'" Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah also took up the matter, and they were the ones who took the lead in it. Then the matter spread among the people.

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not think well of their own kind, and say: "This is an obvious lie"?﴾

Al-Hasan said: "Their own kind" means the people of their religion, because the believers are like a single soul. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa’: 29.]] and His saying: ﴿So greet one another﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 61.]].

Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: the sense of the verse is: "Why, when you heard it, did you not think as the believing men and the believing women thought well of their own selves."

It was also said: He meant by "their own selves" their families and their wives. They said: this verse refers to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife Umm Ayyub.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from his shaykhs that his wife Umm Ayyub said to Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd: "O Abu Ayyub, do you not hear what people are saying about ʿAʾishah?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by God, I would not have done it." He said: "Then ʿAʾishah, by God, is better than you. Glory be to God, this is a great slander." So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not...﴾ the verses, i.e., as Abu Ayyub and his wife did and as they both said.

His saying: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾ means: a clear lie.

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in the sight of God, are the liars.﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into of the slander.﴾ "Plunged into" means: engaged in, from the slander.

﴿When you received it with your tongues⁠—taking it up and relating it from one another.﴾ Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿idh tatalaqqawnahu﴾ with two tas, [[From talaqqi (to receive).]] and ʿAʾishah read: ﴿talliqunahu﴾ with a kasrah on the lam and a light qaf, from the lie. Al-walq, al-alaq, al-alq and al-liq all mean lying. [[It is in Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/61.]]

Al-Khalil said: the root of walq is haste, and he recited:

"They came in troops from Syria, hastening" [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/13.]]

meaning, they hasten. It is said: "Walaqa fulan fi al-sayr," meaning he persisted in the journey and hastened in it. So the meaning of ʿAʾishah's reading is: "when you persist in your lie."

Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ read: ﴿idh tulqunahu﴾ from iltiqa' (casting), [[With a damma on the ta', sukun on the lam and damma on the qaf, from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 12/204.]] and its parallel and proof is His saying: ﴿And they cast to them the word﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 36.]] and so on.

﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you think it is trivial, while it is, in the sight of God, great.﴾

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ "Glory be to You" may carry the sense of exalting God above such things, or of wonder.

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ "He admonishes you" means He forbids you and warns you that you return; it was also said: "He admonishes you lest you return to its like."

﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of the matter of ʿAʾishah and Safwan; All-Wise, who judged her innocent.

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.﴾ This refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his hypocrite companions.

﴿And God knows, while you do not know.﴾ ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Kind and Merciful⁠—﴾ here there is an implied sense: that He would have hastened His punishment upon you.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 11–20 (part 1 of 2):

Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you (Qur'an 24:11), and so on.

Mention of the occasion of revelation of these verses and the story of the slander (al-ifk).

Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mihrajan informed us, by my reading to him, and he acknowledged it, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us in the year 316, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us. And Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-San'ani narrated to us, saying:
We read to 'Abd al-Razzaq, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, 'Alqama ibn Waqqas, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba ibn Mas'ud informed me, concerning the report of 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the people of the slander said what they said to her, and Allah cleared her. Each of them related to me a portion of her report, and some of them were more retentive of it than others. I have retained from each one the report that he related to me, and some of their reports confirm others. They mentioned that 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), and may Allah be pleased with her, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take her with him.
'A'isha said: He drew lots among us in a campaign he undertook, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was after Allah, glorified is He, had revealed the hijab. I was carried in my howdah, and I would be lowered from it at our halts. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his campaign and returned, and we drew near Madina, he announced the departure one night, so I got up when they announced the departure, and I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to the saddle and touched my chest, and my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and my search for it detained me. Meanwhile, the men who used to load the camel came, lifted my howdah, and fastened it onto my camel on which I used to ride, and they thought I was in it.
She said: The women at that time were light, not weighed down by flesh; they would only eat a little food. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they loaded it and lifted it. I was a young girl, so they sent the camel off and marched on. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their campsite, and there was no caller and no answerer there. So I headed to my place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I slept. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had stayed behind the army. He set out at night and reached my place at dawn, and he saw the figure of a sleeping person and came to me, and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the hijab was prescribed for me. I awoke only by his saying "Inna lillah," when he recognized me, so I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not speak a word to me besides his "Inna lillah," until he made his mount kneel and I stepped on its foreleg, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted in the blazing heat of midday. Whoever was to perish, perished concerning my affair, and the one who took the lead in the slander was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. I came to Madina, and I fell ill for a month upon my arrival, while the people were engaged in the talk of the people of the slander, and I was not aware of any of that. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not notice from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the gentleness that I used to see from him when I was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would only come in, greet, and then say: "How are you?" and I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had recovered, going out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi', which was our place for relieving ourselves, and we did not go out except at night to night, and that was before we took toilets close to our houses. Our practice was the ancient practice of the Arabs regarding relieving oneself in open spaces, for we were harmed by having toilets near our houses. So I set out, I and Umm Mistah, who was 'Atika bint Abi Ruhm ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn 'Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthatha ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. I and the daughter of Abi Ruhm came back toward my house when we had finished our need, and Umm Mistah stumbled over her cloak, and she said: "Mistah is ruined!" I said to her: "What a bad thing you said! Do you revile a man who witnessed Badr?" She said: "O you! Did you not hear what he said?"
She said: I said: "And what is it?" She told me the talk of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in to me, greeted, and then said: "How are you?" I said: "Would you permit me to go to my parents?" She said: I wanted at that time to be certain of the news from them both. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted me, so I went to my parents and said to my mother: "O mother, what are the people talking about?"
She said: "O daughter, make it easy on yourself, for by Allah, there has rarely been a woman who was beautiful with a husband who loved her, and who had co-wives, but they did not provoke her much." I said: "Glory be to Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?" She said: "Yes." She said:
I spent that night until morning, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then I woke up weeping. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zayd when revelation was delayed, and consulted them about separating from his family.
As for Usama, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the affection he held for them in his heart, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good." As for 'Ali, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her. If you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barira and said: "O Barira, have you seen anything that makes you doubt concerning the affair of 'A'isha?" Barira said to him: "By He who sent you with the truth, if I have seen anything in her that I would conceal, it is no more than that she is a young girl who sleeps over her family's dough, so a domestic animal comes and eats it."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and sought his excuse from 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said while on the pulpit:
"O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me concerning my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my family's house except with me."
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood and said: "I excuse you, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, you have ordered us and we will do your command."
She said: Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, who was the chief of the Khazraj, and was a righteous man, but partisan zeal carried him away, said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You lie, by the life of Allah!" Sa'd said: "By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites."
She said: The Aws and the Khazraj rose up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to calm them until they were silent, and he was silent.
She said: I remained that day, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep, while my parents thought that weeping would split my liver.
She said: While they were both sitting with me, and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, and I permitted her, so she sat and wept with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, and sat. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said about me had been said to me, and he had remained for a month without revelation concerning my affair. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat, then said: "As to what follows, O 'A'isha, it has reached me that such and such is said about you. If you are innocent, Allah, glorified is He, will clear you. And if you have committed a sin, seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I did not feel a single drop. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So I said, and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this matter until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you a sin, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Yusuf, and I do not remember his name: 'So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.'"
She said: Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I, by Allah, at that time knew that I was innocent, and that Allah, glorified is He, would clear me by my innocence. But, by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning my affair to be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my own estimation for Allah to speak about me with a matter to be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream by which Allah would clear me.
She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when Allah, glorified is He, sent down revelation upon His Prophet (ﷺ). He was seized by what used to seize him of the distress at the time of revelation, until sweat poured from him like pearls, even in the cold day, from the weight of the revelation that was sent down to him.
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was: "Rejoice, O 'A'isha, by Allah, Allah has cleared you." My mother said to me: "Get up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise anyone but Allah, glorified is He, who sent down my innocence."
She said: Then Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you," ten verses, and Allah, glorified is He, sent down this verse for my innocence.
She said: Abu Bakr, who used to spend on Mistah because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about 'A'isha." So Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the kinsmen..." up to "Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?" (Qur'an 24:22).
Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I indeed love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistah the maintenance that he used to give him, and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."
'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): "What do you know, or what have you seen?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing but good."
'A'isha said: She was the one who used to rival me among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah, glorified is He, protected her through piety. And her sister Hamna bint Jahsh fought on her behalf, and she perished among those who perished.
Al-Zuhri said: This is what has reached us from these men.
Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh narrated to us in Makka, and Muhammad ibn Harb al-Madini in al-Fustat, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me from Hisham ibn 'Urwa from his father from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. Abu Uways said: And 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr also narrated to me from 'Amra from 'A'isha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ), when he wished to travel on a journey, would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, he took her with him. So the lot of 'A'isha came out in the campaign of the Prophet (ﷺ) against Banu al-Mustaliq of Khuza'a, and he mentioned the report at length with a similar meaning.
'Urwa said, concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) questioning Barira about 'A'isha: He rebuked her, some of his companions said: "Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah." 'Urwa said: That was criticized in the one who said it. She said: "No, by Allah, I know nothing about her except what the goldsmith knows of red gold ingots. And if she had done what the people say, Allah would inform you of it." So the people marvelled at her understanding.
He said: When that was reported to the one who had been spoken of, he said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I never uncovered the side of a woman ever," and he was then killed as a martyr in the way of Allah. And he added at its end: She said: Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal lay in wait for Hassan ibn Thabit, and struck him with a sword, and when he struck him he said:
"Get out of the way of the sword's blow from me, for I am a youth, when I am provoked, and I am not a poet.
But I protect my sanctuary and take revenge on the lying slanderer who accused the innocent ones."
Hassan ibn Thabit shouted and called the people for help against Safwan, so Safwan fled. Hassan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained about Safwan for his striking him. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked him to forgive Safwan's striking him, and he forgave it for the Prophet (ﷺ), and in return he was compensated with a great palm garden and a Roman slave girl. Then Hassan sold that garden to Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan during his governorship for a great sum of money. 'A'isha said: Poetry was then composed about the people of the slander.
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Mistah for his slandering 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and he was called 'Awf:
"O 'Awf, woe to you, why did you not say a word of knowledge, and did not seek thereby any gain?
Then the heat of a proud people seized you, and 'Awf was not one to cut off in cutting.
When you slandered a chaste woman, not defiled, trustworthy in her pocket, of whom we knew no lowliness,
among those who slandered her, and you were a people of falsehood, using ugly speech, of foul language,
then Allah sent down an excuse for her innocence, and what 'Awf and Allah's dealings with him had done.
So if I live, I will repay 'Awf for his speech with the worst recompense, for what I found to be following."
Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari, then al-Najjari, said, clearing 'A'isha of what was said about her and apologizing to her:
"A chaste, sound woman, who is not suspected of a rank, and who wakes up hungry from the flesh of heedless women.
A wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance, and the generous, bountiful virtues.
A noble lady of a tribe of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, of noble endeavours, whose glory never departs.
Refined, whose tent Allah has perfumed, and purified her from every blemish and falsehood.
If what came from me was what was said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And what has been said is not a blemish upon you for all time, but the speech of a man who is not a fool.
And how, when my love, as long as I live, and my support for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings,
they have a rank high above the people, whose excellence the reach of the boaster falls short of."
He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that those who slandered 'A'isha be given the prescribed punishment, eighty lashes each. Hassan ibn Thabit said:
"'Abd Allah has indeed been repaid, though he was not of his people, and Mistah, when they said his name was 'hajir' (evil talk).
They pursued stoning with words against the wife of their Prophet, and they earned the wrath of the Lord, the Generous, so they were ruined.
They harmed the Messenger of Allah concerning her, so they covered over the disgraces of humiliation with which they were disgraced and exposed."

So this is the occasion of revelation of the verse and its story. As for the tafsir, His saying, Exalted is He: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander" — with falsehood — "are a band" — a group — "among you."

Al-Farra' said: "al-'usba" is the group, from one to forty.

"Do not reckon it an evil for you" — O 'A'isha and Safwan — "rather it is good for you," because Allah will reward you for it and make your innocence manifest. "For every man of them" — meaning of those who brought the slander — "is what he earned of sin," the recompense for what he committed of sin and disobedience.

"And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof" — who bore most of it, and so began the talk of it. The reading of the majority is "kibrahu" with a kasra on the kaf; Khalil, al-A'raj and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read it with a damma on the kaf.

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: This is an error, because "kubr" with a damma on the kaf is used for lineage and age. From it is the hadith: "Clientage is for the eldest," and he is the eldest son of a man among the males and the closest of them to him in lineage.

Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, like "saffar" and "sifr."

The exegetes differed concerning the one meant by His saying, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment."

Some people said: It is Hassan ibn Thabit.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from 'Amir al-Sha'bi that 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I have not heard of anything more beautiful than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I quoted it I hoped for Paradise for him. His saying to Abu Sufyan:

"You satirized Muhammad, so answer for him, and with Allah is the recompense in that.
My father, my mother, and my honour are a shield for the honour of Muhammad from you.
Do you revile him, when you are not his equal? So the evil of you both is a ransom for the good of the two of you.
My tongue is a sharp sword with no flaw in it, and my sea is not muddied by buckets."

It was said: O Mother of the Believers, does not Allah say, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: Has he not already suffered a great punishment? Did his sight not depart, and was he not struck with the sword and paralysed?

Abu al-Duha related from Masruq who said: I was with 'A'isha when Hassan ibn Thabit entered, and she ordered that a cushion be placed for him. When he left, I said to 'A'isha: Do you allow this man to enter upon you when he said what he said, and Allah sent down concerning him, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: And what punishment is more severe than blindness? Perhaps Allah made that great punishment the loss of his sight. And she said: He used to defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, it is 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 11–20 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said in the hadith of the slander (al-ifk): "Then I mounted, and Safwan took hold of the reins, and we passed by a group of the hypocrites, and it was their custom to alight apart from the people. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, their leader, said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'ʿAʾishah.' He said: 'By God, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her. The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her.'" Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah also took up the matter, and they were the ones who took the lead in it. Then the matter spread among the people.

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not think well of their own kind, and say: "This is an obvious lie"?﴾

Al-Hasan said: "Their own kind" means the people of their religion, because the believers are like a single soul. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa’: 29.]] and His saying: ﴿So greet one another﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 61.]].

Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: the sense of the verse is: "Why, when you heard it, did you not think as the believing men and the believing women thought well of their own selves."

It was also said: He meant by "their own selves" their families and their wives. They said: this verse refers to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife Umm Ayyub.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from his shaykhs that his wife Umm Ayyub said to Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd: "O Abu Ayyub, do you not hear what people are saying about ʿAʾishah?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by God, I would not have done it." He said: "Then ʿAʾishah, by God, is better than you. Glory be to God, this is a great slander." So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not...﴾ the verses, i.e., as Abu Ayyub and his wife did and as they both said.

His saying: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾ means: a clear lie.

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in the sight of God, are the liars.﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into of the slander.﴾ "Plunged into" means: engaged in, from the slander.

﴿When you received it with your tongues⁠—taking it up and relating it from one another.﴾ Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿idh tatalaqqawnahu﴾ with two tas, [[From talaqqi (to receive).]] and ʿAʾishah read: ﴿talliqunahu﴾ with a kasrah on the lam and a light qaf, from the lie. Al-walq, al-alaq, al-alq and al-liq all mean lying. [[It is in Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/61.]]

Al-Khalil said: the root of walq is haste, and he recited:

"They came in troops from Syria, hastening" [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/13.]]

meaning, they hasten. It is said: "Walaqa fulan fi al-sayr," meaning he persisted in the journey and hastened in it. So the meaning of ʿAʾishah's reading is: "when you persist in your lie."

Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ read: ﴿idh tulqunahu﴾ from iltiqa' (casting), [[With a damma on the ta', sukun on the lam and damma on the qaf, from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 12/204.]] and its parallel and proof is His saying: ﴿And they cast to them the word﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 36.]] and so on.

﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you think it is trivial, while it is, in the sight of God, great.﴾

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ "Glory be to You" may carry the sense of exalting God above such things, or of wonder.

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ "He admonishes you" means He forbids you and warns you that you return; it was also said: "He admonishes you lest you return to its like."

﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of the matter of ʿAʾishah and Safwan; All-Wise, who judged her innocent.

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.﴾ This refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his hypocrite companions.

﴿And God knows, while you do not know.﴾ ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Kind and Merciful⁠—﴾ here there is an implied sense: that He would have hastened His punishment upon you.

Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you (Qur'an 24:11), and so on.

Mention of the occasion of revelation of these verses and the story of the slander (al-ifk).

Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mihrajan informed us, by my reading to him, and he acknowledged it, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us in the year 316, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us. And Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-San'ani narrated to us, saying:
We read to 'Abd al-Razzaq, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, 'Alqama ibn Waqqas, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba ibn Mas'ud informed me, concerning the report of 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the people of the slander said what they said to her, and Allah cleared her. Each of them related to me a portion of her report, and some of them were more retentive of it than others. I have retained from each one the report that he related to me, and some of their reports confirm others. They mentioned that 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), and may Allah be pleased with her, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take her with him.
'A'isha said: He drew lots among us in a campaign he undertook, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was after Allah, glorified is He, had revealed the hijab. I was carried in my howdah, and I would be lowered from it at our halts. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his campaign and returned, and we drew near Madina, he announced the departure one night, so I got up when they announced the departure, and I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to the saddle and touched my chest, and my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and my search for it detained me. Meanwhile, the men who used to load the camel came, lifted my howdah, and fastened it onto my camel on which I used to ride, and they thought I was in it.
She said: The women at that time were light, not weighed down by flesh; they would only eat a little food. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they loaded it and lifted it. I was a young girl, so they sent the camel off and marched on. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their campsite, and there was no caller and no answerer there. So I headed to my place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I slept. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had stayed behind the army. He set out at night and reached my place at dawn, and he saw the figure of a sleeping person and came to me, and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the hijab was prescribed for me. I awoke only by his saying "Inna lillah," when he recognized me, so I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not speak a word to me besides his "Inna lillah," until he made his mount kneel and I stepped on its foreleg, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted in the blazing heat of midday. Whoever was to perish, perished concerning my affair, and the one who took the lead in the slander was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. I came to Madina, and I fell ill for a month upon my arrival, while the people were engaged in the talk of the people of the slander, and I was not aware of any of that. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not notice from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the gentleness that I used to see from him when I was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would only come in, greet, and then say: "How are you?" and I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had recovered, going out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi', which was our place for relieving ourselves, and we did not go out except at night to night, and that was before we took toilets close to our houses. Our practice was the ancient practice of the Arabs regarding relieving oneself in open spaces, for we were harmed by having toilets near our houses. So I set out, I and Umm Mistah, who was 'Atika bint Abi Ruhm ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn 'Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthatha ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. I and the daughter of Abi Ruhm came back toward my house when we had finished our need, and Umm Mistah stumbled over her cloak, and she said: "Mistah is ruined!" I said to her: "What a bad thing you said! Do you revile a man who witnessed Badr?" She said: "O you! Did you not hear what he said?"
She said: I said: "And what is it?" She told me the talk of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in to me, greeted, and then said: "How are you?" I said: "Would you permit me to go to my parents?" She said: I wanted at that time to be certain of the news from them both. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted me, so I went to my parents and said to my mother: "O mother, what are the people talking about?"
She said: "O daughter, make it easy on yourself, for by Allah, there has rarely been a woman who was beautiful with a husband who loved her, and who had co-wives, but they did not provoke her much." I said: "Glory be to Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?" She said: "Yes." She said:
I spent that night until morning, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then I woke up weeping. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zayd when revelation was delayed, and consulted them about separating from his family.
As for Usama, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the affection he held for them in his heart, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good." As for 'Ali, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her. If you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barira and said: "O Barira, have you seen anything that makes you doubt concerning the affair of 'A'isha?" Barira said to him: "By He who sent you with the truth, if I have seen anything in her that I would conceal, it is no more than that she is a young girl who sleeps over her family's dough, so a domestic animal comes and eats it."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and sought his excuse from 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said while on the pulpit:
"O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me concerning my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my family's house except with me."
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood and said: "I excuse you, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, you have ordered us and we will do your command."
She said: Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, who was the chief of the Khazraj, and was a righteous man, but partisan zeal carried him away, said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You lie, by the life of Allah!" Sa'd said: "By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites."
She said: The Aws and the Khazraj rose up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to calm them until they were silent, and he was silent.
She said: I remained that day, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep, while my parents thought that weeping would split my liver.
She said: While they were both sitting with me, and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, and I permitted her, so she sat and wept with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, and sat. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said about me had been said to me, and he had remained for a month without revelation concerning my affair. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat, then said: "As to what follows, O 'A'isha, it has reached me that such and such is said about you. If you are innocent, Allah, glorified is He, will clear you. And if you have committed a sin, seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I did not feel a single drop. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So I said, and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this matter until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you a sin, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Yusuf, and I do not remember his name: 'So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.'"
She said: Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I, by Allah, at that time knew that I was innocent, and that Allah, glorified is He, would clear me by my innocence. But, by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning my affair to be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my own estimation for Allah to speak about me with a matter to be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream by which Allah would clear me.
She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when Allah, glorified is He, sent down revelation upon His Prophet (ﷺ). He was seized by what used to seize him of the distress at the time of revelation, until sweat poured from him like pearls, even in the cold day, from the weight of the revelation that was sent down to him.
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved, he was smiling, and the first word he spoke was: "Rejoice, O 'A'isha, by Allah, Allah has cleared you." My mother said to me: "Get up and go to him." I said: "By Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise anyone but Allah, glorified is He, who sent down my innocence."
She said: Then Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you," ten verses, and Allah, glorified is He, sent down this verse for my innocence.
She said: Abu Bakr, who used to spend on Mistah because of his kinship to him and his poverty, said: "By Allah, I will never spend anything on him again after what he said about 'A'isha." So Allah, glorified is He, sent down: "And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to the kinsmen..." up to "Do you not love that Allah should forgive you?" (Qur'an 24:22).
Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "By Allah, I indeed love that Allah should forgive me." So he returned to Mistah the maintenance that he used to give him, and said: "I will never withdraw it from him."
'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had asked Zaynab bint Jahsh, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): "What do you know, or what have you seen?" She said: "O Messenger of Allah, I guard my hearing and my sight. By Allah, I know nothing but good."
'A'isha said: She was the one who used to rival me among the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), but Allah, glorified is He, protected her through piety. And her sister Hamna bint Jahsh fought on her behalf, and she perished among those who perished.
Al-Zuhri said: This is what has reached us from these men.
Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sa'igh narrated to us in Makka, and Muhammad ibn Harb al-Madini in al-Fustat, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me from Hisham ibn 'Urwa from his father from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. Abu Uways said: And 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr also narrated to me from 'Amra from 'A'isha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ), when he wished to travel on a journey, would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, he took her with him. So the lot of 'A'isha came out in the campaign of the Prophet (ﷺ) against Banu al-Mustaliq of Khuza'a, and he mentioned the report at length with a similar meaning.
'Urwa said, concerning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) questioning Barira about 'A'isha: He rebuked her, some of his companions said: "Speak the truth to the Messenger of Allah." 'Urwa said: That was criticized in the one who said it. She said: "No, by Allah, I know nothing about her except what the goldsmith knows of red gold ingots. And if she had done what the people say, Allah would inform you of it." So the people marvelled at her understanding.
He said: When that was reported to the one who had been spoken of, he said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I never uncovered the side of a woman ever," and he was then killed as a martyr in the way of Allah. And he added at its end: She said: Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal lay in wait for Hassan ibn Thabit, and struck him with a sword, and when he struck him he said:
"Get out of the way of the sword's blow from me, for I am a youth, when I am provoked, and I am not a poet.
But I protect my sanctuary and take revenge on the lying slanderer who accused the innocent ones."
Hassan ibn Thabit shouted and called the people for help against Safwan, so Safwan fled. Hassan came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained about Safwan for his striking him. The Prophet (ﷺ) asked him to forgive Safwan's striking him, and he forgave it for the Prophet (ﷺ), and in return he was compensated with a great palm garden and a Roman slave girl. Then Hassan sold that garden to Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan during his governorship for a great sum of money. 'A'isha said: Poetry was then composed about the people of the slander.
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said to Mistah for his slandering 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, and he was called 'Awf:
"O 'Awf, woe to you, why did you not say a word of knowledge, and did not seek thereby any gain?
Then the heat of a proud people seized you, and 'Awf was not one to cut off in cutting.
When you slandered a chaste woman, not defiled, trustworthy in her pocket, of whom we knew no lowliness,
among those who slandered her, and you were a people of falsehood, using ugly speech, of foul language,
then Allah sent down an excuse for her innocence, and what 'Awf and Allah's dealings with him had done.
So if I live, I will repay 'Awf for his speech with the worst recompense, for what I found to be following."
Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari, then al-Najjari, said, clearing 'A'isha of what was said about her and apologizing to her:
"A chaste, sound woman, who is not suspected of a rank, and who wakes up hungry from the flesh of heedless women.
A wife of the best of people in religion and lineage, the Prophet of guidance, and the generous, bountiful virtues.
A noble lady of a tribe of Lu'ayy ibn Ghalib, of noble endeavours, whose glory never departs.
Refined, whose tent Allah has perfumed, and purified her from every blemish and falsehood.
If what came from me was what was said, then may my fingers never raise my whip against me.
And what has been said is not a blemish upon you for all time, but the speech of a man who is not a fool.
And how, when my love, as long as I live, and my support for the family of the Messenger of Allah, the adornment of gatherings,
they have a rank high above the people, whose excellence the reach of the boaster falls short of."
He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered that those who slandered 'A'isha be given the prescribed punishment, eighty lashes each. Hassan ibn Thabit said:
"'Abd Allah has indeed been repaid, though he was not of his people, and Mistah, when they said his name was 'hajir' (evil talk).
They pursued stoning with words against the wife of their Prophet, and they earned the wrath of the Lord, the Generous, so they were ruined.
They harmed the Messenger of Allah concerning her, so they covered over the disgraces of humiliation with which they were disgraced and exposed."

So this is the occasion of revelation of the verse and its story. As for the tafsir, His saying, Exalted is He: "Verily, those who brought forth the slander" — with falsehood — "are a band" — a group — "among you."

Al-Farra' said: "al-'usba" is the group, from one to forty.

"Do not reckon it an evil for you" — O 'A'isha and Safwan — "rather it is good for you," because Allah will reward you for it and make your innocence manifest. "For every man of them" — meaning of those who brought the slander — "is what he earned of sin," the recompense for what he committed of sin and disobedience.

"And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof" — who bore most of it, and so began the talk of it. The reading of the majority is "kibrahu" with a kasra on the kaf; Khalil, al-A'raj and Ya'qub al-Hadrami read it with a damma on the kaf.

Abu 'Amr ibn al-'Ala' said: This is an error, because "kubr" with a damma on the kaf is used for lineage and age. From it is the hadith: "Clientage is for the eldest," and he is the eldest son of a man among the males and the closest of them to him in lineage.

Al-Kisa'i said: They are two dialects, like "saffar" and "sifr."

The exegetes differed concerning the one meant by His saying, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment."

Some people said: It is Hassan ibn Thabit.

Dawud ibn Abi Hind related from 'Amir al-Sha'bi that 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I have not heard of anything more beautiful than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I quoted it I hoped for Paradise for him. His saying to Abu Sufyan:

"You satirized Muhammad, so answer for him, and with Allah is the recompense in that.
My father, my mother, and my honour are a shield for the honour of Muhammad from you.
Do you revile him, when you are not his equal? So the evil of you both is a ransom for the good of the two of you.
My tongue is a sharp sword with no flaw in it, and my sea is not muddied by buckets."

It was said: O Mother of the Believers, does not Allah say, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: Has he not already suffered a great punishment? Did his sight not depart, and was he not struck with the sword and paralysed?

Abu al-Duha related from Masruq who said: I was with 'A'isha when Hassan ibn Thabit entered, and she ordered that a cushion be placed for him. When he left, I said to 'A'isha: Do you allow this man to enter upon you when he said what he said, and Allah sent down concerning him, "And he among them who took upon himself the greater part thereof, for him is a great punishment"?

She said: And what punishment is more severe than blindness? Perhaps Allah made that great punishment the loss of his sight. And she said: He used to defend the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Others said: Rather, it is 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his companions.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 11–20 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, who said in the hadith of the slander (al-ifk): "Then I mounted, and Safwan took hold of the reins, and we passed by a group of the hypocrites, and it was their custom to alight apart from the people. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, their leader, said: 'Who is this?' They said: 'ʿAʾishah.' He said: 'By God, she has not escaped from him, nor has he escaped from her. The wife of your Prophet spent the night with a man until morning, then he came leading her.'" Hassan, Mistah and Hamnah also took up the matter, and they were the ones who took the lead in it. Then the matter spread among the people.

﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not think well of their own kind, and say: "This is an obvious lie"?﴾

Al-Hasan said: "Their own kind" means the people of their religion, because the believers are like a single soul. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾ [[Surat al-Nisa’: 29.]] and His saying: ﴿So greet one another﴾ [[Surat al-Nur: 61.]].

Some of the scholars of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: the sense of the verse is: "Why, when you heard it, did you not think as the believing men and the believing women thought well of their own selves."

It was also said: He meant by "their own selves" their families and their wives. They said: this verse refers to Abu Ayyub al-Ansari and his wife Umm Ayyub.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar narrated from his shaykhs that his wife Umm Ayyub said to Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd: "O Abu Ayyub, do you not hear what people are saying about ʿAʾishah?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by God, I would not have done it." He said: "Then ʿAʾishah, by God, is better than you. Glory be to God, this is a great slander." So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not...﴾ the verses, i.e., as Abu Ayyub and his wife did and as they both said.

His saying: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾ means: a clear lie.

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in the sight of God, are the liars.﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into of the slander.﴾ "Plunged into" means: engaged in, from the slander.

﴿When you received it with your tongues⁠—taking it up and relating it from one another.﴾ Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿idh tatalaqqawnahu﴾ with two tas, [[From talaqqi (to receive).]] and ʿAʾishah read: ﴿talliqunahu﴾ with a kasrah on the lam and a light qaf, from the lie. Al-walq, al-alaq, al-alq and al-liq all mean lying. [[It is in Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/61.]]

Al-Khalil said: the root of walq is haste, and he recited:

"They came in troops from Syria, hastening" [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/13.]]

meaning, they hasten. It is said: "Walaqa fulan fi al-sayr," meaning he persisted in the journey and hastened in it. So the meaning of ʿAʾishah's reading is: "when you persist in your lie."

Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ read: ﴿idh tulqunahu﴾ from iltiqa' (casting), [[With a damma on the ta', sukun on the lam and damma on the qaf, from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 12/204.]] and its parallel and proof is His saying: ﴿And they cast to them the word﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 36.]] and so on.

﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you think it is trivial, while it is, in the sight of God, great.﴾

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ "Glory be to You" may carry the sense of exalting God above such things, or of wonder.

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ "He admonishes you" means He forbids you and warns you that you return; it was also said: "He admonishes you lest you return to its like."

﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of the matter of ʿAʾishah and Safwan; All-Wise, who judged her innocent.

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.﴾ This refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his hypocrite companions.

﴿And God knows, while you do not know.﴾ ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Kind and Merciful⁠—﴾ here there is an implied sense: that He would have hastened His punishment upon you.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 11–20 (part 1 of 2):

Verily, those who brought forth the slander are a band among you (Qur'an 24:11), and so on.

Mention of the occasion of revelation of these verses and the story of the slander (al-ifk).

Abu Nu'aym 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Mihrajan informed us, by my reading to him, and he acknowledged it, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us in the year 316, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us. And Abu Nu'aym informed us, saying: Abu 'Awana informed us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-San'ani narrated to us, saying:
We read to 'Abd al-Razzaq, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, 'Alqama ibn Waqqas, and 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utba ibn Mas'ud informed me, concerning the report of 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the people of the slander said what they said to her, and Allah cleared her. Each of them related to me a portion of her report, and some of them were more retentive of it than others. I have retained from each one the report that he related to me, and some of their reports confirm others. They mentioned that 'A'isha, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), and may Allah be pleased with her, said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever one's lot came out, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take her with him.
'A'isha said: He drew lots among us in a campaign he undertook, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was after Allah, glorified is He, had revealed the hijab. I was carried in my howdah, and I would be lowered from it at our halts. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his campaign and returned, and we drew near Madina, he announced the departure one night, so I got up when they announced the departure, and I walked until I passed the army. When I had finished my need, I came back to the saddle and touched my chest, and my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken. So I returned and searched for my necklace, and my search for it detained me. Meanwhile, the men who used to load the camel came, lifted my howdah, and fastened it onto my camel on which I used to ride, and they thought I was in it.
She said: The women at that time were light, not weighed down by flesh; they would only eat a little food. So the people did not notice the lightness of the howdah when they loaded it and lifted it. I was a young girl, so they sent the camel off and marched on. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their campsite, and there was no caller and no answerer there. So I headed to my place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return to me. While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I slept. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had stayed behind the army. He set out at night and reached my place at dawn, and he saw the figure of a sleeping person and came to me, and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the hijab was prescribed for me. I awoke only by his saying "Inna lillah," when he recognized me, so I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not speak a word to me besides his "Inna lillah," until he made his mount kneel and I stepped on its foreleg, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted in the blazing heat of midday. Whoever was to perish, perished concerning my affair, and the one who took the lead in the slander was 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. I came to Madina, and I fell ill for a month upon my arrival, while the people were engaged in the talk of the people of the slander, and I was not aware of any of that. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not notice from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the gentleness that I used to see from him when I was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would only come in, greet, and then say: "How are you?" and I was not aware of the evil until I went out after I had recovered, going out with Umm Mistah toward al-Manasi', which was our place for relieving ourselves, and we did not go out except at night to night, and that was before we took toilets close to our houses. Our practice was the ancient practice of the Arabs regarding relieving oneself in open spaces, for we were harmed by having toilets near our houses. So I set out, I and Umm Mistah, who was 'Atika bint Abi Ruhm ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn 'Abd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn 'Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthatha ibn 'Abbad ibn al-Muttalib. I and the daughter of Abi Ruhm came back toward my house when we had finished our need, and Umm Mistah stumbled over her cloak, and she said: "Mistah is ruined!" I said to her: "What a bad thing you said! Do you revile a man who witnessed Badr?" She said: "O you! Did you not hear what he said?"
She said: I said: "And what is it?" She told me the talk of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness. When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came in to me, greeted, and then said: "How are you?" I said: "Would you permit me to go to my parents?" She said: I wanted at that time to be certain of the news from them both. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted me, so I went to my parents and said to my mother: "O mother, what are the people talking about?"
She said: "O daughter, make it easy on yourself, for by Allah, there has rarely been a woman who was beautiful with a husband who loved her, and who had co-wives, but they did not provoke her much." I said: "Glory be to Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?" She said: "Yes." She said:
I spent that night until morning, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep. Then I woke up weeping. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usama ibn Zayd when revelation was delayed, and consulted them about separating from his family.
As for Usama, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and of the affection he held for them in his heart, saying: "O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good." As for 'Ali, he said: "Allah has not constrained you, and there are many women besides her. If you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barira and said: "O Barira, have you seen anything that makes you doubt concerning the affair of 'A'isha?" Barira said to him: "By He who sent you with the truth, if I have seen anything in her that I would conceal, it is no more than that she is a young girl who sleeps over her family's dough, so a domestic animal comes and eats it."
She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and sought his excuse from 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said while on the pulpit:
"O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me concerning my family? By Allah, I know nothing about my family but good, and they have mentioned a man about whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my family's house except with me."
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood and said: "I excuse you, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; and if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, you have ordered us and we will do your command."
She said: Sa'd ibn 'Ubada, who was the chief of the Khazraj, and was a righteous man, but partisan zeal carried him away, said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: "You lie, by the life of Allah!" Sa'd said: "By Allah, we will kill him, for you are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites."
She said: The Aws and the Khazraj rose up until they were about to fight one another, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued to calm them until they were silent, and he was silent.
She said: I remained that day, my tears would not dry and I could not close my eyes in sleep, while my parents thought that weeping would split my liver.
She said: While they were both sitting with me, and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, and I permitted her, so she sat and wept with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, and sat. She said: He had not sat with me since what was said about me had been said to me, and he had remained for a month without revelation concerning my affair. She said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat, then said: "As to what follows, O 'A'isha, it has reached me that such and such is said about you. If you are innocent, Allah, glorified is He, will clear you. And if you have committed a sin, seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses his sin and then repents, Allah accepts his repentance."
She said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I did not feel a single drop. I said to my father: "Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf." He said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." I said to my mother: "Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf." She said: "By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So I said, and I was a young girl who did not recite much of the Qur'an: "Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this matter until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. So if I tell you that I am innocent, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will not believe me; and if I confess to you a sin, and Allah knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except that of the father of Yusuf, and I do not remember his name: 'So patience is most fitting; and Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe.'"
She said: Then I turned over and lay down on my bed, and I, by Allah, at that time knew that I was innocent, and that Allah, glorified is He, would clear me by my innocence. But, by Allah, I did not think that revelation would be sent down concerning my affair to be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my own estimation for Allah to speak about me with a matter to be recited. But I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream by which Allah would clear me.
She said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when Allah, glorified is He, sent down revelation upon His Prophet (ﷺ).
