He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by God, I would not have done it." He said: "Then ʿAʾishah, by God, is better than you. Glory be to God, this is a great slander." So God, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and the believing women not...﴾ the verses, i.e., as Abu Ayyub and his wife did and as they both said.

His saying: ﴿and say, "This is an obvious lie"﴾ means: a clear lie.

﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it? Since they did not bring the witnesses, those, in the sight of God, are the liars.﴾

﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into of the slander.﴾ "Plunged into" means: engaged in, from the slander.

﴿When you received it with your tongues⁠—taking it up and relating it from one another.﴾ Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿idh tatalaqqawnahu﴾ with two tas, [[From talaqqi (to receive).]] and ʿAʾishah read: ﴿talliqunahu﴾ with a kasrah on the lam and a light qaf, from the lie. Al-walq, al-alaq, al-alq and al-liq all mean lying. [[It is in Sahih al-Bukhari: 5/61.]]

Al-Khalil said: the root of walq is haste, and he recited:

"They came in troops from Syria, hastening" [[Fath al-Qadir: 4/13.]]

meaning, they hasten. It is said: "Walaqa fulan fi al-sayr," meaning he persisted in the journey and hastened in it. So the meaning of ʿAʾishah's reading is: "when you persist in your lie."

Muhammad ibn al-Sumayqaʿ read: ﴿idh tulqunahu﴾ from iltiqa' (casting), [[With a damma on the ta', sukun on the lam and damma on the qaf, from the tafsir of al-Qurtubi: 12/204.]] and its parallel and proof is His saying: ﴿And they cast to them the word﴾ [[Surat al-Nahl: 36.]] and so on.

﴿And you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of, and you think it is trivial, while it is, in the sight of God, great.﴾

﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say: "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ "Glory be to You" may carry the sense of exalting God above such things, or of wonder.

﴿God admonishes you never to return to the like of it, if you are believers.﴾ "He admonishes you" means He forbids you and warns you that you return; it was also said: "He admonishes you lest you return to its like."

﴿And God makes the signs clear to you, and God is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾ All-Knowing of the matter of ʿAʾishah and Safwan; All-Wise, who judged her innocent.

﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter.﴾ This refers to ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his hypocrite companions.

﴿And God knows, while you do not know.﴾ ﴿And were it not for the grace of God upon you and His mercy, and that God is Kind and Merciful⁠—﴾ here there is an implied sense: that He would have hastened His punishment upon you.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 21–26:

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Sayf al-Tamimi narrated to us, saying: Ghalib ibn Tamim al-Saʿdi narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Jamil narrated to us, from Musa ibn ʿUqba al-Madini, from Abu Ruh al-Kalbi, from Hurr ibn Nusayr al-Hadrami, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever strengthens the arm of a man among the people in a dispute about which he has no knowledge, he is under the shadow of the wrath of Allah, Glorified is He, until he withdraws. Whoever intercedes concerning a punishment among the punishments of Allah, Exalted is He, so that it is not enforced, has truly opposed Allah and sought His wrath, and upon him is the curse of Allah, continuing until the Day of Resurrection. Whoever spreads a word about a Muslim man, while he is innocent of it, wishing to disgrace him with it in this world, it is truly incumbent upon Allah to melt him in the Fire." ﴿وَلَا يَأْتَلِ﴾: "and let not swear." This is the reading of the majority. It is of the form (yaftaʿil) from al-ilyah (al-alliyya), which is an oath. Al-Akhfash said: "If you wish, you may take it from the Arabic saying: mā alawtu jahdi fī shaʾni fulān, meaning: I did not leave off my utmost effort concerning so-and-so." Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi, Abu Mikhlad al-Sadusi, Abu Jaʿfar and Zayd ibn Aslam read (wa-lā yatawalla), with the tā' placed before and the hamza placed after, and it is of the form (yaftaʿil) from al-alliya and al-alw.

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Dahhak said: Some of the Companions, among them Abu Bakr, swore that they would not give charity to a man who had spoken anything of the slander and that they would not benefit them, so Allah, Glorified is He, revealed this verse.

﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْغَافِلَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ لُعِنُوا فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ وَلَهُمْ عَذَابٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾: "The heedless" means those who are chaste and unaware of immoralities and of what they were accused of, like the heedlessness of ʿA'isha regarding what was in it. The scholars differed concerning the ruling of the verse. A group said: it is specifically about ʿA'isha and the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), to the exclusion of the rest of the believing women.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me, saying: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid al-Himmani narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from al-ʿAwwam ibn Hawshab, saying: A shaykh from Banu Kahil narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAbbas explained Surat al-Nur, and when he reached this verse, ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْغَافِلَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: "This is concerning ʿA'isha and the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically, and it is unspecified (mubhama), there is no repentance in it. Then he recited ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ up to His saying ﴿إِلَّا الَّذِينَ تَابُوا مِن بَعْدِ ذَٰلِكَ وَأَصْلَحُوا﴾, so He made repentance for these and did not make repentance for those. He said: A man intended to stand up and kiss his head because of the excellence of his explanation.

Others said: this verse was revealed concerning the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and it remained so until the verse at the beginning of the surah was revealed: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ يَرْمُونَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَأْتُوا بِأَرْبَعَةِ شُهَدَاءَ﴾ up to ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾, so Allah revealed flogging and repentance for it. Thus repentance is accepted, and testimony is rejected.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Hayyan narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ʿIsa narrated to us, saying: ʿAli ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said: We have been informed that it was revealed concerning the polytheists of Makka, when there was a covenant between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Whenever a woman went out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madina as an emigrant, the polytheists of Makka slandered her and said: "She only went out to commit adultery."

﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: the majority read it with the tā', while the people of Kufa, except ʿAsim, read it with the yā', because the verb precedes. ﴿أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ﴾: this was before their mouths were sealed. It was also said: the meaning is that the tongues of some of them testify against others. ﴿وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ in the world. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ﴾: their recompense and reckoning. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾: the majority read it with a fatha on the qaf, while Mujahid read ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ with a damma as an attribute of Allah and His affirmation, the reading of Abu [...]: "yuwaffihim Allah al-haqqa dinahum" (Allah will fully pay them their due in truth).

﴿وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ﴾: He makes clear to them the reality of what He had promised them in the world.

﴿الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَاتِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَالطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾, the verse. Most exegetes said: "The wicked words (al-khabithat min al-qawl) are for wicked people (lil-khabithin min al-nas), and wicked people are for wicked words; and good words are for good people, and good people are for good words."

Ibn Zayd said: "The wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men are for wicked women, and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women."

﴿أُولَٰئِكَ﴾: meaning ʿA'isha and Safwan. He referred to them with the plural form, like His saying ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 11], while the intended meaning is two brothers. ﴿مُبَرَّءُونَ﴾: exonerated (munazzahun) ﴿مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.

Abu Nasr al-Nuʿman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nuʿman al-Jurjani informed us with it, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karim al-Bahili informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sufyan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Walid al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jadʿan, from his grandmother, from ʿA'isha, that she said: "I have been given nine things that no woman has been given. Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with my image in his palm when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ordered to marry me. He married me as a virgin, and no one other than me was married as a virgin. He died while his head was in my lap. He was buried in my house. The angels surrounded my house. The revelation would descend upon him while he was with his family, and they would disperse from him. It would descend upon him while I was with him under his blanket. I am the daughter of his successor and his truthful companion (siddiq). My innocence descended from the heavens. I was created good, and I was [destined] for a good man. I was promised forgiveness and generous provision."

Abu Nasr al-Nuʿman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nuʿman al-Jurjani informed us with it, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karim al-Bahili informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sufyan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Walid al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jadʿan, from his grandmother, from ʿA'isha, that she said: "I have been given nine things that no woman has been given. It would descend upon him while I was with him under his blanket. I am the daughter of his successor and his truthful companion (siddiq). My innocence descended from the heavens. Ibn Muhays and Ya'qub read zakka with the doubling (tashdid), meaning purified (ṭahhara). Their proof is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ اللَّهَ يُزَكِّي مَن يَشَاءُ﴾, that is, He purifies whom He wills from sin and wrongdoing through mercy and forgiveness. ﴿وَاللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾.

Whoever intercedes concerning a punishment among the punishments of Allah, Exalted is He, so that it is not enforced, has truly opposed Allah and sought His wrath, and upon him is the curse of Allah, continuing until the Day of Resurrection. ﴿وَلَا يَأْتَلِ﴾: "and let not swear." This is the reading of the majority. It is of the form (yaftaʿil) from al-ilyah (al-alliyya), which is an oath. Al-Akhfash said: "If you wish, you may take it from the Arabic saying: mā alawtu jahdi fī shaʾni fulān, meaning: I did not leave off my utmost effort concerning so-and-so." Abu Raja' al-ʿUtaridi, Abu Mikhlad al-Sadusi, Abu Jaʿfar and Zayd ibn Aslam read (wa-lā yatawalla), with the tā' placed before and the hamza placed after, and it is of the form (yaftaʿil) from al-alliya and al-alw.

﴿وَلْيَعْفُوا وَلْيَصْفَحُوا﴾: concerning them, namely their immersion in the matter of ʿA'isha.

Most exegetes said: "The wicked words (al-khabithat min al-qawl) are for wicked people (lil-khabithin min al-nas), and wicked people are for wicked words; and good words are for good people, and good people are for good words."

Whenever a woman went out to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Madina as an emigrant, the polytheists of Makka slandered her and said: "She only went out to commit adultery."

﴿يَوْمَ تَشْهَدُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: the majority read it with the tā', while the people of Kufa, except ʿAsim, read it with the yā', because the verb precedes. ﴿أَلْسِنَتُهُمْ﴾: this was before their mouths were sealed. It was also said: the meaning is that the tongues of some of them testify against others. ﴿وَأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَرْجُلُهُم بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ in the world. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ يُوَفِّيهِمُ اللَّهُ دِينَهُمُ﴾: their recompense and reckoning. ﴿الْحَقَّ﴾: the majority read it with a fatha on the qaf, while Mujahid read ﴿الْحَقُّ﴾ with a damma as an attribute of Allah and His affirmation, the reading of Abu [...]: "yuwaffihim Allah al-haqqa dinahum" (Allah will fully pay them their due in truth).

﴿وَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمُبِينُ﴾: He makes clear to them the reality of what He had promised them in the world.

﴿الْخَبِيثَاتُ لِلْخَبِيثِينَ وَالْخَبِيثُونَ لِلْخَبِيثَاتِ وَالطَّيِّبَاتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَالطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّبَاتِ﴾, the verse. Most exegetes said: "The wicked words (al-khabithat min al-qawl) are for wicked people (lil-khabithin min al-nas), and wicked people are for wicked words; and good words are for good people, and good people are for good words."

Ibn Zayd said: "The wicked women are for wicked men, and wicked men are for wicked women, and good women are for good men, and good men are for good women."

﴿أُولَٰئِكَ﴾: meaning ʿA'isha and Safwan. He referred to them with the plural form, like His saying ﴿فَإِنْ كَانَ لَهُ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 11], while the intended meaning is two brothers. ﴿مُبَرَّءُونَ﴾: exonerated (munazzahun) ﴿مِمَّا يَقُولُونَ لَهُم مَّغْفِرَةٌ وَرِزْقٌ كَرِيمٌ﴾.

Abu Nasr al-Nuʿman ibn Muhammad ibn al-Nuʿman al-Jurjani informed us with it, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Karim al-Bahili informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sufyan al-Tirmidhi narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Walid al-Kindi narrated to us, saying: Abu Hafs narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Jadʿan, from his grandmother, from ʿA'isha, that she said: "I have been given nine things that no woman has been given. Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with my image in his palm when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was ordered to marry me. He married me as a virgin, and no one other than me was married as a virgin. He died while his head was in my lap. He was buried in my house. The angels surrounded my house. The revelation would descend upon him while he was with his family, and they would disperse from him. It would descend upon him while I was with him under his blanket. I am the daughter of his successor and his truthful companion (siddiq). My innocence descended from the heavens. I was created good, and I was [destined] for a good man. I was promised forgiveness and generous provision."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 27–31:

O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses… (the verse).

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Yahyawayh narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Thawr and Ibrahim ibn Abi Sufyan narrated to us, the two saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar from ʿAdi ibn Thabit, who said: A woman from the Ansar came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am in my house in a state in which I do not like anyone to see me, neither a father nor a son. Then the father comes in upon me, and a man of my family keeps entering upon me while I am in that state. So what should I do?" Then this verse was revealed: "O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your houses until you have sought permission and greeted their occupants…" (the verse).

Some exegetes said: "Until you seek permission (hatta tasta'nisu)" means "until you seek permission (tastaʾdhinu)."

Saʿid ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "It is only 'until you seek permission,' but the scribe made an error." Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Aʿmash used to recite it thus: "until you seek permission." In the verse there is a transposition: its meaning is "until you greet its occupants and seek permission," and likewise it is in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud, which is to say: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?"

Yunus ibn ʿUbayd narrated from ʿAmr ibn Saʿid al-Thaqafi that a man asked permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), saying: "Am I entering?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to a woman called Rawdah: "Stand up to this man and teach him, for he does not know how to seek permission properly. Tell him: say, 'Peace be upon you, may I enter?'" The man heard her and said it, and he said: "Enter."

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: it is clearing the throat and coughing.

Al-Aʿmash narrated from ʿAmr ibn Murrah from Yahya ibn al-Khazzaz from the nephew of Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas'ud, from Zaynab, who said: "ʿAbd Allah, when he came from some errand and reached the door, would clear his throat and spit, out of dislike that she might be caught in a matter he disliked."

ʿIkrimah: it is glorifying God (tasbih), magnifying God (takbir) and the like.

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Kharijah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: "We said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the 'seeking of permission' (al-istiʾnas) that God, glory be to Him, intends in 'until you seek permission and greet its occupants'?" He said: "A man says a takbir, a tasbih and a tahmid, clears his throat, and thereby makes the people of the house aware."

Al-Khalil said: al-istiʾnas means seeking clear sight, from His saying: "I perceived a fire" (Surah Taha: 10).

The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: al-istiʾnas means seeking companionship, which is to look whether there is anyone in the house who would let them know that he is entering upon them. The Arabs say: "Go and seek to find out (fastaʾnis) whether you see anyone in the house?" meaning: look whether you see anyone in it.

It is related that Abu Musa al-Ashʿari came to the house of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?"

ʿUmar said: "Once." Abu Musa said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" ʿUmar said: "Twice." Abu Musa said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" and he went away. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent someone after him to bring him back, and asked him about what he had done. He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Seeking permission is three times; if they permit you, enter, otherwise return.'"

ʿUmar said: "You must bring me proof, or I will punish you." Abu Musa set out and brought to him those who had heard that with him.

ʿAta' ibn Yasar narrated that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shall I seek permission to enter upon my mother?" He said: "Yes." He said: "She has no servant but me; should I seek permission every time I enter?" He said: "Would you like to see her naked?" The man said: "No." He said: "Then seek permission to enter upon her."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from his father from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever looks into a house without their permission, it is lawful for them to gouge out his eye."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shabbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying:

Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us from al-Zuhri that he heard Sahl ibn Saʿd say: "A man looked into one of the chambers of the Prophet's (ﷺ) chambers, and he had a comb with which he was scratching his head. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If I knew that you were looking, I would have stabbed you in your eyes with it. Seeking permission is only because of looking.'"

"And if you do not find anyone in them" — that is, in the houses — "who permits you to enter them, then do not enter them until you are given permission. And if you are told, 'Return,' then return. It is purer for you" — that is, returning is more pure and more upright for you — "and Allah is Knowing of what you do."

When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the inns and dwellings on the roads of Syria that have no inhabitant?" So Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: "There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited, wherein is enjoyment for you" — that is, benefit for you — without seeking permission.

They differed about what these houses are. Qatadah said: they are the inns and the houses built for travellers, so that they may take shelter in them and store their goods in them.

Mujahid said: they used to place saddles and goods in houses on the roads of Medina that had no one in them, and the roads at that time were safe, so it was permitted for them to enter them without permission.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah: they are the houses of Mecca. Al-Dahhak: the ruined house in which the traveller takes shelter in summer and winter. ʿAta': they are ruined houses, and the "enjoyment" is relieving oneself in them, from the toilet and urination. Ibn Zayd: the houses of merchants and their shops in the markets. Ibn Jarir: all houses that are without an inhabitant, in general, since seeking permission only came so that one would not fall upon what one does not like of nakedness; when that is not feared, there is no point in seeking permission.

"And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal."

"Say to the believing men that they should lower (yaghuddu) — restrain (yakuffu) — some of their gaze" — from looking at what is not permitted. They differed about His saying "min" (some of). Some said: it is an added particle, meaning "they should lower their gaze." Others said: it is established in meaning, because believers are not ordered to lower the gaze at all, but are only ordered to lower it from what is not permitted.

"And that they should guard their private parts" — from whoever is not lawful. This is the saying of most exegetes.

Ibn Zayd said: every mention of guarding the private parts in the Qur'an refers to fornication, except in this place, for here he intended concealment, meaning: "and that they should guard their private parts so that no one looks at them."

The evidence for this interpretation is the omission of "that is purer for them" (dhalika azka lahum) in the following: "Indeed Allah is Acquainted with what they do."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me in my house, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Rabiʿ al-Zahrani narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Abi ʿAmr narrated to us from al-Muttalib ibn HanTab from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Guarantee for me six things from yourselves, and I will guarantee Paradise for you: be truthful when you speak, fulfil when you promise, render what you are entrusted with, guard your private parts, lower your gaze, and restrain your hands."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shabbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: ʿAnbasah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us that he heard ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Looking at the beauty of a woman is one of the poisoned arrows of Iblis. Whoever turns away his gaze seeking the reward of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, Allah will replace it with an act of worship that will gladden him."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Salih al-Antaki narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Aban ibn Yazid narrated to us from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir from Abu Ja'far from Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "While a man was praying, a woman passed by him; he looked at her and followed her with his eyes, and his eyes were lost."

"And say to the believing women that they should lower some of their gaze" — from what is not permitted — "and guard their private parts" — from what is not lawful. It is also said: "and guard their private parts" means they should cover them so that no one sees them.

"And not to display their adornment" — and that they should not show to non-mahram men their adornment. The adornments are of two kinds: one is what is hidden, such as anklets, earrings, necklaces, bracelets and the like; and the other is "what appears of it." The scholars differed about the apparent adornment which Allah, glory be to Him, excepted and permitted. Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the garments; and also from him: the outer garment. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: "Take your adornment at every place of worship" (Surah al-A'raf: 31), meaning your garments.

Ibn ʿAbbas and his companions said: kohl, the ring, the bracelet and dyeing (with henna). al-Dahhak and al-Awza'i: the face and the two palms. al-Hasan: the face and the garments.

ʿAyesha related from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/229] that he said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day, when she has reached maturity (idha ʿarakat, i.e. menstruated), to show anything except her face and her hand up to here," and he gripped half of the forearm.

Allah, glory be to Him, and His Messenger only permitted a woman to display this amount of her body because it is not awrah; so it is permissible for her to uncover it in prayer, while the rest of her body is awrah and she is obliged to cover it.

"And let them draw their headcoverings (khumur) over their bosoms" — that is, their veils (maqani'), the plural of khimar, which is the covering of a woman's head — so that they cover with it their hair, their earrings and their necks.

ʿAyesha said: "May Allah have mercy on the early emigrant women: when Allah, glory be to Him, revealed this verse, they split their thick woollen cloaks and covered themselves with them."

"And not to display their adornment" — the hidden adornment which they were ordered to cover, and it was not permitted for them to uncover it in prayer or before non-mahram men; it is everything other than the face, the two palms, and the tops of the feet — "except to their husbands, or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters, or their women" — that is, the women of the believers, so it is not lawful for a Muslim woman to uncover herself before a polytheist woman, unless she is a slave of hers; this is His saying: "or what their right hands possess."

From Ibn Jurayj: Hisham ibn al-Ghar narrated from ʿUbadah ibn Nasi that he disliked that a Christian woman should kiss a Muslim woman or see her nakedness, and he interpreted "or their women" accordingly.

ʿUbadah said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah: "To proceed: it has reached me that women enter the bathhouses along with women of the People of the Book. Forbid that and prevent it."

He said: Then Abu ʿUbaydah stood up in that place, supplicating: "O Allah, whichever woman enters the bathhouse without illness or sickness, desiring whiteness for her face, blacken her face on the day when faces turn white."

Some said: by His saying "or what their right hands possess" He meant their male and female slaves, for there is no harm if they show them of their adornment what they show to their mahram relatives.

"Or the male attendants who have no desire (ghayri uli al-iraba) among men" — those who follow you in order to get some of your food, and have no need for women, and are not drawn to them.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the one whom women are not shy of. Also from him: the foolish impotent man.

Mujahid: the imbecile who knows nothing of women. al-Hasan: the one whose penis does not rise. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: the idiot. ʿIkrimah: the castrated. al-Hakam ibn Aban, from ʿIkrimah: the effeminate man whose penis does not stand.

Al-Zuhri narrated from ʿUrwah from ʿAyesha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "A certain effeminate man used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they counted him among those without desire. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered one day while he was with some of his wives, and he was describing a woman, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When she comes forward, she comes with four (folds); when she turns back, she turns back with eight.'

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I do not think this one knows what is here; do not let this one enter upon you.' So they veiled him from them."

Ibn Zayd: it is the one who follows the people until he seems to be one of them, and grew up among them, and has no desire for their women; he only follows them for their kindness to him. The word iriba and irb means need; one says: "I had need of such-and-such (arabtu ila kadha), I have need (arab), iraban," when one needs it.

The readers differed over His saying "ghayri" (other than). Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿAmir and ʿAsim, by the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read it in the accusative, and it has two aspects: first, that it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) and a qat', since "al-tabiʿin" is definite and "ghayr" is not indefinite; second, that it is an exception, with "ghayr" meaning "illa" (except). The rest read it in the genitive as an attribute of "al-tabiʿin".

"Or the children who have not attained knowledge of women's private nakedness" — that is, who have not uncovered the nakedness of women through intercourse with them, so that they would look upon it. The word "tifl" may be singular or plural.

"And let them not stamp their feet" — meaning, let them not move them when they walk — "so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known," meaning the anklet and the jewellery. "And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you" — from the shortcoming that occurs in obeying His command and prohibition. It is also said: its meaning is: return to obedience to Allah in what He has commanded and forbidden you of the etiquettes mentioned in this surah.

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Kharijah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Wasil ibn al-Sa'ib from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, who said: "We said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the 'seeking of permission' (al-istiʾnas) that God, glory be to Him, intends in 'until you seek permission and greet its occupants'?" He said: "A man says a takbir, a tasbih and a tahmid, clears his throat, and thereby makes the people of the house aware."

Al-Khalil said: al-istiʾnas means seeking clear sight, from His saying: "I perceived a fire" (Surah Taha: 10).

The people of meanings (ahl al-maʿani) said: al-istiʾnas means seeking companionship, which is to look whether there is anyone in the house who would let them know that he is entering upon them. The Arabs say: "Go and seek to find out (fastaʾnis) whether you see anyone in the house?" meaning: look whether you see anyone in it.

It is related that Abu Musa al-Ashʿari came to the house of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, and said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?"

ʿUmar said: "Once." Abu Musa said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" ʿUmar said: "Twice." Abu Musa said: "Peace be upon you, may I enter?" and he went away. ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, sent someone after him to bring him back, and asked him about what he had done. He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'Seeking permission is three times; if they permit you, enter, otherwise return.'"

ʿUmar said: "You must bring me proof, or I will punish you." Abu Musa set out and brought to him those who had heard that with him.

ʿAta' ibn Yasar narrated that a man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Shall I seek permission to enter upon my mother?" He said: "Yes." He said: "She has no servant but me; should I seek permission every time I enter?" He said: "Would you like to see her naked?" The man said: "No." He said: "Then seek permission to enter upon her."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid narrated to us from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from his father from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever looks into a house without their permission, it is lawful for them to gouge out his eye."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shabbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying:

Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us from al-Zuhri that he heard Sahl ibn Saʿd say: "A man looked into one of the chambers of the Prophet's (ﷺ) chambers, and he had a comb with which he was scratching his head. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'If I knew that you were looking, I would have stabbed you in your eyes with it. Seeking permission is only because of looking.'"

"And if you do not find anyone in them" — that is, in the houses — "who permits you to enter them, then do not enter them until you are given permission. And if you are told, 'Return,' then return. It is purer for you" — that is, returning is more pure and more upright for you — "and Allah is Knowing of what you do."

When this verse was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about the inns and dwellings on the roads of Syria that have no inhabitant?" So Allah, glory be to Him, revealed: "There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited, wherein is enjoyment for you" — that is, benefit for you — without seeking permission.

They differed about what these houses are. Qatadah said: they are the inns and the houses built for travellers, so that they may take shelter in them and store their goods in them.

Mujahid said: they used to place saddles and goods in houses on the roads of Medina that had no one in them, and the roads at that time were safe, so it was permitted for them to enter them without permission.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah: they are the houses of Mecca. Al-Dahhak: the ruined house in which the traveller takes shelter in summer and winter. ʿAta': they are ruined houses, and the "enjoyment" is relieving oneself in them, from the toilet and urination. Ibn Jarir: all houses that are without an inhabitant, in general, since seeking permission only came so that one would not fall upon what one does not like of nakedness; when that is not feared, there is no point in seeking permission.

"And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal."

"Say to the believing men that they should lower (yaghuddu) — restrain (yakuffu) — some of their gaze" — from looking at what is not permitted. They differed about His saying "min" (some of). Some said: it is an added particle, meaning "they should lower their gaze." Others said: it is established in meaning, because believers are not ordered to lower the gaze at all, but are only ordered to lower it from what is not permitted.

"And that they should guard their private parts" — from whoever is not lawful. This is the saying of most exegetes.

Ibn Zayd said: every mention of guarding the private parts in the Qur'an refers to fornication, except in this place, for here he intended concealment, meaning: "and that they should guard their private parts so that no one looks at them."

The evidence for this interpretation is the omission of "that is purer for them" (dhalika azka lahum) in the following: "Indeed Allah is Acquainted with what they do."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shabbah narrated to us, saying: al-Hadrami narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: ʿAnbasah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us that he heard ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Looking at the beauty of a woman is one of the poisoned arrows of Iblis. "And not to display their adornment" — and that they should not show to non-mahram men their adornment. The adornments are of two kinds: one is what is hidden, such as anklets, earrings, necklaces, bracelets and the like; and the other is "what appears of it." The scholars differed about the apparent adornment which Allah, glory be to Him, excepted and permitted. Ibn Mas'ud said: it is the garments; and also from him: the outer garment. The evidence for this interpretation is His saying: "Take your adornment at every place of worship" (Surah al-A'raf: 31), meaning your garments.

Ibn ʿAbbas and his companions said: kohl, the ring, the bracelet and dyeing (with henna). al-Dahhak and al-Awza'i: the face and the two palms. al-Hasan: the face and the garments.

ʿAyesha related from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/229] that he said: "It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day, when she has reached maturity (idha ʿarakat, i.e. menstruated), to show anything except her face and her hand up to here," and he gripped half of the forearm.

Allah, glory be to Him, and His Messenger only permitted a woman to display this amount of her body because it is not awrah; so it is permissible for her to uncover it in prayer, while the rest of her body is awrah and she is obliged to cover it.

"And let them draw their headcoverings (khumur) over their bosoms" — that is, their veils (maqani'), the plural of khimar, which is the covering of a woman's head — so that they cover with it their hair, their earrings and their necks.

ʿAyesha said: "May Allah have mercy on the early emigrant women: when Allah, glory be to Him, revealed this verse, they split their thick woollen cloaks and covered themselves with them."

"And not to display their adornment" — the hidden adornment which they were ordered to cover, and it was not permitted for them to uncover it in prayer or before non-mahram men; it is everything other than the face, the two palms, and the tops of the feet — "except to their husbands, or their fathers, or the fathers of their husbands, or their sons, or the sons of their husbands, or their brothers, or the sons of their brothers, or the sons of their sisters, or their women" — that is, the women of the believers, so it is not lawful for a Muslim woman to uncover herself before a polytheist woman, unless she is a slave of hers; this is His saying: "or what their right hands possess."

From Ibn Jurayj: Hisham ibn al-Ghar narrated from ʿUbadah ibn Nasi that he disliked that a Christian woman should kiss a Muslim woman or see her nakedness, and he interpreted "or their women" accordingly.

ʿUbadah said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abu ʿUbaydah ibn al-Jarrah: "To proceed: it has reached me that women enter the bathhouses along with women of the People of the Book. Forbid that and prevent it."

He said: Then Abu ʿUbaydah stood up in that place, supplicating: "O Allah, whichever woman enters the bathhouse without illness or sickness, desiring whiteness for her face, blacken her face on the day when faces turn white."

Some said: by His saying "or what their right hands possess" He meant their male and female slaves, for there is no harm if they show them of their adornment what they show to their mahram relatives.

"Or the male attendants who have no desire (ghayri uli al-iraba) among men" — those who follow you in order to get some of your food, and have no need for women, and are not drawn to them.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it is the one whom women are not shy of. Also from him: the foolish impotent man.

Mujahid: the imbecile who knows nothing of women. al-Hasan: the one whose penis does not rise. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: the idiot. ʿIkrimah: the castrated. al-Hakam ibn Aban, from ʿIkrimah: the effeminate man whose penis does not stand.

Al-Zuhri narrated from ʿUrwah from ʿAyesha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "A certain effeminate man used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ), and they counted him among those without desire. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered one day while he was with some of his wives, and he was describing a woman, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When she comes forward, she comes with four (folds); when she turns back, she turns back with eight.'

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I do not think this one knows what is here; do not let this one enter upon you.' So they veiled him from them."

Ibn Zayd: it is the one who follows the people until he seems to be one of them, and grew up among them, and has no desire for their women; he only follows them for their kindness to him. The word iriba and irb means need; one says: "I had need of such-and-such (arabtu ila kadha), I have need (arab), iraban," when one needs it.

The readers differed over His saying "ghayri" (other than). Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿAmir and ʿAsim, by the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read it in the accusative, and it has two aspects: first, that it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) and a qat', since "al-tabiʿin" is definite and "ghayr" is not indefinite; second, that it is an exception, with "ghayr" meaning "illa" (except). The rest read it in the genitive as an attribute of "al-tabiʿin".

"Or the children who have not attained knowledge of women's private nakedness" — that is, who have not uncovered the nakedness of women through intercourse with them, so that they would look upon it. The word "tifl" may be singular or plural.

"And let them not stamp their feet" — meaning, let them not move them when they walk — "so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known," meaning the anklet and the jewellery. "And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you" — from the shortcoming that occurs in obeying His command and prohibition. It is also said: its meaning is: return to obedience to Allah in what He has commanded and forbidden you of the etiquettes mentioned in this surah.

Then the Prophet (ﷺ) entered one day while he was with some of his wives, and he was describing a woman, so the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'When she comes forward, she comes with four (folds); when she turns back, she turns back with eight.'

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'I do not think this one knows what is here; do not let this one enter upon you.' So they veiled him from them."

Ibn Zayd: it is the one who follows the people until he seems to be one of them, and grew up among them, and has no desire for their women; he only follows them for their kindness to him. The word iriba and irb means need; one says: "I had need of such-and-such (arabtu ila kadha), I have need (arab), iraban," when one needs it.

The readers differed over His saying "ghayri" (other than). Abu Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿAmir and ʿAsim, by the transmission of Abu Bakr and al-Mufaddal, read it in the accusative, and it has two aspects: first, that it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) and a qat', since "al-tabiʿin" is definite and "ghayr" is not indefinite; second, that it is an exception, with "ghayr" meaning "illa" (except). The rest read it in the genitive as an attribute of "al-tabiʿin".

"Or the children who have not attained knowledge of women's private nakedness" — that is, who have not uncovered the nakedness of women through intercourse with them, so that they would look upon it. The word "tifl" may be singular or plural.

"And let them not stamp their feet" — meaning, let them not move them when they walk — "so that what they conceal of their adornment may be known," meaning the anklet and the jewellery. "And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you" — from the shortcoming that occurs in obeying His command and prohibition. It is also said: its meaning is: return to obedience to Allah in what He has commanded and forbidden you of the etiquettes mentioned in this surah.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O believers, perhaps you will prosper.﴾ ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾, i.e., marry off, O believers, those among your free men and women who have no spouse, ﴿and the righteous among your male servants and female servants﴾. Al-Hasan recited "min ʿabīdikum" (from your male slaves).

Al-ʾAyāmā (the unmarried) is the plural of al-ʾAyyim, which refers to a man or woman who has no spouse. It is said: a man is ʾayyim, and a woman is ʾayyim or ʾayyimah. The verb from it is "āmat al-marʾah" (the woman became a widow), "taʾayyamat" (she remained unmarried after being married), and "taʾayyuman" (she became a widow or divorcee). The poet said:

*Have you not seen that God has made His religion prevail,*
*and Saʿd at the gate of al-Qadisiyyah is firm?*
*So we returned, and many women had become widows,*
*and the women of Saʿd were not among the widows.*
[[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Ibn Kathir, 8/83, with variation in the text.]]

Another poet said:

*If you marry, I will marry; and if you remain unmarried, I too will remain unmarried,*
*though I am more eager than you to remain unmarried.*
[[Jami al-Bayan, al-Tabari, 18/167.]]

Some jurists interpreted the verse as obligatory and binding, so they made marriage obligatory upon whoever is able to marry. The rest interpreted it as recommended (mandub) and desirable (mustahabb). This is the sound, well-known view, and it is the view of the majority.

Al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It is obligatory for a man and a woman to marry when their souls long for it, because Allah, exalted is His praise and sanctified are His names, commanded it, approved of it, and recommended it.

It has reached us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Marry, so that you may increase in number, for I will boast of you before the nations, even on account of the miscarried fetus."
[[Al-Musannaf, 6/173. Without the phrase "even on account of the miscarried fetus."]] [32]

He (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever loves my natural way (fitrah), let him follow my sunnah, and it is marriage."
[[Musnad Abi Yaʿla, 5/133.]]

He also said: "A man is elevated in rank by the supplication of his child after him."
[[Al-Musannaf, 3/361, by Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Sukuni, transmitted from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.]] [33]

Al-Shafiʿi said: "And whoever does not feel an inclination toward it, it is more beloved to me that he devote himself to the worship of Allah, mighty and majestic."
[[Kitab al-Umm, 5/155. This is not a hadith.]] [34]

Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the women who sit at home (al-qawaʿid min al-nisaʾ) and mentioned a servant whom He honored, saying, ﴿and a master and a chaste one (ḥaṣūran)﴾. Al-ḥaṣūr is one who does not approach women. Allah did not encourage them to marry, which shows that what is recommended is for the one who needs it.
[[Mukhtasar al-Muzani, 163. He transmitted it in full from Imam al-Shafiʿi.]]

*Chapter mentioning some of the reports that encourage marriage*

Ahmad ibn Abi (chain) related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ishaq al-Jurjani related to us: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari related to us: Ashʿath related to us, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade tabattul (celibacy).
[[Musnad Ahmad, 5/17.]]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Hadithi related to me: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan al-Sufi related to us: Muhammad ibn Salih ibn Dharih related to us: Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallis related to us: Jundal related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Abu al-Mughallis, from Abu Najih al-Sulami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has the means to marry and does not marry is not one of us."
[[Tafsir Jawami al-Jami, al-Tabrisi, 2/618. Quoted from al-Kashshaf, 3/234.]] [35]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to me: Makhlad ibn Jaʿfar al-Baqirhi related to us: Ahmad ibn Yaʿqub al-Maqri, the nephew of ʿAwf, related to us: Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallis related to us: Mundal related to us, from Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has a child who reaches maturity, and he has the means to marry him off but does not marry him off, and he commits sin (ahdatha), then the sin is shared between them."
[[Tafsir Majmaʿ al-Bayan, 7/245.]] [36]

Al-Husayn related to me: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Daqqaq related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us: Abu Yusuf al-Saydalani related to us: Khalid ibn Ismaʿil related to us, from ʿUbayd Allah, from Salih, the client of al-Tawmah, who said: Abu Hurayrah said: "Even if nothing remained of the world except one day, I would meet Allah with a wife. I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The worst of you are your bachelors.'"
[[Musnad Abi Yaʿla, 4/38.]] [37]

With its chain from Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you marries, his devil cries out, 'Woe to him! The son of Adam has protected two-thirds of his religion from me.'"
[[Kanz al-ʿUmmal, 16/278.]] [38]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to me: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us: Abu Zakariyya Yahya ibn ʿAli ibn Khalaf al-Qattan related to us: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to us: Muhammad ibn Rabiʿah al-Kilabi related to us: Muhammad ibn Thabit al-ʿAqili related to us, from Harun ibn Ruʾab, from Abu Najih al-Sulami, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Poor, poor is the man who has no wife, and poor is the woman who has no husband."
They said: "O Messenger of Allah, even if she is wealthy in money?"
He said: "Even if she is wealthy in money."
[[Al-Durr al-Manthur, 2/311, with variation.]] [39]

Al-Husayn related to me: al-Fadl ibn al-Fadl al-Kindi related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Musa related to us: Hisham ibn ʿAmmar related to us: Hammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us: Khalid ibn al-Zabarqan related to us, from Sulayman ibn Habib, from Abu Umamah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Four groups Allah has cursed from above His Throne, and His angels say Amen to it: the one who restrains himself from women so that he neither marries nor takes a concubine, lest he have a child; the man who imitates women, though Allah created him male; the woman who imitates men, though Allah created her female; and the one who misleads the poor."
[[Musnad al-Shamiyyin, al-Tabarani, 2/412.]] [40]

Khalid said: That is, the one who mocks them. He says to the poor man, "Come, I will give you," and when he comes he says, "I have nothing with me." He tells the blind man, "Beware of the animal," when there is nothing in front of him. And he asks a man about the people's house, misdirecting him.

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh related to me: Abu Hudhayfah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Salam al-Bayruti related to us: Ahmad ibn Saʿid ibn Yaʿqub related to me: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid related to us: Muʿawiyah ibn Yahya related to me, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Makhul, from ʿAfif ibn al-Harith, from ʿAtiyyah ibn Bishr al-Mazini, who said: ʿAkkaf ibn Wadaʿah al-Hilali came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he said: "O ʿAkkaf, do you have a wife?" He said: "No, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Or a slave girl?" He said: "No." He said: "And you are healthy and well-off?" He said: "Yes, and praise be to Allah."

He said: "Then you are among the brothers of the devils. Either you are one of the monks of the Christians, or you are a believer. So do as we do, for among our sunnah is marriage. The worst of you are your bachelors, and the lowest of your dead are your bachelors. The devil has no weapon against a man more effective than women. Indeed, those who are married are the purified and the cleared of indecency. Woe to you, O ʿAkkaf! Verily, they are the companions of David, the companions of Job, the companions of Joseph, peace be upon them, and the companions of Kursuf."

They said: "O Messenger of Allah, who is Kursuf?"
He said: "A man who worshipped Allah, exalted is He, on the shore of one of the seas for thirty years, fasting by day and standing in prayer by night, never slackening in fasting or standing in prayer. Then he disbelieved in the Mighty Allah because of a woman he loved, and he abandoned what he had been doing in worshipping his Lord, mighty and majestic. Then Allah, glorified is He, overtook him for what had passed from him. Woe to you, O ʿAkkaf! Marry, for you are among the sinners."

He said: "Marry me to whomever you wish before I depart."

He said: "Then I have married you, in the name of Allah, to Karimah, the daughter of Kulthum al-Himyari."
[[Musnad Abi Yaʿla, 12/262.]] [41]

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me: Muhammad ibn al-Muzaffar al-Bazzaz related to us: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Nuʿman related to us in Egypt: ʿAli ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Mughirah related to us: Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, related to us: Abu Yahya [[In the second manuscript: in Egypt, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from ʿAlqamah.]] ibn Qays, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When a hundred and eighty years pass over my community, then celibacy, seclusion, and monasticism upon the mountaintops become permissible."
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi, 10/361, with variation.]] [42]

*Section on the kind of women who are recommended and preferred*

Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Thaqafi related to me, by my reading to him in my house: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn al-Jaʿd related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar al-Qawariri related to us: ʿUmar ibn al-Walid related to us: I heard Muʿawiyah ibn Yahya narrate from Yazid ibn Jabir, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from ʿIyad ibn Ghanm al-Ashʿari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "O ʿIyad, do not marry an old woman or a barren one, for I will boast of my numbers."
[[Kanz al-ʿUmmal, 16/296, with the addition: "...with you, the deaf."]] [43]

Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad related to me: Burhan ibn ʿAli al-Sufi related to us: Abu Bakr Mardak ibn Ahmad al-Bardhaʿi related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us: Ishaq ibn Bishr al-Kahili related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Idris al-Madani related to me, from Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry virgins, for their mouths are sweeter, their wombs more fruitful, and their affection more lasting."
[[Al-Musannaf, al-Sanʿani, 6/160, with variation: Ibn Jurayj said, and ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab said:.]] [44]

With its chain, he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When one of you wishes to marry a woman, let him ask about her hair just as he asks about her face, for hair is one of the two beauties."
[[Al-Mawdʿat, Ibn al-Jawzi, 2/262, and Kanz al-ʿUmmal, 16/291.]] [45]

With it he also said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry the blue-eyed women, for in them is gentleness."
[[Kanz al-ʿUmmal, 16/302.]] [46]

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to me: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb related to us: ʿAbdan ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Karimah related to us: Hisham ibn ʿUrwah related to us, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The greatest of the women of my community in blessing are those with the most beautiful faces and the lowest dowry."
[[Musnad al-Shihab, Ibn Salamah, 2/183.]] [47]

*Section on the etiquette related to marriage and the wedding procession*

Abu ʿAmr al-Furati related to us: Abu Musa related to us: Abu ʿAli al-Shaybani related to us: Muhammad ibn Rafiʿ related to us: Yazid ibn Harun related to us: ʿIsa ibn Maymun related to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Announce the marriage, hold it in the mosques, and beat the tambourines for it, and let one of you hold a wedding feast even if only with a sheep."
[[Kanz al-ʿUmmal, 16/292.]] [48]

Abu ʿAbd Allah ibn Fanjawayh related to us: Ahmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Hamdan and ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf both said: Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Kirkan al-Qurmasini related to us: Abu al-Zanbaʿ Rawh ibn al-Faraj related to us: Abu Salamah al-Basri al-ʿAtaki, al-Qasim ibn ʿUmar, related to us: Bishr ibn Ibrahim al-Ansari related to us, from al-Awzaʿi, from Makhul, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: Muʿadh ibn Jabal related to me, saying: "I witnessed the wedding of a man from the Ansar with the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon, and the Ansari was married. Then he said: 'On harmony, goodness, and auspicious omen, beat the tambourines over the head of your companion.' The baskets came, containing fruit and sugar, and the people rushed to snatch them, but they then held back and did not snatch. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'How beautiful is forbearance; will you not snatch?' They said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you forbade us from snatching on such-and-such a day.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'I only forbade you from snatching from the army's provisions, and I did not forbid you from snatching from wedding feasts.' Then he said: 'Indeed, snatch!'"
[[Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid, al-Haythami, 4/290.]] [49]

Muʿadh ibn Jabal said: By Allah, I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) dragging us and we dragging him in that snatching.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad related to me: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Ahmad ibn Malik related to us: Abu al-ʿAbbas ʿAbd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hashish al-Baghdadi related to us: ʿUthman ibn Maʿbad related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ibrahim [[In the second manuscript: Abu al-ʿAbbas ʿAbd Allah ibn Ibrahim.]] related to us, from Sufyan ibn ʿAmir al-ʿAmiri, from Safiyyah, their client woman, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give the marriage announcement with the tambourines, for it is more excellent in blessing and greater in abundance."
[[See al-Mughni, Ibn Qudamah, 7/435.]] [50]

Al-Husayn related to me: Tafran ibn al-Husayn related to us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Dawud al-Sijistani related to us: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Salim al-Azdi al-Sulami related to us: Hafs ibn ʿAbd Allah related to us, from Ibrahim ibn Tahman, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Ishaq ibn Sahl ibn Abi Hantamah, from his father, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "A young slave girl of the Ansar was with me in my care, and I married her off. The Prophet (ﷺ) entered and heard no singing, so he said: 'O ʿAʾishah, will you not sing for her? For this tribe of the Ansar love singing.'"
[[Sahih Ibn Hibban, 13/185.]] [51]

Al-Husayn related to me: ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf related to us: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Zuhayr ibn Thumamah al-Bazzar related to us: Abu Musa ibn al-Muthanna al-Zammar related to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, from Layth, from ʿAta, that the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by a bride, and he said: "If only there were entertainment with this."
[[Al-Musannaf, al-Kufi, 3/321.]] [52]

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me: Ibn Abi related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Salim al-Hamadhani related to us: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Razi al-Hasankhani related to us: Saʿid ibn Mansur related to us: Miskin ibn Maymun related to us: ʿUrwah ibn Ruwaym related to me, who said: "While ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Qurt was dozing in Homs, a bride passed by with fires lit, so he struck them with a stick and they dispersed from her. When morning came, he sat on his pulpit and said: 'Abu Jandalah married, and he made large bowls of food. May Allah have mercy on Abu Jandalah and bless his forefathers. May Allah curse the companions of your bride who lit the fires and imitated the people of polytheism, and Allah will extinguish their light on the Day of Resurrection.'" ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty; and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me: ʿAli ibn Ahmad ibn Nasrawayh related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Wahb related to us: Abu Zurʿah related to me: Ibrahim ibn Musa al-Farra related to us: Muslim ibn Khalid related to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Seek provision through marriage."
[[Al-Durr al-Manthur, 5/45.]] [53]

Ibn Fanjawayh related to me: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Bishr related to us: Abu Yusuf Muhammad ibn Sufyan ibn Musa al-Saffar [[In the second manuscript: Abu Yusuf ibn Sufyan ibn Musa.]] in al-Maṣṣiṣah related to us: Abu ʿAbd Allah Ahmad ibn Nasih related to us: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-Darawardi related to us, from Ibn ʿAjlan, that a man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and complained to him of need, and he said: "Then you should resort to al-bāʾah (marriage)."
[[Fayd al-Qadir Sharh al-Jami al-Saghir, al-Manawi, 3/318.]] A man complained of need to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, after the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: "You should resort to al-bāʾah." [54] A man came to ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, after Abu Bakr, and complained of need to him, and he said: "You should resort to al-bāʾah." Each of them meant the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty.﴾ Ibn ʿAjlan said: Abu Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "Seek wealth through marriage."

﴿And let those who cannot find marriage keep themselves chaste﴾ from unlawful sexual relations, ﴿until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾, and widens His provision for them.

﴿And those who seek a deed of manumission (al-kitab)﴾, i.e., al-mukatabah (the contract of manumission). It is that a man says to his slave or slave girl: "I have made a mukatabah with you, on condition that you give me such-and-such in fixed installments, and when you pay that, you will be free." If the slave accepts this, and then pays the mukatabah money by the installments he named, he becomes free. If he is unable to pay, his master may return him to slavery, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The mukatabah is a slave as long as one dirham remains owed to him."
[[Al-Musannaf, al-Kufi, 5/66.]] [55] The root of the word is from kataba, which means gathering and joining, and from it come kataybah (a military unit), kutub al-baghl (the saddle-like seams of a mule's saddle), and kitab (writing). The mukatib was so named because he gathers the installments of the mukatabah money, joining some with others.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 2 of 2):

﴿...from among those whom your right hands possess, write a contract with them﴾ (fa-kātibūhum, the contract of manumission known as *mukatabah*, by which a slave purchases his freedom in installments). The jurists differed over the ruling of this verse. One group said: it is a binding command and an obligation upon a man to grant a contract of manumission to his slave whom he knows to be good, when the slave asks for it at its value or more. If the slave asks for less than its value, the master is not obliged. This is the view of ʿAmr ibn Dinar and ʿAtaʾ, and Dawud ibn ʿAli and Muhammad ibn Jarir among the jurists adopted it. It is also a report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas. Those who supported this position cited the report of Qatada that Sirin asked Anas ibn Malik to grant him a contract, and he delayed. So he complained to ʿUmar, who struck him with a whip (durrah) and ordered him to grant the contract. They also argued that this verse was revealed concerning a slave of Huwaytib ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzza called Subh, who asked his master for a contract, and he refused. So God revealed this verse, and Huwaytib granted him a contract for one hundred dinars and remitted twenty of them to him. He paid it off and was killed on the day of Hunayn in battle.

It is also narrated from ʿUmar that he said: "It is one of the resolute commands of God: whoever asks for a contract, let him be granted one."

Others said: it is a recommendation and an encouragement, and the master is not obliged to grant his slave a contract, whether the slave offers its value, more than it, or less. This is the view of al-Shaʿbi and al-Hasan al-Basri, and al-Shafiʿi, Malik, Abu Hanifa and all the other jurists adopted it.

As for His words ﴿if you know any good in them﴾, they differed over it. Ibn ʿUmar, Ibn Zayd and Malik ibn Anas said: it means strength for earning a livelihood and gaining, so that they can pay what they agreed to pay. Al-Thawri also held this view.

Al-Walibi narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "If you know that they have a means of earning and do not place their upkeep upon the Muslims."

Al-Hasan, Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: it means wealth. This is also a report of al-ʿAwfi from Ibn ʿAbbas, and they based this on His words ﴿if he leaves any good﴾ (Qur'an 2:180). Al-Khalil said: "If He had meant wealth, He would have said: if you know good in them."

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed me: Harun ibn Muhammad related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us: Yahya al-Hammani related to us: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us from al-Aʿmash, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Layla al-Kindi, from Salman, who said: a slave said to him, "Grant me a contract." He said, "Do you have property?" He said, "No." He said, "You would feed me the filth of people," and he refused him.

Ibrahim, ʿUbayda, Abu Salih and Ibn Zayd said: it means truthfulness, fidelity and trustworthiness. Tawus and ʿAmr ibn Dinar said: it means wealth and trustworthiness.

Al-Shafiʿi said: the most apparent meaning of "good" in this verse is earning together with trustworthiness, so I prefer that he should not refuse to grant a contract to one who is like this.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shanba related to us (in the second copy: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba): Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz al-ʿUthmani and Abu al-Nadr Ishaq ibn Ibrahim related to us: Yahya ibn Hamza related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAjlan informed me, from Saʿid ibn Abi Saʿid al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, who said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Three are a right upon God to help them: a man who goes out in the way of God; a man who marries seeking to be free from what God has forbidden; and a man who grants a contract of manumission, seeking to pay it off." [Al-Musannaf: 5/259, al-Sanʿani, with variations.] [56]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me: Harun ibn Muhammad ibn Harun related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz related to us: Yahya al-Hammani related to us: Hammad ibn Zayd related to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from ʿUbayda, concerning His words ﴿if you know any good in them﴾, that he said: "If they establish the prayer."

It was also said: the mukatib must be an adult of sound mind. As for an insane person or a child, their contract is not valid, because they are not people capable of seeking (such a contract). Also, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The pen is lifted from three..." (the hadith). [57] [Musnad Ahmad: 6/100.]

Abu Hanifa said: the contract of a child is valid if he is an adolescent with discernment, on the basis of his own principle: if he is an intelligent adolescent and free, and his guardian permits him to transact, his transaction is valid. Likewise, the master with his slave: if he grants him a contract, he has permitted him to transact, so his contract is valid.

The jurists differed concerning the payment due under the contract. Malik, Abu Hanifa and his companions said: the contract is valid whether the payment is immediate or deferred, because God said ﴿write a contract with them, if you know any good in them﴾ and did not stipulate a term for it. Also, it is a contract on a specific item, so it is valid immediate or deferred, like a sale.

Al-Shafiʿi said: the contract is not valid if the payment is immediate; it is only valid if it is deferred, and its minimum is two installments.

﴿And give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾. They differed over it. Some said: the address is to the masters, and it means that he should remit something from the payment of the contract. Then they differed over that thing. One group said: it is a quarter of the amount, and this is the view of ʿAli, and al-Thawri adopted it.

Shuʿba narrated from ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami, that he granted a contract to a slave of his for twelve hundred and remitted a quarter, and had me witness it. Then he said to me: "Your friend used to do this," meaning ʿAli, may God honor his face. This has also been narrated as a hadith traced to the Prophet.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Hanash al-Maqri related to us: Abu ʿAbd Allah Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Musa related to us: Yusuf ibn Saʿid ibn Muslim related to us: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Habib (i.e., Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami), from ʿAli, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His words ﴿and give them of the wealth of God which He has given you﴾, that he said: "A quarter of the contract." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra, al-Bayhaqi: 10/329.] [58]

Others said: there is no fixed limit to it; it is left to the master, who may remit something from the payment of the contract. Asbat narrated from al-Suddi, from his father, who said: Zaynab bint Qays ibn Makhrama granted me a contract for ten thousand, and she had prayed towards both qiblahs with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and she remitted a thousand to me. Al-Jurayri narrated from Abu Nadra, from Abu Saʿid, client of Ibn Usayd, who said: Abu Usayd granted me a contract for twelve hundred, so I brought it to him, and he took a thousand from it and returned two hundred to me.

Nafiʿ said: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar granted a contract to a slave of his called Sharqi for thirty-five thousand dirhams, and he remitted five thousand dirhams from the final installment.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: when Ibn ʿUmar granted a contract to his mukatab, he did not remit anything from the first installments, for fear that he would fail and his charity would return to him. But when he reached the final part of his contract, he remitted what he wished. According to this view, His words ﴿and give them﴾ are a command of recommendation.

Others said: its meaning is: give them their share which God has appointed for them from the obligatory charities, by His words ﴿and for the slaves﴾ (Qur'an 9:60). This is the view of al-Hasan, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son. According to this interpretation, it is a command of obligation.

Barida and Ibrahim said: it is an exhortation to all people to help them.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shanba related to us (in the second copy: ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba): Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Faryabi related to us: Safwan ibn Salih related to us: al-Walid related to us: Zuhayr informed me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAqil, from Abu Umama ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever helps a mukatab in his bondage, or a warrior in his hardship, or a fighter in the way of God, God will shade him under the shade of His Throne on a day when there is no shade but His shade." [Ahkam al-Qur'an, al-Jassas: 3/162.] [59]

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Musa ibn Muhammad ibn ʿAli related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿUthman ibn Abi Shayba related to us: ʿAli ibn Ahmad al-Wasiti related to us: Ishaq ibn Mansur related to us, from ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Harb, from Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Dallani, from Kharija ibn Hilal, from Abu Saʿid, Rafiʿ ibn Khadij and Ibn ʿUmar, who said: a slave of ʿUthman, may God be pleased with him, called Kays came to us and said: "Go to the Commander of the Faithful and speak to him that he should grant me a contract." So we entered upon ʿUthman and said to him: "This slave of yours asked us that you grant him a contract." He said: "I have taken him for one hundred and fifty; let him bring it and he is free." He said: "So we went out, and each of us helped him with something." [In the second copy an addition: "He went and it was not long before he came, and said: 'Come with me.' So we came with him and entered..."] He said: "Wait at the door." Then he said: "O Kays, do you remember the day I twisted your ear?" I said: "Yes, my master." He said: "Did I not forbid you from saying 'my master'?" He said: "He kept at me until I remembered." He said: "Get up and take my ear." He said: "I refused, but he kept at me until I got up, took his ear and twisted it, while he said: 'Pull harder, pull harder,' until when he saw that I had reached what I had reached with him, he said: 'Enough.' Then he said: 'How sweet is the reward in this world! Go out, you are free, and what you have is yours.'"

﴿And do not compel your slave-girls to prostitution...﴾ (the verse).

It was revealed concerning Muʿadha and Musayka, the two slave-girls of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, the hypocrite. He used to compel them to fornication in exchange for a fee he took from them, and this is what they used to do in the Jahiliyya: they would hire out their female slaves. When Islam came, Muʿadha said to Musayka: "This matter we are in cannot be free of two aspects. If it is good, we have had our fill of it; and if it is evil, it is time for us to abandon it." So God revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning six slave-girls of ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy, whom he compelled to fornication and took their earnings. They were Muʿadha, Musayka, Umayma, Amra, Arwa and Qutayla. One day one of them came to him with a dinar, and another came with a cloak. He said to them: "Go back and commit fornication." They said: "By God, we will not do it; God has brought us Islam and forbidden fornication." So they went to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and complained to him, and God revealed this verse.

Ma'mar narrated from al-Zuhri that ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy took a man of Quraysh prisoner at Badr. ʿAbd Allah had a slave-girl called Muʿadha, and the Qurayshi prisoner wanted her for himself, but she was Muslim and refused him. Ibn Ubayy compelled her to this and beat her, hoping she would conceive for the Qurayshi, so that he would ask for a ransom for his child. So God revealed: ﴿and do not compel your slave-girls (fatayatikum, i.e., your female slaves) to prostitution (al-bighaʾ)﴾, meaning fornication.

﴿If they desire chastity (in tahassuna)﴾: here "in" means "when" (idh), and it is not a conditional, because it is not permitted to compel them to fornication even if they do not desire chastity. A parallel is His words ﴿and give up what remains of usury, if you are believers﴾ (Qur'an 2:278), and His words ﴿and you will be the uppermost, if you are believers﴾ (Qur'an 3:139), meaning "when." And His words ﴿you will surely enter the Sacred Mosque, if God wills, secure﴾ (Qur'an 48:27) mean "when God wills." Tahassun means abstaining from unlawful intercourse (al-taʿaffuf).

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: there is a transposition in the verse, and its sense is: (And marry off the single ones among you, if they desire chastity). Then He said: (And do not compel your slave-girls to prostitution, so that you may seek the goods of the worldly life). And whoever compels them, after the prohibition has come, ﴿then indeed God, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful to them﴾, and the sin falls upon the one who compels. When al-Hasan recited this verse, he said: "For them, by God, for them."

﴿And We have sent down to you clear signs, and an example of those who passed away before you, and an admonition for the God-fearing﴾ (the verse). [Example here means a report, a lesson, and a warning.]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 1 of 2):

﴿O believers, perhaps you will prosper.﴾ ﴿And marry off the unmarried among you﴾, i.e., marry off, O believers, those among your free men and women who have no spouse, ﴿and the righteous among your male servants and female servants﴾. Al-Hasan recited "min ʿabīdikum" (from your male slaves).

Al-ʾAyāmā (the unmarried) is the plural of al-ʾAyyim, which refers to a man or woman who has no spouse. It is said: a man is ʾayyim, and a woman is ʾayyim or ʾayyimah. The verb from it is "āmat al-marʾah" (the woman became a widow), "taʾayyamat" (she remained unmarried after being married), and "taʾayyuman" (she became a widow or divorcee). The poet said:

*Have you not seen that God has made His religion prevail,*
*and Saʿd at the gate of al-Qadisiyyah is firm?*
*So we returned, and many women had become widows,*
*and the women of Saʿd were not among the widows.*
[[Al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah, Ibn Kathir, 8/83, with variation in the text.]]

Another poet said:

*If you marry, I will marry; and if you remain unmarried, I too will remain unmarried,*
*though I am more eager than you to remain unmarried.*
[[Jami al-Bayan, al-Tabari, 18/167.]]

Some jurists interpreted the verse as obligatory and binding, so they made marriage obligatory upon whoever is able to marry. The rest interpreted it as recommended (mandub) and desirable (mustahabb). This is the sound, well-known view, and it is the view of the majority.

Al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: It is obligatory for a man and a woman to marry when their souls long for it, because Allah, exalted is His praise and sanctified are His names, commanded it, approved of it, and recommended it.

It has reached us that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Marry, so that you may increase in number, for I will boast of you before the nations, even on account of the miscarried fetus."
[[Al-Musannaf, 6/173. Without the phrase "even on account of the miscarried fetus."]] [32]

He (ﷺ) also said: "Whoever loves my natural way (fitrah), let him follow my sunnah, and it is marriage."
[[Musnad Abi Yaʿla, 5/133.]]

He also said: "A man is elevated in rank by the supplication of his child after him."
[[Al-Musannaf, 3/361, by Ibn Abi Shaybah al-Sukuni, transmitted from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab.]] [33]

Al-Shafiʿi said: "And whoever does not feel an inclination toward it, it is more beloved to me that he devote himself to the worship of Allah, mighty and majestic."
[[Kitab al-Umm, 5/155. This is not a hadith.]] [34]

Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the women who sit at home (al-qawaʿid min al-nisaʾ) and mentioned a servant whom He honored, saying, ﴿and a master and a chaste one (ḥaṣūran)﴾. Al-ḥaṣūr is one who does not approach women. Allah did not encourage them to marry, which shows that what is recommended is for the one who needs it.
[[Mukhtasar al-Muzani, 163. He transmitted it in full from Imam al-Shafiʿi.]]

*Chapter mentioning some of the reports that encourage marriage*

Ahmad ibn Abi (chain) related to us: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ishaq al-Jurjani related to us: Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami related to us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi related to us: Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Ansari related to us: Ashʿath related to us, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade tabattul (celibacy).
[[Musnad Ahmad, 5/17.]]
