Rather, it takes its share of both, and when it is so, it is better and brighter for its beauty.

al-Suddī and a group said: That is, it is not in a shaded enclosure (*maqnūh*), which the sun does not reach, nor is it exposed to the sun where the shade does not reach it. So neither the sun nor the shade harms it.

Some said: It is moderate; it is not from the east, where heat would reach it, nor from the west, where cold would harm it. This is the report of Ibn Ẓabyān from Ibn ʿAbbās.

Ibn Zayd said: It is Syrian, because Syria is neither eastern nor western. You say: "It is eastern and western," as you say: "So-and-so is neither traveller nor resident." And this is not white nor black when it has a share of both. The poet said:

*In the hands of men who did not sheathe their swords,*
*And the slain were not many when they were drawn.* [[Lisān al-ʿArab: 4/235.]]

He means they did this.

al-Ḥasan said: This tree is not one of the trees of this world; if it were in the earth it would be eastern or western. It is only a likeness that Allah, glory be to Him, struck for His light. The Qur'an has made clear that it is from the trees of this world, since it is an apposition to "the tree," when it says ﴿an olive﴾. He singled out the olive from among all the trees because its oil is brighter and yellower.

It was also said: because its branch is green from its beginning to its end, and its oil does not need a press to extract it.

It was also said: because it is the first tree to grow in this world, and it was said: after the Flood. It was also said: because its place of growth is the dwelling of the prophets and the saints and the holy land. It was also said: because seventy prophets blessed it, among them Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him). He said: for this reason He said ﴿blessed﴾.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn al-Ḥāfiẓ informed me in my house, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Aḥmad ibn Mālik narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿĪsā ibn al-Sakkīn al-Balladī narrated to us, saying: Hāshim ibn al-Qāsim al-Ḥarrānī narrated to me, saying: Yaʿlā ibn al-Ashdaq narrated to us from his paternal uncle ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ḥarrād, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Allah, bless the oil and the olive; O Allah, bless the oil and the olive." [60] [[Tafsīr al-Qurṭubī: 12/258.]]

And al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad informed me, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣūfī narrated to us, saying: Abū Shuʿayb al-Ḥarrānī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to me, saying: Zuhayr narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿĪsā narrated to us from ʿAṭāʾ from Abū Usayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Eat the oil and anoint yourselves with it, for it is from a blessed tree." [61] [[Sunan al-Tirmidhī: 3/186.]]

And al-Ḥusayn informed me, saying: Aḥmad ibn Jaʿfar ibn Ḥamdān narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Sufayq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abū Ḥamzah narrated to us from Jābir from Abū al-Ṭufayl from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Thābit al-Anṣārī, who said: He called his sons and called for oil, and said: "Anoint your heads." They said: "We will not anoint our heads with oil." He said: Then he took the staff and began striking them, saying: "Do you turn away from the oil of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?"

And ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf ibn Māmūlah narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb al-Dīnawarī informed us, saying: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd [[In the second copy: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad.]] Allāh ibn Sinān narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn ʿUthmān ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahīʿah narrated to us from Yazīd ibn Abī Ḥabīb from Abū al-Khayr from ʿUqbah ibn ʿĀmir that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Adhere to this blessed tree, the olive oil, and treat yourselves with it, for it is a remedy against hemorrhoids." [62]

Then He, glory be to Him, said ﴿its oil would almost glow﴾, from its purity and its radiance. ﴿Even if no fire touched it﴾: it was said: even if fire were to touch it. The scholars differed concerning the meaning of this likeness and the one likened, and concerning what is meant by the niche, the glass, and the lamp.

Some people said: This is a likeness that Allah, glory be to Him, struck for His Prophet Muḥammad (ﷺ). Shimr ibn ʿAṭiyyah said: Ibn ʿAbbās came to Kaʿb al-Aḥbār and said to him: "Tell me about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿The likeness of His light is like a niche﴾, the verse." Kaʿb said: This is a likeness that Allah, glory be to Him, struck for Muḥammad (ﷺ). The niche is his breast, the glass is his heart, the lamp in it is prophethood, kindled ﴿from a blessed tree﴾, which is the tree of prophethood. The light of Muḥammad and his affair almost becomes clear to people even if he did not speak, that he is a prophet, just as that oil almost glows ﴿even if no fire touched it﴾.

Abū Bakr al-Jawzaqī informed us, saying: Abū ʿUthmān al-Baṣrī narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn ibn Manṣūr narrated to us, saying: Abān ibn Rāshid al-Ḥarzī [[In the second copy: al-Kharzī.]] narrated to us, saying: al-Waraʿ ibn Nāfiʿ narrated to us from Sālim from Ibn ʿUmar concerning this verse that he said: The niche is the inside of Muḥammad, the glass is his heart, and the lamp is the light that Allah placed in it. ﴿Neither eastern nor western﴾: neither Jewish nor Christian. ﴿Kindled from a blessed tree﴾: Ibrāhīm. ﴿Light upon light﴾: the light that Allah placed in the heart of Ibrāhīm, just as He placed it in the heart of Muḥammad (ﷺ).

Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurẓī said: The niche is Ibrāhīm, the glass is Ismāʿīl, the lamp is Muḥammad (ﷺ). Allah named him a lamp just as He named him a lantern, when He, Mighty is He, said ﴿and a radiant lantern﴾ [al-Aḥzāb 33:46]. ﴿Kindled from a blessed tree﴾: this is Ibrāhīm. He named him blessed because most of the prophets were from his loins. ﴿Neither eastern nor western﴾: meaning Ibrāhīm was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but was ḥanīf (upright) and a Muslim. He said that because the Jews pray toward the west before the sunset, and the Christians toward the east. ﴿Its oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾: meaning the virtues of Muḥammad would almost appear to people before he was given revelation. ﴿Light upon light﴾: a prophet from the seed of a prophet.

Muqātil related from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, who said: He likened ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib to the niche, ʿAbd Allāh to the glass, and the Prophet (ﷺ) to the lamp, who was in the loins of both. He inherited prophethood from Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him). ﴿Kindled from a blessed tree, an olive, neither eastern nor western﴾: rather, it is Meccan, because Mecca is the centre of the world.

Some eloquent speakers described this tree and said: It is the tree of piety and good pleasure, and the tree of guidance and faith. A tree whose root is prophethood, whose branch is glory, whose boughs are revelation, whose leaves are interpretation, and whose servants are Jibrīl and Mīkāʾīl.

Others said: This is a likeness that Allah, glory be to Him, struck for the believer.

al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas related from Abū al-ʿĀliyah from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, who said: This is the likeness of the believer. The niche is himself, the glass is his breast, and the lamp is what Allah, glory be to Him, placed of faith and Qur'an in his heart. ﴿Kindled from a blessed tree﴾, which is sincerity to Allah alone, without partner. So his likeness is like a tree surrounded by other trees, green and lush, which the sun does not reach in any condition, neither when it rises nor when it sets. Likewise the believer is protected from afflictions reaching him, though he is tested by them, and Allah, exalted is He, makes him firm in them. He is between four qualities: if he is given, he is thankful; if he is tested, he is patient; if he judges, he is just; if he speaks, he is truthful. He is among the people like a living man walking among the graves of the dead.

Then He said ﴿light upon light﴾: he turns in five kinds of light. His speech is light, his deeds are light, his entrance is light, his exit is light, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is light, to Paradise.

Ibn ʿAbbās said: This is the likeness of the light of Allah and His guidance in the heart of the believer, as the pure oil almost glows before fire touches it. If fire touches it, its light increases upon its light. Likewise the heart of the believer almost acts upon guidance before knowledge reaches it; then when knowledge comes to it, guidance increases upon guidance and light upon light. Like the saying of Ibrāhīm (peace be upon him) before knowledge came to him, ﴿This is my Lord﴾ [al-Anʿām 6:76], when he saw the star, without anyone having informed him that it had a Lord. When Allah informed him that He is his Lord, guidance increased upon guidance. Then He said ﴿light upon light﴾, meaning the faith of the believer and his deeds.

al-Ḥasan and Ibn Zayd said: This is a likeness of the Qur'an in the heart of the believer. Just as this lamp is used for light and it remains as it is, not diminishing, so the Qur'an is followed for guidance, taken up and acted upon. So the *miṣbāḥ* is the Qur'an, the *zujājah* is the heart of the believer, the niche is his tongue and mouth, and the blessed tree is the tree of revelation.

﴿Its oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾: it says: the proof of the Qur'an almost becomes clear even if one does not recite it. It was also said: the proofs of Allah upon His creation almost shine for whoever reflects upon them and contemplates them, even if the Qur'an had not been sent down.

﴿Light upon light﴾: meaning that the Qur'an is a light from Allah, which He creates along with what He had established for them of proofs and signs before the Qur'an was sent down, so they increased in light upon light by that.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verses 35–38 (part 2 of 2):

Then He informed that this mentioned light is precious, so the Mighty One said: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ He brought the parables close to the understanding, bringing the thing He intended within reach of minds and facilitating the paths of comprehension for mankind.

Then the Mighty One said: ﴿In houses﴾. The structure of the verse is: "That lamp is in houses." It is also permissible that its meaning be: "It is kindled in houses," and these houses are the mosques, according to most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Fanjawayh al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Ibn Hanash [In the second copy: Habash] al-Muqri narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ashkab narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'a al-Kilabi narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn Shihab, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The mosques are the houses of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on earth, and they shine for the people of the heavens as the stars shine for the people of the earth."

Amr ibn Maymun said: "I met the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they were saying: 'The mosques are the houses of Allah, and it is incumbent upon Allah to honour whoever visits Him in them.'"

Al-Husayn [In the second copy: al-Hasan] ibn Muhammad ibn al-Husayn informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim ibn Shadhan narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Thabit al-Hariri [In the second copy: al-Hadawi] narrated to us, saying: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Salih ibn Hayyan, from Ibn Abi [In the second copy: Ibn Buraydah] Buraydah, concerning His saying, glorified is He: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised...﴾ the verse. He said: "They are only four mosques, none of which was built except by a prophet: the Ka'bah, which Ibrahim and Isma'il built and made the qiblah; Bayt al-Maqdis, which Dawud and Sulayman built; the Mosque of Madinah, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) built; and the Mosque of Quba, which 'was founded upon piety' [9:108], built by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari [In the second copy: Abu Abd Allah al-Dinawari] informed me, saying: Abu Zur'a Ahmad ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamadhani in Kufa narrated to us, saying: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad al-Qabusi narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Nafi' ibn al-Harith, from Anas ibn Malik and from Buraydah, who both said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited this verse: ﴿In houses which Allah has permitted to be raised and in which His name is mentioned﴾ up to His saying ﴿and the eyes﴾. A man stood up and said: 'Which houses are these, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The houses of the prophets.'"

He said: Then Abu Bakr stood up to him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this house one of them?" (pointing to the house of Ali and Fatimah). He said: "Yes, it is among the best of them." [63] [Al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/50.]

Al-Sadiq: "They are the houses of the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Al-Suddi: "They are Madinah."

The most correct of the opinions is that they are the mosques, because the context of the verse indicates that they are houses built for prayer and worship.

If it is asked: What is the reason for the singular in "the niche" and "the lamp," while "houses" is plural, given that one niche can only be in one house?

We say: This is from the shifting address (al-khitab al-mutalawwin), which begins with the singular and ends with the plural, like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾ [65:1] and similar. It was also said: it refers back to each of the houses. It was also said: it is like His saying, glorified is He: ﴿and made the moon therein a light﴾ [71:16], whereas it is only in one of them.

﴿to be raised﴾ means: to be built, according to Mujahid. Its parallel is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House, and Isma'il﴾ [2:127]. Al-Hasan said: it means to be exalted (ta'zim). ﴿and in which His name is mentioned﴾: Ibn Abbas said: "His Book is recited in them." ﴿Glorifying Him therein﴾: Qatadah, Ashhab al-Uqayli, Nasr ibn Asim al-Laythi, Ibn Amir and Asim read it with a fatha on the ba' (yusabbahu), in the passive form (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il), [i.e., ﴿is glorified﴾].

Then He said: ﴿men﴾, meaning: they are men, as one says: "Zayd was struck" and "your food was eaten," and then it is asked: "Who did it?" and it is clarified, and one says: "So-and-so, and so-and-so." The pause on this reading is at His saying ﴿and the mornings and evenings﴾. Others read it with a kasra on the ba' (yusabbihu), making the glorification an action of the men.

Ibn Abbas said: "Every tasbih in the Qur'an is a prayer," indicated by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿in the mornings and evenings﴾, meaning: in the early mornings and the evenings.

The exegetes said: He intends the obligatory prayers. The prayer performed in the early morning (al-ghuduw) is the Fajr prayer, and those performed in the evenings (al-asal) are the Zuhr, 'Asr and the two evening prayers (Maghrib and 'Isha), because the name asil applies to all of them.

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ibn Shanbah narrated to us, saying: Umayr ibn Mirdas narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd narrated to us, from his father, from Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No one goes out in the morning or returns in the evening to the mosque, preferring it over anything else, except that Allah prepares for him a welcome in Paradise every time he goes out or returns, just as if one of you were visited in his honour by someone he loves to visit." [Kanz al-Ummal: 7/569.] [64]

Ibn Fanjawayh also informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: Abu Salamah Yahya ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hasani narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Madani, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever goes out to the mosque and returns in order to learn good or to teach it, is like the one who fights in the way of Allah, returning with booty. And whoever goes out to it for other than that, is like one who looks at a thing that is not his: he sees the worshippers but is not one of them, and he sees the remembrers but is not one of them." [Muwatta' of Imam Malik: 1/716; Musnad Ahmad: 2/350; al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim: 1/91.] [65]

Then He described them, saying: ﴿men﴾. It was said: the reason for specifying men in mentioning these houses is that women are not obliged to attend Friday prayer or congregational prayers in the mosques.

﴿whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: He specified commerce because it is the greatest thing a person is occupied with that distracts him from the prayers and all other acts of obedience. ﴿Nor sale﴾. If it is said: commerce is a term that applies to buying and selling, so what is the purpose of adding mention of sale to commerce? The answer to this is what al-Waqidi said: he meant by commerce the buying (shira'), as His parallel saying, glorified is He: ﴿And when they see a commerce﴾ [62:11], meaning buying.

﴿from the remembrance of Allah and the establishment of prayer﴾, meaning: the establishment of prayer. The ha' (of iqamah) is dropped (from iqamah) in the construct (idafah) because the preposition and what it governs are considered by them like a single letter. They dispensed with the ha' by the genitive noun that follows, since the ha' was a substitute for the waw. The original of the word is aqwama, iqwaman, and they found the damma on the waw heavy, so they made it sukun; two sukun letters came together, so they dropped the waw and transferred its vowel to the qaf, and they replaced the dropped waw with a ha' at the end of the word, as an enlargement of the word, as they did in their saying "'idah" and "wiznah," whose origin is "wi'dah" and "wizanah" [i.e., 'idah from wa'd and wiznah from wazn]. When it is made a construct, the ha' is dropped and the construct serves as its substitute, as in the saying of the poet:

"Indeed the companion has hastened the separation and departed,
and they have broken with you the promise they promised." [Lisan al-Arab: 1/651.]

He meant: "'idat al-amr" (the promise of the matter), so he dropped the ha' when he made it a construct.

﴿and the giving of zakah﴾: the obligatory zakah, according to al-Hasan.

Ibn Abbas said: "Zakah is the sincerity of obedience to Allah, glorified and exalted." Ibn Hayyan said: "They are the People of the Suffah."

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Hamdan informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Sahlawayh narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn Shabib narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Amr ibn Dinar, a client of the family of al-Zubayr, informed me, from Salim, from Ibn Umar, that he was in the market when the prayer was called, so they closed their shops and entered the mosque. Ibn Umar said: "Concerning them was revealed: ﴿men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾."

Abu Abd Allah al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dinawari informed me, saying: Abu Sa'id Ahmad ibn Umar ibn Habish al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Tayfur al-Nasai narrated to us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Darraj, from Abu Hujayr, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed the mosques have pegs (awtad); the angels are their companions, looking after them. If they fall ill, they visit them, and if they are in need, they help them." [Musnad Ahmad: 2/418.] [66]

He also said: "The one who sits in the mosque has three qualities: a brother he gains, or a firm word, or an awaited mercy."

﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be overturned﴾: from its terror, between hope for deliverance and fear of destruction.

﴿and eyes﴾: to which side they will be taken, to the right or to the left? And from where will their books be given to them, from the right side or from the left side? And that is the Day of Resurrection.

﴿That Allah may reward them with the best of what they did﴾: meaning, they were occupied with the remembrance of Allah, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah. ﴿That Allah may reward them with the best﴾: meaning, with the best of what they did. ﴿And increase them from His bounty﴾: what they did not deserve by their deeds. ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.﴾

Then He set forth a parable for the deeds of the disbelievers, so the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage﴾. It is the ray that you see at midday in the deserts when the heat is intense, appearing as if it were water; when a person approaches it, it dissolves and he sees nothing. It is called sarab (mirage) because it flows (yansarib), i.e., runs like water.

﴿In a level plain﴾. It is the plural of qa' (plain), like jar and jiyarah (neighbour and neighbours). The qa' is the wide, flat expanse of land, and it is in such a place that the mirage occurs.

﴿Which the thirsty one thinks is water﴾, i.e., the thirsty one supposes it to be water. ﴿Until, when he comes to it﴾, meaning: he finds that it was not what he had imagined to be water, and he finds nothing as he had supposed. It was also said that the meaning is: he came to the place of the mirage, and the mention of the mirage was sufficient in place of its location. Likewise the disbeliever supposes that his deeds will suffice him or benefit him in some way; but when death comes upon him and he is in need of his deeds, he finds that his deeds neither avail him anything nor benefit him. ﴿And finds Allah with him﴾, i.e., he finds Allah lying in wait for him at that moment. ﴿So He pays him his account in full﴾, the recompense for his deeds. ﴿And Allah is swift at reckoning.﴾ Or [it is] ﴿like darknesses﴾.

This is another parable that Allah the Exalted set forth for the deeds of the disbelievers as well. He says: the likeness of their deeds in their error and corruption, and their misguidance, ignorance and bewilderment therein, is like ﴿darknesses in a deep sea﴾, i.e., the deep sea with abundant water, and this is the greatest darkness; and lujjat al-bahr (the depth of the sea) is its central part. ﴿Covered by waves﴾, i.e., waves rising above it; ﴿above it waves, piled up﴾; ﴿above it clouds﴾. So whoever does not love me and love Abu Bakr, 'Umar and 'A'ishah, for him there is no light!" Then ﴿And whomever Allah does not grant light, for him there is no light﴾ was revealed concerning him. [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/286.]] [67]

[[Sahih al-Bukhari: 6/41.]] [68]

﴿In a level plain﴾. It is the plural of qa' (plain), like jar and jiyarah (neighbour and neighbours). The qa' is the wide, flat expanse of land, and it is in such a place that the mirage occurs.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 24, verse 45–55:

﴿And Allah created every moving creature﴾ — read as khalaqa (with the verb in the form of the verb) by all readers except Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir... [Note: the source text reads: "خالق على الاسم كوفي غير عاصم، الباقون: خَلَقَ ... على الفعل"; rendered below.]

Rendering the passage:

"And Allah created every moving creature" — the reading khāliq (as a noun, "Creator") is that of the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read khalaqa (as a verb) ﴿from water﴾, i.e., from a drop of semen. It has been said: he said "from water" because the origin of creation is water. Then some of the water was turned into wind, from which the angels were created; some of it into fire, from which the jinn were created; and some of it into clay, from which Adam was created.

﴿Of them is one that walks on its belly﴾, like serpents and fish; ﴿and of them is one that walks on two legs﴾, like birds; ﴿and of them is one that walks on four legs﴾, like livestock, wild animals, and predators. He did not mention what walks on more than four because it is like what walks on four in the eye of the observer.

﴿Allah creates what He wills, as He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿We have certainly sent down verses that make things clear, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ ﴿And they say, "We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger and have obeyed," [meaning the hypocrites]; then a faction of them turn away after that. And they are not [truly] believers.﴾ — and he calls to other than the judgment of Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those are not believers.﴾

These verses were revealed concerning Bishr the hypocrite and his Jewish opponent when they disputed over a piece of land. The Jew kept dragging him toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to judge between them, while the hypocrite kept dragging him toward Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, saying: "Muhammad is unjust toward us." This is His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a faction of them turn away. But if the right were theirs, they would come to him in compliance.﴾ — compliant, obedient, submitting to his judgment. ﴿Is there in their hearts disease, or have they doubted?﴾

The meaning is: they are indeed so. He used the wording of reproach to make the blame more emphatic, like Jarir's saying in praise:

"Are you not the best of those who have mounted the mounts, and the most generous of the people in the belly of a hungry [guest]?"

The meaning is: you are indeed so.

﴿Or do they fear that Allah will be unjust to them, and His Messenger?﴾ — i.e., will wrong them. ﴿Rather, those are the wrongdoers﴾ — against themselves, by their turning away from the truth, and placing the litigation in other than its proper place.

﴿The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah﴾ — i.e., to the Book of Allah ﴿and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and remains conscious of Him — those are the attainers [of success].﴾ ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go out.﴾ This is because the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Wherever you go, we will go with you; if you stay, we stay; if you leave, we leave; and if you order us to fight, we fight." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is known."﴾

That is, this is obedience merely in words and tongue without belief; thus it is known from you to be false, that you are lying in it. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid. It was also said: its meaning is that known obedience is better and more excellent than this oath which you break.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — of your obedience and disobedience.

﴿Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be guided."﴾ — i.e., if you turn away from obedience to Allah and His Messenger and from submission to their judgment, then upon him (the Messenger) is what he was charged and commanded with, namely conveying the message, and upon you is what you were charged with, namely obeying and following him. And if you obey him, you will be guided.

I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAqil al-Warraq, along with others, say: We heard Abu ʿAmr Ismaʿil ibn Nujayd al-Sulami say: I heard Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Ismaʿil al-Ḥiri say: Whoever makes the Sunnah his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks wisdom; and whoever makes his desire his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks innovation — based on Allah's saying: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided.﴾

﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ ﴿Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ — the lām was introduced to answer the implied oath, because the promise is a statement; its sense is: and Allah the Exalted said: "Those who believed and did righteous deeds — by Allah, He will surely make them successors upon the earth." That is, He will bequeath to them the lands of the disbelievers, Arabs and non-Arabs, making them their kings, governors, and inhabitants.

﴿As He made successors those before them﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel, when He destroyed the tyrants in Egypt and Syria and gave them their land and their homes. The common readers read kamā istakhlafa with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and lām, based on His saying ﴿Allah has promised﴾ and His saying ﴿He will surely make them successors﴾.

Abu Bakr narrated from ʿĀṣim with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a kasra on the lām, following the grammatical form of what has not named its agent (passive).

﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾ — i.e., will firmly settle for them their religion (millah) which He has approved for them and commanded them with. ﴿And He will surely replace them﴾ — Ibn Kathir, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqub read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and this is the preference of Abu Hatim; others read it with the intensified form (tashdid), and both are dialects. Some of the scholars said: tabdīl is changing a state into another state, while ibdāl is removing a thing and putting something else in its place. ﴿After their fear, security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me.﴾ ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that — those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ — i.e., disbelief in Allah, after this blessing.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿAliyah concerning this verse, he said: The Prophet ﷺ remained ten years in fear, calling to Allah secretly and openly; then he was commanded to emigrate to Medina. There he and his companions remained in fear, rising in arms and sleeping in arms. A man said: "Will there not come upon us a day when we are secure and lay down our weapons?" The Prophet ﷺ said:

"You will not wait long before a man among you sits in a great assembly, reclining, with no weapon on him."

Then Allah revealed this verse, and Allah fulfilled His promise and made him victorious over the Arabian Peninsula. ﴿And Allah created every moving creature﴾ — read as khalaqa (with the verb in the form of the verb) by all readers except Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Ibn Amir... [Note: the source text reads: "خالق على الاسم كوفي غير عاصم، الباقون: خَلَقَ ... على الفعل"; rendered below.]

Rendering the passage:

"And Allah created every moving creature" — the reading khāliq (as a noun, "Creator") is that of the Kufans other than ʿĀṣim; the rest read khalaqa (as a verb) ﴿from water﴾, i.e., from a drop of semen. It has been said: he said "from water" because the origin of creation is water. Then some of the water was turned into wind, from which the angels were created; some of it into fire, from which the jinn were created; and some of it into clay, from which Adam was created.

﴿Of them is one that walks on its belly﴾, like serpents and fish; ﴿and of them is one that walks on two legs﴾, like birds; ﴿and of them is one that walks on four legs﴾, like livestock, wild animals, and predators. He did not mention what walks on more than four because it is like what walks on four in the eye of the observer.

﴿Allah creates what He wills, as He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.﴾ ﴿We have certainly sent down verses that make things clear, and Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.﴾ ﴿And they say, "We have believed in Allah and in the Messenger and have obeyed," [meaning the hypocrites]; then a faction of them turn away after that. And they are not [truly] believers.﴾ — and he calls to other than the judgment of Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those are not believers.﴾

These verses were revealed concerning Bishr the hypocrite and his Jewish opponent when they disputed over a piece of land. The Jew kept dragging him toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to judge between them, while the hypocrite kept dragging him toward Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, saying: "Muhammad is unjust toward us." This is His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a faction of them turn away. But if the right were theirs, they would come to him in compliance.﴾ — compliant, obedient, submitting to his judgment. ﴿Is there in their hearts disease, or have they doubted?﴾

The meaning is: they are indeed so. He used the wording of reproach to make the blame more emphatic, like Jarir's saying in praise:

"Are you not the best of those who have mounted the mounts, and the most generous of the people in the belly of a hungry [guest]?"

The meaning is: you are indeed so.

﴿Or do they fear that Allah will be unjust to them, and His Messenger?﴾ — i.e., will wrong them. ﴿Rather, those are the wrongdoers﴾ — against themselves, by their turning away from the truth, and placing the litigation in other than its proper place.

﴿The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah﴾ — i.e., to the Book of Allah ﴿and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and remains conscious of Him — those are the attainers [of success].﴾ ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go out.﴾ This is because the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Wherever you go, we will go with you; if you stay, we stay; if you leave, we leave; and if you order us to fight, we fight." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is known."﴾

That is, this is obedience merely in words and tongue without belief; thus it is known from you to be false, that you are lying in it. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid. It was also said: its meaning is that known obedience is better and more excellent than this oath which you break.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — of your obedience and disobedience.

﴿Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be guided."﴾ — i.e., if you turn away from obedience to Allah and His Messenger and from submission to their judgment, then upon him (the Messenger) is what he was charged and commanded with, namely conveying the message, and upon you is what you were charged with, namely obeying and following him. And if you obey him, you will be guided.

I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAqil al-Warraq, along with others, say: We heard Abu ʿAmr Ismaʿil ibn Nujayd al-Sulami say: I heard Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Ismaʿil al-Ḥiri say: Whoever makes the Sunnah his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks wisdom; and whoever makes his desire his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks innovation — based on Allah's saying: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided.﴾

﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ ﴿Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ — the lām was introduced to answer the implied oath, because the promise is a statement; its sense is: and Allah the Exalted said: "Those who believed and did righteous deeds — by Allah, He will surely make them successors upon the earth." That is, He will bequeath to them the lands of the disbelievers, Arabs and non-Arabs, making them their kings, governors, and inhabitants.

﴿As He made successors those before them﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel, when He destroyed the tyrants in Egypt and Syria and gave them their land and their homes. The common readers read kamā istakhlafa with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and lām, based on His saying ﴿Allah has promised﴾ and His saying ﴿He will surely make them successors﴾.

Abu Bakr narrated from ʿĀṣim with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a kasra on the lām, following the grammatical form of what has not named its agent (passive).

﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾ — i.e., will firmly settle for them their religion (millah) which He has approved for them and commanded them with. ﴿And He will surely replace them﴾ — Ibn Kathir, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqub read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and this is the preference of Abu Hatim; others read it with the intensified form (tashdid), and both are dialects. Some of the scholars said: tabdīl is changing a state into another state, while ibdāl is removing a thing and putting something else in its place. ﴿After their fear, security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me.﴾ ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that — those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ — i.e., disbelief in Allah, after this blessing.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿAliyah concerning this verse, he said: The Prophet ﷺ remained ten years in fear, calling to Allah secretly and openly; then he was commanded to emigrate to Medina. There he and his companions remained in fear, rising in arms and sleeping in arms. A man said: "Will there not come upon us a day when we are secure and lay down our weapons?" The Prophet ﷺ said:

"You will not wait long before a man among you sits in a great assembly, reclining, with no weapon on him."

Then Allah revealed this verse, and Allah fulfilled His promise and made him victorious over the Arabian Peninsula. They believed, then they became tyrannical and disbelieved after this blessing, and they killed ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan. So Allah changed their state and brought back the fear He had lifted from them.

Muqatil said: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Hudaybiyyah, his companions were saddened, so Allah fed them the palm-dates of Khaybar, promised them that they would enter Mecca the following year in security, and revealed this verse.

I say: In it is clear evidence for the soundness of the caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and the imamate of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them.

Saʿid ibn Jumhan narrated from Safinah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The caliphate after me is thirty [years], then it will be kingship."

Safinah said: "The caliphate of Abu Bakr lasted two years, ʿUmar ten, ʿUthman twelve, and ʿAli six."

Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Tabarani informed us with it, saying: Shafiʿ ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ibn al-Washshaʾ told us, saying: Ibn Ismaʿil al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah told us, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir told us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The caliphate after me among my community is in four: Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, and ʿAli."

[Editor's note: we have not found this in the sources.]

﴿The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah﴾ — i.e., to the Book of Allah ﴿and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey." And those are the successful.﴾ ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and remains conscious of Him — those are the attainers [of success].﴾ ﴿And they swore by Allah their most emphatic oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go out.﴾ This is because the hypocrites used to say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Wherever you go, we will go with you; if you stay, we stay; if you leave, we leave; and if you order us to fight, we fight." So Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "Do not swear; [your] obedience is known."﴾

That is, this is obedience merely in words and tongue without belief; thus it is known from you to be false, that you are lying in it. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid. It was also said: its meaning is that known obedience is better and more excellent than this oath which you break.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ — of your obedience and disobedience.

﴿Say, "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger. But if you turn away, then upon him is only that with which he has been charged, and upon you is that with which you have been charged. And if you obey him, you will be guided."﴾ — i.e., if you turn away from obedience to Allah and His Messenger and from submission to their judgment, then upon him (the Messenger) is what he was charged and commanded with, namely conveying the message, and upon you is what you were charged with, namely obeying and following him. And if you obey him, you will be guided.

I heard Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn ʿAqil al-Warraq, along with others, say: We heard Abu ʿAmr Ismaʿil ibn Nujayd al-Sulami say: I heard Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Ismaʿil al-Ḥiri say: Whoever makes the Sunnah his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks wisdom; and whoever makes his desire his command upon himself, in saying and in deed, speaks innovation — based on Allah's saying: ﴿And if you obey him, you will be guided.﴾

﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance.﴾ ﴿Allah has promised those who have believed among you and done righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth﴾ — the lām was introduced to answer the implied oath, because the promise is a statement; its sense is: and Allah the Exalted said: "Those who believed and did righteous deeds — by Allah, He will surely make them successors upon the earth." That is, He will bequeath to them the lands of the disbelievers, Arabs and non-Arabs, making them their kings, governors, and inhabitants.

﴿As He made successors those before them﴾ — meaning the Children of Israel, when He destroyed the tyrants in Egypt and Syria and gave them their land and their homes. The common readers read kamā istakhlafa with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and lām, based on His saying ﴿Allah has promised﴾ and His saying ﴿He will surely make them successors﴾.

Abu Bakr narrated from ʿĀṣim with a ḍamma on the tāʾ and a kasra on the lām, following the grammatical form of what has not named its agent (passive).

﴿And He will surely establish for them their religion﴾ — i.e., will firmly settle for them their religion (millah) which He has approved for them and commanded them with. ﴿And He will surely replace them﴾ — Ibn Kathir, ʿĀṣim, and Yaʿqub read it with the lightened form (takhfif), and this is the preference of Abu Hatim; others read it with the intensified form (tashdid), and both are dialects. Some of the scholars said: tabdīl is changing a state into another state, while ibdāl is removing a thing and putting something else in its place. ﴿After their fear, security. They worship Me, not associating anything with Me.﴾ ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that — those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ — i.e., disbelief in Allah, after this blessing.

Al-Rabiʿ narrated from Abu al-ʿAliyah concerning this verse, he said: The Prophet ﷺ remained ten years in fear, calling to Allah secretly and openly; then he was commanded to emigrate to Medina. There he and his companions remained in fear, rising in arms and sleeping in arms. A man said: "Will there not come upon us a day when we are secure and lay down our weapons?" The Prophet ﷺ said:

"You will not wait long before a man among you sits in a great assembly, reclining, with no weapon on him."

Then Allah revealed this verse, and Allah fulfilled His promise and made him victorious over the Arabian Peninsula. They believed, then they became tyrannical and disbelieved after this blessing, and they killed ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan. So Allah changed their state and brought back the fear He had lifted from them.

Muqatil said: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from al-Hudaybiyyah, his companions were saddened, so Allah fed them the palm-dates of Khaybar, promised them that they would enter Mecca the following year in security, and revealed this verse.

I say: In it is clear evidence for the soundness of the caliphate of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and the imamate of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, may Allah be pleased with them.

Saʿid ibn Jumhan narrated from Safinah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The caliphate after me is thirty [years], then it will be kingship."

Safinah said: "The caliphate of Abu Bakr lasted two years, ʿUmar ten, ʿUthman twelve, and ʿAli six."

Abu ʿAbd Allah ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Tabarani informed us with it, saying: Shafiʿ ibn Muhammad informed us, saying: Ibn al-Washshaʾ told us, saying: Ibn Ismaʿil al-Baghdadi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah told us, saying: Hushaym ibn Bashir told us, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"The caliphate after me among my community is in four: Abu Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthman, and ʿAli."

[Editor's note: we have not found this in the sources.]

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 24, verses 56–64:**

﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ ﴿Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve...﴾ This is the reading of the majority. Ibn ‘Amir and Hamzah read it with the ya' (yahsabanna), meaning: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that they can escape﴾ themselves, because the verb ḥasiba (to think/suppose) takes two objects. Al-Farra' said: it is permissible for the verb to refer to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. ﴿Let not Muhammad think the disbelievers can escape﴾ in the earth, ﴿and their refuge is the Fire, and what an evil destination.﴾

﴿O you who believe, let your slaves ask your permission...﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a young man from the Ansar called Mudlij ibn ‘Amr to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab at midday to summon him. He entered and found ‘Umar in a state that ‘Umar disliked him seeing. ‘Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish Allah had commanded us and prohibited us regarding the times of seeking permission." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Marthad. She had a grown servant who entered upon her at a time she disliked. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Our servants and attendants enter upon us at times we dislike." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let them ask your permission﴾ — the lam here is the lam of command — ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾, meaning the male and female slaves, ﴿and those among you who have not reached puberty﴾, meaning from among the free, ﴿three times﴾, at three times: ﴿before the prayer of dawn, and when you put off your clothing at midday for rest, and after the prayer of ‘Isha'.﴾

‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Let not the Bedouins overcome you regarding the name of your prayers. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿and after the prayer of ‘Isha'﴾, and the ‘atamah (the late night prayer) is only the ‘atamah of camels." He specified these times because they are the hours of heedlessness, seclusion, removing clothes and undress. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Three times of privacy for you﴾ [72].

The people of Kufa read ﴿thalatha﴾ in the accusative, in response to His saying ﴿three times﴾ (thalatha marrat), while the others read it in the nominative, meaning: "these are three times of privacy (awrah)." ﴿It is not sinful for you nor for them﴾, meaning the slaves, servants and children, ﴿to enter without permission﴾ ﴿after these (times)﴾, meaning after these three times. ﴿They are constant attendants upon you﴾, i.e. they go in and out, come and go, and move about among you in their affairs and business without permission. ﴿Some of you attend upon others.﴾ ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse. One group said: it is abrogated (mansukh) and is not acted upon today.

Abu Muhammad al-Rumi informed us, saying: Abu al-‘Abbas al-Sarraj informed us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from ‘Ikrimah: that a group of people from Iraq said to Ibn ‘Abbas: "What is your view on this verse? We were commanded in it with what we were commanded, and no one acts upon it." (The verse is) the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿O you who believe, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission...﴾ — the verse. Ibn ‘Abbas said: "Allah is Gentle, Forbearing, Compassionate, Merciful, and He loves concealment. The people did not have curtains or partitions for their houses, so a servant, a child or a man would often enter upon his family. So Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded them to seek permission in those times of privacy. Then Allah brought them curtains and goodness, and I have not seen anyone act upon that."

Others said: it is muhkam (not abrogated) and acting upon it is obligatory.

Sufyan narrated from Musa ibn Abi ‘A'ishah, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi about this verse, ﴿let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾. I said: "Is it abrogated?" He said: "No, by Allah, it has not been abrogated." I said: "The people do not act upon it?" He said: "Allah is the One sought for help."

Abu ‘Awanah narrated from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse, who said: "Some people say it was abrogated. By Allah, it was not abrogated, but it is something people are negligent about."

﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾, i.e. from among your free ones, ﴿let them ask permission at all times to enter upon you, as those before them asked permission﴾, meaning the free adults.

﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

﴿And women past child-bearing﴾, meaning those who have ceased to bear children due to old age, so they neither menstruate nor give birth. Its singular is qa'idah.

﴿Who do not hope for marriage﴾, i.e. who no longer aspire to marry, and have despaired of husbands.

﴿There is no sin upon them if they put off their garments﴾ in front of men, meaning their outer garments (jalabib), and the veil that is over the khimar (headscarf) and the cloak worn over the garments. This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "that they may put off some of their garments"; ﴿without displaying adornment﴾, meaning without intending by putting off the outer garment and clothing to show their adornment. Tabarruj (displaying oneself) is for a woman to reveal her attractions which she should conceal.

﴿But to refrain (by keeping them on) is better for them.﴾ ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾

The scholars differed about the interpretation and ruling of this verse. Ibn ‘Abbas said: When Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, the Muslims refrained from eating with the sick, the chronically ill, the blind and the lame. They said: "Food is the best of wealth, and Allah has forbidden us to consume wealth falsely. The blind cannot see the good food, the lame cannot compete for food, and the sick cannot eat their fill." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse. According to this interpretation, ‘ala (upon) means fi (in), i.e. there is no blame on you in eating with the blind, the lame and the sick.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and Muqassam said: The lame and the blind used to keep away from eating with the healthy, because people were disgusted by them and disliked eating with them. The people of Medina would not mix with them in their food, whether blind, lame or sick, out of disgust. So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed as a concession to the sick and the chronically ill to eat from the houses of those named in this verse. That is because some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when they had no food to feed them, would take them to the houses of their fathers and mothers, i.e. some of those named in this verse. The disabled would feel uneasy about eating that food, because it was given to them by someone who was not its owner, and they would say: "They only take us to the houses of others." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse.

‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, who said: I asked al-Zuhri about this verse, and he said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me that when the Muslims went out to fight, they left their disabled behind, and they would hand them the keys to their doors and say: "We have permitted you to eat what is in our houses." But they would feel uneasy about that and say: "We will not enter them while they are absent." So this was revealed as a concession for them.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: It means ﴿there is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ regarding staying behind from jihad in the way of Allah. They said: "And here the statement is complete."

As for His saying ﴿nor upon yourselves﴾ — the verse — it is a new statement, separate from what precedes it.

Ibn ‘Abbas said: A group of people refrained from eating in these houses when He, glorified, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, and they said: "It is not lawful for anyone of us to eat at the house of anyone." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse: ﴿Nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or what you possess the keys to.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: By this is meant a man's agent and steward over his estate and livestock. There is no harm for him to eat from the fruit of his estate and drink from the milk of his livestock.

Al-Dahhak said: It means from the houses of your slaves and those you own.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: from your own houses, that which you chose and possessed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "mallaktum" with the intensive form.

Ibn ‘Abbas said: This verse was revealed concerning al-Harith ibn ‘Amr. He went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as a warrior and left Malik ibn Zayd in charge of his family. When he returned, he found him in a state of hardship, and asked him about his condition. He said: "I was reluctant to eat from your food without your permission." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse.

Al-Hasan and Qatadah used to hold that a man entering the house of his friend and refraining from his food without seeking permission was permitted by this verse.

﴿Or your friend. There is no sin upon you to eat together or separately.﴾

Some said: It was revealed concerning a clan of Kinanah called the Banu Layth ibn ‘Amr. They used to refrain from eating food alone, so a man would sit with food before him from morning until evening, the camels' milk having been drawn and the situation ordered, out of reluctance to eat alone. If evening came and he found no one, he would eat. So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse. This is the view of Qatadah, al-Dahhak, Ibn Jurayj, and a narration of al-Walibi from Ibn ‘Abbas.

‘Ata' al-Khurasani narrated from him, saying: A wealthy man would enter upon a poor relative or friend and invite him to his food, saying: "By Allah, I feel reluctant to eat with you, because I am wealthy and you are poor." So this verse was revealed.

‘Ikrimah and Abu Salih said: It was revealed concerning a people from the Ansar who would not eat when a guest arrived except with their guest. So they were permitted to eat wherever they wished, together or separately.

﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another﴾, i.e. let some of you greet others, like His saying: ﴿and do not kill yourselves﴾ [an-Nisa': 29].

From al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Ibn Habib narrated to us verbatim, in the months of the year 388 (AH), saying: Abu Hatim Muhammad ibn Hibban al-Busti narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tabari narrated to us, saying: al-Fadl ibn Sahl al-A'raj narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Mada'ini narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Zayd ibn Wahb, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Peace (al-salam) is one of the names of Allah, the Exalted, so spread it among yourselves. For when a Muslim passes by a group of people and greets them, and they return his greeting, he has a superiority of a degree over them by mentioning them with peace. If they do not return it, one better and purer than them will return it." [Kanz al-‘Ummal 9/114] [73].

And Abu al-Qasim informed us, saying: Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-‘Abbas al-Baghawi informed us, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd al-Malik ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Wahhab al-Baghawi narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying:

Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Sam‘an informed me that Sa'id al-Maqburi informed him, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When one of you comes upon a gathering, let him greet them. If he wishes to sit, let him sit. When he rises, let him greet them, for the first greeting is not more deserving than the last."

[74].

Some of them said: Its meaning is: When you enter the houses of your own selves, greet your family and dependents. This is the view of Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, Tawus, al-Zuhri, Qatadah, al-Dahhak, ‘Amr ibn Dinar, and a narration of ‘Ata' al-Khurasani from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: If there is no one in the house, let him say: "Peace be upon us from our Lord, and upon the righteous servants of Allah. Peace be upon the people of the house, and the mercy of Allah."

Ibn Habib narrated to us verbatim, saying: Abu Muhammad ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Ka'b al-‘Adl narrated to us by dictation, saying: Abu Nasr al-Yasa' ibn Zayd ibn Sahl al-Rassi narrated to us in Mecca in the year 282 (AH), saying: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: I served the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he never said to me about something I had done: "Why did you do it?" Nor did he say to me about something I had broken: "Why did you break it?" I was standing at his head pouring water on his hands. He raised his head and said: "Shall I teach you three qualities by which you will benefit?" I said: "My father and mother be sacrificed for you, O Messenger of Allah, yes." He said: "Whoever of my nation you meet, greet him, and your life will be prolonged. When you enter, greet them, and the good of your house will increase. And pray the Duha prayer, for it is the prayer of the righteous." [al-Durr al-Manthur 5/60, with variation] [75].

Some of them said: That is, when you enter the mosques, greet those within them.

Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, saying: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Hamdun ibn Khalid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhl al-San'ani narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, from Ibn ‘Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another﴾ — the verse.

He said: When you enter the mosque, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah."

﴿A greeting from Allah, blessed and good.﴾ It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: you greet your selves with it as a greeting. It was also said it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state, meaning: you do it as a greeting from Allah. ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you, that you may understand.﴾

﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾, i.e. with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, such as a war, Friday prayer, congregational prayer, or consultation on a matter that has arisen, ﴿they do not depart until they have asked his permission.﴾ That is: they do not separate from him, nor withdraw from the gathering for the matter they have assembled for, until they seek his permission. ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission, O Muhammad — those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali regarding this verse, who said: It is about Friday. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit on Friday, and a man wished to relieve himself, and a man had an ailment, he would not leave the mosque until he stood opposite the Messenger of Allah ﷺ where he could see him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would know that he had only stood up to seek permission, and he would permit whomever he wished of them.

﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you wish among them﴾ to leave, ﴿and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: It means: beware of the Messenger's supplication against you if you anger him, for his supplication is binding and is not like the supplication of others.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Do not call him as some of you call others: "O Muhammad," but honour him and exalt him, and say: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah," in gentleness and humility.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away﴾, i.e. who depart, from which comes tasallul al-qata (the sand-grouse slips away), ﴿covertly﴾, i.e. concealing themselves behind one another and slipping away lightly, ﴿and so they go off.﴾ Liwadh is a verbal noun of lāwadha bi-fulan (to shelter behind someone), yulawidhu mula-wadhah and liwadh. If it were a verbal noun of lādha, one would say liyadh, like qiyam and siyam.

It was also said: This refers to the digging of the trench, when the hypocrites would leave without the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, hiding themselves.

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial befall them﴾, i.e. a killing, according to Ibn ‘Abbas; ‘Ata': earthquakes and calamities; Ja'far ibn Muhammad: a tyrannical ruler set over them; al-Hasan: a affliction that reveals what is in their hearts of hypocrisy, ﴿or a painful punishment befall them﴾, i.e. a painful, swift punishment in this world. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, as servants, possession, creation, and as evidence of His existence, His oneness, and the perfection of His power and wisdom.

﴿He already knows your condition, and the Day they will be returned to Him, then He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾

Others said: it is muhkam (not abrogated) and acting upon it is obligatory.

Sufyan narrated from Musa ibn Abi ‘A'ishah, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi about this verse, ﴿let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾. I said: "Is it abrogated?" He said: "No, by Allah, it has not been abrogated." I said: "The people do not act upon it?" He said: "Allah is the One sought for help."

Abu ‘Awanah narrated from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse, who said: "Some people say it was abrogated. By Allah, it was not abrogated, but it is something people are negligent about."

﴿And when the children among you reach puberty﴾, i.e. from among your free ones, ﴿let them ask permission at all times to enter upon you, as those before them asked permission﴾, meaning the free adults.

﴿Thus Allah makes clear to you His signs, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

﴿And women past child-bearing﴾, meaning those who have ceased to bear children due to old age, so they neither menstruate nor give birth. Its singular is qa'idah.

﴿Who do not hope for marriage﴾, i.e. who no longer aspire to marry, and have despaired of husbands.

﴿There is no sin upon them if they put off their garments﴾ in front of men, meaning their outer garments (jalabib), and the veil that is over the khimar (headscarf) and the cloak worn over the garments. This interpretation is supported by the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "that they may put off some of their garments"; ﴿without displaying adornment﴾, meaning without intending by putting off the outer garment and clothing to show their adornment. Tabarruj (displaying oneself) is for a woman to reveal her attractions which she should conceal.

﴿But to refrain (by keeping them on) is better for them.﴾ ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾

﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾

The scholars differed about the interpretation and ruling of this verse. Ibn ‘Abbas said: When Allah, glorified and exalted, revealed His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, the Muslims refrained from eating with the sick, the chronically ill, the blind and the lame. They said: "Food is the best of wealth, and Allah has forbidden us to consume wealth falsely. The blind cannot see the good food, the lame cannot compete for food, and the sick cannot eat their fill." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse. According to this interpretation, ‘ala (upon) means fi (in), i.e. there is no blame on you in eating with the blind, the lame and the sick.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and Muqassam said: The lame and the blind used to keep away from eating with the healthy, because people were disgusted by them and disliked eating with them. The people of Medina would not mix with them in their food, whether blind, lame or sick, out of disgust. So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse.

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed as a concession to the sick and the chronically ill to eat from the houses of those named in this verse. That is because some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when they had no food to feed them, would take them to the houses of their fathers and mothers, i.e. some of those named in this verse. The disabled would feel uneasy about eating that food, because it was given to them by someone who was not its owner, and they would say: "They only take us to the houses of others." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse.

‘Abd al-Razzaq narrated from Ma'mar, who said: I asked al-Zuhri about this verse, and he said: ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah informed me that when the Muslims went out to fight, they left their disabled behind, and they would hand them the keys to their doors and say: "We have permitted you to eat what is in our houses." But they would feel uneasy about that and say: "We will not enter them while they are absent." So this was revealed as a concession for them.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd said: It means ﴿there is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick﴾ regarding staying behind from jihad in the way of Allah. They said: "And here the statement is complete."

As for His saying ﴿nor upon yourselves﴾ — the verse — it is a new statement, separate from what precedes it.

Ibn ‘Abbas said: A group of people refrained from eating in these houses when He, glorified, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, and they said: "It is not lawful for anyone of us to eat at the house of anyone." So Allah, glorified, revealed this verse: ﴿Nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses, or the houses of your fathers, or the houses of your mothers, or the houses of your brothers, or the houses of your sisters, or the houses of your paternal uncles, or the houses of your paternal aunts, or the houses of your maternal uncles, or the houses of your maternal aunts, or what you possess the keys to.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: By this is meant a man's agent and steward over his estate and livestock. There is no harm for him to eat from the fruit of his estate and drink from the milk of his livestock.

Al-Dahhak said: It means from the houses of your slaves and those you own.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: from your own houses, that which you chose and possessed. Sa'id ibn Jubayr read "mallaktum" with the intensive form.

﴿Or your friend. There is no sin upon you to eat together or separately.﴾

Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Sam‘an informed me that Sa'id al-Maqburi informed him, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "When one of you comes upon a gathering, let him greet them. [74].

He said: When you enter the mosque, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of Allah."

﴿A greeting from Allah, blessed and good.﴾ It is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: you greet your selves with it as a greeting. It was also said it is in the accusative as a circumstantial state, meaning: you do it as a greeting from Allah. ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you, that you may understand.﴾

﴿The believers are only those who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, and when they are with him on a matter of common concern﴾, i.e. with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, such as a war, Friday prayer, congregational prayer, or consultation on a matter that has arisen, ﴿they do not depart until they have asked his permission.﴾ That is: they do not separate from him, nor withdraw from the gathering for the matter they have assembled for, until they seek his permission. ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission, O Muhammad — those are the ones who believe in Allah and His Messenger.﴾

Ibn Fanjawayh informed me, saying: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn ‘Isa narrated to us, saying: ‘Ali narrated to us, from Abu Hamzah al-Thumali regarding this verse, who said: It is about Friday. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit on Friday, and a man wished to relieve himself, and a man had an ailment, he would not leave the mosque until he stood opposite the Messenger of Allah ﷺ where he could see him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would know that he had only stood up to seek permission, and he would permit whomever he wished of them.

﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs, give permission to whom you wish among them﴾ to leave, ﴿and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.﴾

﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others.﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: It means: beware of the Messenger's supplication against you if you anger him, for his supplication is binding and is not like the supplication of others.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: Do not call him as some of you call others: "O Muhammad," but honour him and exalt him, and say: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah," in gentleness and humility.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away﴾, i.e. who depart, from which comes tasallul al-qata (the sand-grouse slips away), ﴿covertly﴾, i.e. concealing themselves behind one another and slipping away lightly, ﴿and so they go off.﴾ Liwadh is a verbal noun of lāwadha bi-fulan (to shelter behind someone), yulawidhu mula-wadhah and liwadh. If it were a verbal noun of lādha, one would say liyadh, like qiyam and siyam.

It was also said: This refers to the digging of the trench, when the hypocrites would leave without the command of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, hiding themselves.

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware lest a trial befall them﴾, i.e. a killing, according to Ibn ‘Abbas; ‘Ata': earthquakes and calamities; Ja'far ibn Muhammad: a tyrannical ruler set over them; al-Hasan: a affliction that reveals what is in their hearts of hypocrisy, ﴿or a painful punishment befall them﴾, i.e. a painful, swift punishment in this world. ﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾, as servants, possession, creation, and as evidence of His existence, His oneness, and the perfection of His power and wisdom.

﴿He already knows your condition, and the Day they will be returned to Him, then He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is All-Knowing of everything.﴾

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 24, verses 56–64:**

﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ ﴿Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve...﴾ This is the reading of the majority. Ibn ‘Amir and Hamzah read it with the ya' (yahsabanna), meaning: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that they can escape﴾ themselves, because the verb ḥasiba (to think/suppose) takes two objects. Al-Farra' said: it is permissible for the verb to refer to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. ﴿Let not Muhammad think the disbelievers can escape﴾ in the earth, ﴿and their refuge is the Fire, and what an evil destination.﴾

He entered and found ‘Umar in a state that ‘Umar disliked him seeing. ‘Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish Allah had commanded us and prohibited us regarding the times of seeking permission." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Marthad. She had a grown servant who entered upon her at a time she disliked. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Our servants and attendants enter upon us at times we dislike." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let them ask your permission﴾ — the lam here is the lam of command — ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾, meaning the male and female slaves, ﴿and those among you who have not reached puberty﴾, meaning from among the free, ﴿three times﴾, at three times: ﴿before the prayer of dawn, and when you put off your clothing at midday for rest, and after the prayer of ‘Isha'.﴾

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse. One group said: it is abrogated (mansukh) and is not acted upon today.

**Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on Surah 24, verses 56–64:**

﴿And establish the prayer, give the zakat, and obey the Messenger, that you may receive mercy.﴾ ﴿Do not think, O Muhammad, that those who disbelieve...﴾ This is the reading of the majority. Ibn ‘Amir and Hamzah read it with the ya' (yahsabanna), meaning: ﴿Let not those who disbelieve think that they can escape﴾ themselves, because the verb ḥasiba (to think/suppose) takes two objects. Al-Farra' said: it is permissible for the verb to refer to the Prophet ﷺ, i.e. ﴿Let not Muhammad think the disbelievers can escape﴾ in the earth, ﴿and their refuge is the Fire, and what an evil destination.﴾

﴿O you who believe, let your slaves ask your permission...﴾

Ibn ‘Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent a young man from the Ansar called Mudlij ibn ‘Amr to ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab at midday to summon him. He entered and found ‘Umar in a state that ‘Umar disliked him seeing. ‘Umar said: "O Messenger of Allah, I wish Allah had commanded us and prohibited us regarding the times of seeking permission." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse.

Muqatil said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Marthad. She had a grown servant who entered upon her at a time she disliked. She came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "Our servants and attendants enter upon us at times we dislike." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who believe, let them ask your permission﴾ — the lam here is the lam of command — ﴿those whom your right hands possess﴾, meaning the male and female slaves, ﴿and those among you who have not reached puberty﴾, meaning from among the free, ﴿three times﴾, at three times: ﴿before the prayer of dawn, and when you put off your clothing at midday for rest, and after the prayer of ‘Isha'.﴾

‘Abd al-Rahman ibn ‘Awf narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Let not the Bedouins overcome you regarding the name of your prayers. Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿and after the prayer of ‘Isha'﴾, and the ‘atamah (the late night prayer) is only the ‘atamah of camels." He specified these times because they are the hours of heedlessness, seclusion, removing clothes and undress. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Three times of privacy for you﴾ [72].

The people of Kufa read ﴿thalatha﴾ in the accusative, in response to His saying ﴿three times﴾ (thalatha marrat), while the others read it in the nominative, meaning: "these are three times of privacy (awrah)." ﴿It is not sinful for you nor for them﴾, meaning the slaves, servants and children, ﴿to enter without permission﴾ ﴿after these (times)﴾, meaning after these three times. ﴿They are constant attendants upon you﴾, i.e. they go in and out, come and go, and move about among you in their affairs and business without permission. ﴿Some of you attend upon others.﴾ ﴿Thus Allah makes the signs clear to you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.﴾

The scholars differed about the ruling of this verse. One group said: it is abrogated (mansukh) and is not acted upon today.

Abu Muhammad al-Rumi informed us, saying: Abu al-‘Abbas al-Sarraj informed us, saying: Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: ‘Abd al-‘Aziz narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from ‘Ikrimah: that a group of people from Iraq said to Ibn ‘Abbas: "What is your view on this verse?
